	}
	var fields int

	case '1':
		fields = 9
	case '2':

	case 'u':

	default:

	}

	if len(parts) != fields {
		return ""
	}
	return parts[fields-1]
}

// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
// semantics should use Remote instead.
func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
	if commonDir == "" {
		return ""
	}
	if name == "" {
		name = "origin"
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	want := `remote "` + name + `"`
	section := ""
	for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
			section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
			continue
		}
		if section != want {

func compareRepos(a, b RepoRow, sortBy string) int {
	nameCmp := strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.Repo.Display()), strings.ToLower(b.Repo.Display()))
	descInt := func(x, y int) int {
		switch {
		case x > y:
			return -1
		case x < y:
			return 1
		default:
			return 0
		}
	}
	descBool := func(x, y bool) int {
		if x == y {
			return 0
		}
		if x {
			return -1
		}
		return 1
	}
	latest := func() int {
		if a.LastActivity.Equal(b.LastActivity) {
			return 0
		}
		if a.LastActivity.After(b.LastActivity) {
			return -1
		}
		return 1
	}

	switch sortBy {
	case "name":
		return nameCmp
	case "latest":
		if c := latest(); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
	case "git":
		if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := descInt(a.Status.Changed, b.Status.Changed); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
	case "tasks":
		if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
	default: // activity
		if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := descBool(a.Live, b.Live); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		if c := latest(); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
	}
	return nameCmp
}

type repoColumnSpec struct {
	name, header string
	width, min   int

func (m Model) repoColumns() []repoColumnSpec {
	names := m.actions.RepoColumns
	if len(names) == 0 {
		names = []string{"repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"}
	}
	defaults := map[string]repoColumnSpec{
		"repo":      {"repo", "REPO", 28, 12},
		"branch":    {"branch", "BRANCH", 22, 10},
		"git":       {"git", "GIT", 16, 8},
		"live":      {"live", "LIVE", 15, 7},
		"latest":    {"latest", "LATEST", 8, 6},
		"worktrees": {"worktrees", "WT", 3, 2},
		"tasks":     {"tasks", "TASKS", 18, 8},
		"category":  {"category", "CATEGORY", 14, 8},
		"path":      {"path", "PATH", 30, 12},
	}
	columns := make([]repoColumnSpec, 0, len(names))
	for _, name := range names {
		if c, ok := defaults[name]; ok {
			columns = append(columns, c)
		}
	}
	// Shrink flexible columns to fit. Configuration controls what exists and in
	// what order; width adapts to the current pane.
	total := 2 + 2*(len(columns)-1)
	for _, c := range columns {
		total += c.width
	}
	for total > m.width {
		changed := false
		for _, preferred := range []string{"path", "tasks", "repo", "branch", "live", "git"} {
			for i := range columns {
				if columns[i].name == preferred && columns[i].width > columns[i].min {
					columns[i].width--
					total--
					changed = true
					if total <= m.width {
						return columns
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if !changed {
			break
		}
	}
	return columns
}

func repoColumnValue(r RepoRow, name string) string {

	return ""

func latestAge(at time.Time) string {
	if at.IsZero() {
		return "—"
	}
	d := time.Since(at)
	switch {
	case d < time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
	case d < 24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
	case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
	case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
	}
}

func fitCell(s string, width int) string {

cat >> internal/stats/store.go <<'EOF'

// ClearQuery selects durable activity rows to delete. Repo is an exact name —
// deletion must not use the fuzzy LIKE semantics a report does.
type ClearQuery struct {
	Repo    string
	Sources []Source
}

// Clear deletes matching activity and returns the number of rows removed.
// With an empty query it clears all activity and collector checkpoints.
func (s *Store) Clear(q ClearQuery) (int64, error) {
	clause := ""
	var args []any
	if q.Repo != "" {
		clause = " WHERE repo = ?"
		args = append(args, q.Repo)
	}
	if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
		if clause == "" {
			clause = " WHERE "
		} else {
			clause += " AND "
		}
		clause += "source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
		for _, source := range q.Sources {
			args = append(args, string(source))
		}
	}
	result, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM activity"+clause, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	if q.Repo == "" && len(q.Sources) == 0 {
		if _, err := s.db.Exec("DELETE FROM collector"); err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
	}
	return result.RowsAffected()
}
EOF

func newStatsPathCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "path",
		Short: "Print the durable activity database path",
		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
			return nil
		},
	}
}

func newStatsClearCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	var (
		all     bool
		repo    string
		sources []string
		yes     bool
	)
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "clear",
		Short: "Delete selected activity data (this is durable data, not cache)",
		Long: `Delete activity rows from $XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db.

Stats are durable observations, not disposable cache: they include session
samples and WakaTime imports that cannot necessarily be reconstructed from Git.
Therefore a scope is required and the operation confirms unless --yes is
explicit.

    dev stats clear --repo api
    dev stats clear --source git
    dev stats clear --repo api --source git
    dev stats clear --all

Use "dev cache clear" for regenerable forge/gitignore caches instead.`,
		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			if all && (repo != "" || len(sources) > 0) {
				return fmt.Errorf("--all cannot be combined with --repo or --source")
			}
			if !all && repo == "" && len(sources) == 0 {
				return fmt.Errorf("choose --repo, --source, or --all; stats data is not treated as disposable cache")
			}
			var parsed []stats.Source
			for _, source := range sources {
				s := stats.Source(strings.ToLower(source))
				switch s {
				case stats.SourceSession, stats.SourceGit, stats.SourceWakaTime:
					parsed = append(parsed, s)
				default:
					return fmt.Errorf("unknown source %q: want session, git or wakatime", source)
				}
			}
			description := "all activity data"
			if !all {
				var parts []string
				if repo != "" {
					parts = append(parts, "repo="+repo)
				}
				if len(parsed) > 0 {
					parts = append(parts, "source="+strings.Join(sources, ","))
				}
				description = strings.Join(parts, " ")
			}
			if !yes {
				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
				if !confirm(app, in, "delete "+description+" from stats.db") {
					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "not changed")
					return nil
				}
			}
			store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir()))
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			defer store.Close()
			q := stats.ClearQuery{}
			if !all {
				q.Repo, q.Sources = repo, parsed
			}
			n, err := store.Clear(q)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "deleted %d activity row(s) from %s\n", n,
				config.Contract(stats.Path(app.Cfg.StateDir())))
			return nil
		},
	}
	f := cmd.Flags()
	f.BoolVar(&all, "all", false, "delete all activity and collector checkpoints")
	f.StringVarP(&repo, "repo", "r", "", "delete this exact repository name")
	f.StringSliceVar(&sources, "source", nil, "delete these sources: session, git, wakatime")
	f.BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "do not prompt")
	return cmd
}

package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func newCacheCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "cache",
		Short: "Inspect and clear regenerable dev caches",
		Long: `Manage files under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev.

These are disposable accelerators: the remote forge inventory and fetched
GitHub gitignore templates. Activity statistics are deliberately not here —
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db contains observations that may not be
reconstructible; use "dev stats path/clear" for it.`,
	}
	cmd.AddCommand(newCacheListCmd(app), newCachePathCmd(app), newCacheClearCmd(app))
	return cmd
}

func cacheRoot() string { return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev") }

func newCachePathCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "path",
		Short: "Print dev's XDG cache directory",
		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, cacheRoot())
			return nil
		},
	}
}

func newCacheListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "list",
		Short: "List cache paths, sizes, and ages",
		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			t := NewTable("CACHE", "SIZE", "AGE", "PATH")
			for _, item := range cacheItems() {
				size, modified, exists := cacheInfo(item.path)
				if !exists {
					t.Add(item.name, "—", "—", config.Contract(item.path)+" (absent)")
					continue
				}
				t.Add(item.name, humanBytes(size), humanAge(time.Since(modified)), config.Contract(item.path))
			}
			t.Render(app.Out)
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nStats data: %s (not cache; use `dev stats clear`)\n",
				config.Contract(filepath.Join(app.Cfg.StateDir(), "stats.db")))
			return nil
		},
	}
}

type cacheItem struct{ name, path string }

func cacheItems() []cacheItem {
	return []cacheItem{
		{"remote", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "remotes.json")},
		{"gitignore", filepath.Join(cacheRoot(), "gitignore")},
	}
}

func newCacheClearCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:       "clear <remote|gitignore|all>",
		Short:     "Remove a regenerable cache",
		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		ValidArgs: []string{"remote", "gitignore", "all"},
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			var targets []cacheItem
			switch args[0] {
			case "remote", "remotes":
				targets = cacheItems()[:1]
			case "gitignore":
				targets = cacheItems()[1:]
			case "all":
				targets = cacheItems()
			default:
				return fmt.Errorf("unknown cache %q: want remote, gitignore or all", args[0])
			}
			removed := 0
			for _, item := range targets {
				if _, err := os.Lstat(item.path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
					continue
				}
				if err := os.RemoveAll(item.path); err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("clear %s: %w", item.name, err)
				}
				removed++
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "cleared %d cache(s) under %s\n", removed, config.Contract(cacheRoot()))
			return nil
		},
	}
}

func cacheInfo(path string) (size int64, modified time.Time, exists bool) {
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, time.Time{}, false
	}
	exists, modified = true, info.ModTime()
	if !info.IsDir() {
		return info.Size(), modified, true
	}
	_ = filepath.WalkDir(path, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		if i, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
			size += i.Size()
			if i.ModTime().After(modified) {
				modified = i.ModTime()
			}
		}
		return nil
	})
	return size, modified, true
}

func humanBytes(n int64) string {
	const unit = 1024
	switch {
	case n < unit:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", n)
	case n < unit*unit:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fK", float64(n)/unit)
	case n < unit*unit*unit:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fM", float64(n)/(unit*unit))
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fG", float64(n)/(unit*unit*unit))
	}
}
EOF

# State, data, and cache locations

`dev` follows XDG and separates intent, durable observations, and regenerable
cache so cleanup cannot erase the wrong thing.

| Path | Contains | Reconstructible? |
|---|---|---|
| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml` | user policy | no |
| `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/*.toml` | state/owner/next for tasks | partially |
| `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` | Git backfill, session samples, WakaTime imports | not always |
| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/remotes.json` | short-lived gh/glab inventory | yes |
| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/gitignore/` | fetched GitHub templates | yes |

Inspect paths:

```bash
dev config path
dev stats path
dev cache path
dev cache list
```

Clear only regenerable cache:

```bash
dev cache clear remote
dev cache clear gitignore
dev cache clear all
```

Clear durable stats only with an explicit scope and confirmation:

```bash
dev stats clear --repo api
dev stats clear --source git
dev stats clear --repo api --source wakatime
dev stats clear --all
```

`stats.db` is not called a cache because session samples and WakaTime imports
may not be reconstructible. Git-derived rows can be regenerated with
`dev stats backfill [--repo api]`.
EOF
echo added

No activity recorded for this repository.

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>

Fix disappearing top bar with dynamic height budgeting

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
p='internal/tui/view.go'
s=open(p).read()
old='''// chrome is the number of lines the header, detail pane and footer take, so
// the list knows how much room it has left.
const chrome = 12

func (m Model) listHeight() int {
	h := m.height - chrome
	if h < 3 {
		return 3
	}
	return h
}'''
new='''// listHeight budgets rows from what the current detail and footer actually
// render. REPOS has more detail and more key hints than TASKS; the old fixed
// chrome allowance let the complete view exceed terminal height, so Bubble
// Tea scrolled the first lines and the top tab bar appeared to disappear.
func (m Model) listHeight() int {
	// Header + its blank line, table header, blank before detail, blank before
	// footer. Detail and footer can each wrap/change by view and terminal width.
	fixed := 2 + 1 + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
	h := m.height - fixed
	if h < 3 {
		return 3
	}
	// A long list adds the "… x–y of n" scroll note.
	if m.count() > h && h > 3 {
		h--
	}
	return h
}

func lineCount(s string) int {
	s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\\n")
	if s == "" {
		return 0
	}
	return strings.Count(s, "\\n") + 1
}'''
if old not in s: raise SystemExit('chrome block missing')
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

## Stats SQLite

`stats.db` 會在第一次使用以下功能時自動建立並初始化 schema：

```bash
dev stats
dev stats backfill
dev stats sample
TUI → H
```

可查看實際位置：

```bash
dev stats path
```

它不被定義成 cache，因為 session samples 與 WakaTime import 不一定能重新產生。

清除必須指定 scope：

```bash
dev stats clear --repo dev-cli
dev stats clear --source git
dev stats clear --repo dev-cli --source wakatime
dev stats clear --all
```

真正 cache 則是：

```bash
dev cache list
dev cache path
dev cache clear remote
dev cache clear gitignore
dev cache clear all
```

`dev cache clear all` 不會碰 `stats.db`。

## Quick thoughts / repo notes

已放入 `TODO.md`，推薦的設計不是把 notes 直接混入 `stats.db`：

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<repo-key>/<timestamp>.md
或
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<repo-key>.jsonl
```

作為 durable source of truth，然後 SQLite FTS 作為可重建搜尋 index：

```text
Markdown / JSONL       可讀、可 export、可 git-sync
        ↓
SQLite FTS index       快速全文搜尋、tags、pinned notes
```

預計 command surface：

```bash
dev note add
dev note list
dev note edit
dev note search
```

這可避免把唯一一份 human intent 放在難以 git merge 的 SQLite binary 裡。

Repo identity 預計優先使用：

```text
forge + owner/repo
```

Local-only repo 再 fallback 到 Git common-dir fingerprint。

```text
1	# dev-cli — a thin glue layer over Git, worktrees, forges, and agent runtimes
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	This machine currently has **31 open Herdr workspaces**, 39 repos under
6	`~/Documents/Program`, and 19 experiments in `~/src/tries`. The Herdr sidebar is
7	being used as a *memory of what I'm working on*, so nothing ever gets closed —
8	Herdr is forced to be both "live runtime" and "WIP inventory" at once. Meanwhile
9	worktrees are confusing: Claude Code has a native `--worktree`, Herdr has
10	`herdr worktree create`, Worktrunk exists, and it's unclear who owns what or how
11	a new worktree gets a working environment (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, `.env`).
12	
13	`dev` fixes this by being **glue, not a second Git database**:
14	
15	```
16	Git remote      durable code state       (source of truth)
17	git worktree    disposable local checkout
18	Herdr / tmux    per-host live runtime
19	dev             human intent + inventory + navigation + one worktree policy
20	```
21	
22	Everything derivable from Git or the runtime is **derived live**. `dev` persists
23	only what Git cannot answer: `state`, `next`, `owner`, `note`.
24	
25	Outcome: closing a Herdr workspace stops feeling like abandoning a task, so the
26	sidebar can shrink back to an actual working set.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 1. Doctrine the tool encodes
31	
32	### 1.1 Task state machine
33	
34	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
35	|---|---|---|---|
36	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | Herdr space open | working on it now |
37	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | space **closed** | back within days |
38	| ❄️ `cold` | committed + pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused; reconstructible anywhere |
39	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | branch + worktree + entry deleted |
40	
41	`dev park` = warm/cold transition. **Closing a space ≠ abandoning a task.**
42	
43	### 1.2 Isolation boundary
44	
45	> **Worktree per change stream, pane per agent.** Not one worktree per agent.
46	
47	### 1.3 Worktree ownership — the confusion-killer
48	
49	This is the question that has been unclear; `dev` takes one explicit stance and
50	the skill teaches agents to respect it.
51	
52	| Worktree kind | Owner | Location | Lifetime |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| Feature / bugfix / experiment / cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `worktree.path_template` (default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>`) | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
55	| Claude Code subagent `isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree` | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
56	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used directly** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` so path policy lives in exactly one place | — | — |
57	| Worktrunk | **not adopted** — `dev wt` fills that role | — | — |
58	
59	Rule of thumb: **might I come back tomorrow → `dev`; dies with this agent turn →
60	Claude Code native.** Never nest a `dev` worktree inside another `dev` worktree.
61	
62	Herdr visibility is preserved: after `git worktree add`, `dev` calls
63	`herdr worktree open --path <path> --label <task>`, which registers the checkout
64	as a Herdr workspace grouped under the parent repo's space with its own
65	branch/ahead/behind row. `dev` additionally pushes
66	`herdr workspace report-metadata --source dev --token stage=HOT --token next="…"`
67	so the sidebar shows the task state (config already documents `$name` tokens
68	require a matching `rows` entry in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`).
69	
70	### 1.4 Worktree provisioning
71	
72	A fresh checkout has no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`. `dev wt create`
73	runs a provisioning step (skippable with `--no-provision`):
74	
75	1. **Copy gitignored files** listed in `worktree.include` — same semantics as
76	   `.worktreeinclude` in the existing `git-workflow` skill (copies only files
77	   that are *both* matched and gitignored).
78	2. **Optional symlinks** for heavy dirs (`worktree.link`, default empty —
79	   opt-in, since sharing `node_modules` across checkouts can break native deps).
80	3. **Post-create commands**: `worktree.post_create = "auto"` detects
81	   `uv.lock`→`uv sync`, `poetry.lock`→`poetry install`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`→`pnpm i
82	   --frozen-lockfile`, `package-lock.json`→`npm ci`, `yarn.lock`→`yarn install
83	   --immutable`, `go.mod`→`go mod download`, `Cargo.toml`→`cargo fetch`;
84	   otherwise an explicit list. Per-repo override in `<repo>/.dev.toml`.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 2. Architecture
89	
90	Go 1.26 (installed), pure-Go deps only (no cgo): `spf13/cobra`,
91	`charmbracelet/bubbletea` + `bubbles` + `lipgloss` + `glamour`,
92	`BurntSushi/toml`, `modernc.org/sqlite`.
93	
94	```
95	cmd/dev/main.go
96	internal/config/     TOML load/merge, path templates, XDG resolution
97	internal/gitx/       porcelain wrappers: worktree list, status, ahead/behind,
98	                     branch classification, wip-commit
99	internal/repo/       scan-root discovery + cache
100	internal/wt/         create/open/remove + provisioning (§1.4)
101	internal/task/       one-TOML-per-task registry
102	internal/runtime/    Runtime interface + herdr / tmux / none adapters
103	internal/forge/      gh + glab adapters (both optional)
104	internal/stats/      sampler, SQLite store, heatmap renderer, WakaTime importer
105	internal/tui/        bubbletea dashboard
106	internal/help/       go:embed'd git-workflow quick pages
107	internal/skill/      go:embed'd SKILL.md + install/sync
108	skill/               SKILL.md + references/ (source of truth, embedded at build)
109	docs/                mkdocs-able reference
110	```
111	
112	### Config — `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`
113	
114	Every path is configurable (per the requirement that `~/Worktrees` may need to
115	live on `/mnt`, or be lowercase):
116	
117	```toml
118	[paths]
119	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries", "~/.local/share/chezmoi"]
120	tries_root    = "~/src/tries"
```
</details></tool-use>

136	
137	// Entry is one logical asset. ID is the stable filename stem and is deliberately
138	// not duplicated inside the TOML document.
139	type Entry struct {
140		SchemaVersion int      `toml:"schema_version" json:"schema_version"`
141		ID            string   `toml:"-" json:"id"`
142		Kind          Kind     `toml:"kind" json:"kind"`
143		Name          string   `toml:"name" json:"name"`
144		Note          string   `toml:"note" json:"note"`
145		Tags          []string `toml:"tags" json:"tags"`
146	
147		// RemoteIdentity is a relocation hint, never sufficient on its own when
148		// several records or live clones could be the observation's owner.
149		RemoteIdentity string `toml:"remote_identity" json:"remote_identity"`
150	
151		Experiment      *Experiment         `toml:"experiment,omitempty" json:"experiment,omitempty"`
152		Locations       map[string]Location `toml:"locations" json:"locations"`
153		RecoveryReceipt *RecoveryReceipt    `toml:"recovery_receipt,omitempty" json:"recovery_receipt,omitempty"`
154		MoveIntent      *MoveIntent         `toml:"move_intent,omitempty" json:"move_intent,omitempty"`
155	
156		Created    time.Time `toml:"created" json:"created"`
157		Discovered time.Time `toml:"discovered" json:"discovered"`
158		LastOpened time.Time `toml:"last_opened" json:"last_opened"`
159		Updated    time.Time `toml:"updated" json:"updated"`
160	}
161	
162	var validID = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`)
163	
164	// ValidateID checks that id can be used as exactly one visible filename stem.
165	func ValidateID(id string) error {
166		if !validID.MatchString(id) || filepath.Base(id) != id || id == "." || id == ".." {
167			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrInvalidID)
168		}
169		return nil
170	}
171	
172	// NormalizeTags trims, lowercases, deduplicates and sorts tags. Sorting makes
173	// persisted output deterministic regardless of the order in which callers add
174	// labels.
175	func NormalizeTags(tags []string) []string {
176		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(tags))
177		for _, tag := range tags {
178			tag = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))
179			if tag != "" {
180				seen[tag] = struct{}{}
181			}
182		}
183		out := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
184		for tag := range seen {
185			out = append(out, tag)
186		}
187		sort.Strings(out)
188		return out
189	}
190	
191	// Normalize applies the lossless normalizations stores use before validation.
192	func (e *Entry) Normalize() {
193		if e == nil {
194			return
195		}
196		e.Name = strings.TrimSpace(e.Name)
197		e.Tags = NormalizeTags(e.Tags)
198		if e.Experiment != nil && e.Experiment.Phase == "" {
199			e.Experiment.Phase = PhaseActive
200		}
201	}
202	
203	// Title is the human label, falling back to the stable ID for damaged display
204	// data. Persisted entries still require a name during validation.
205	func (e Entry) Title() string {
206		if e.Name != "" {
207			return e.Name
208		}
209		return e.ID
210	}
211	
212	// HasTag reports membership after applying the same normalization as storage.
213	func (e Entry) HasTag(tag string) bool {
214		tag = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))
215		return tag != "" && slices.Contains(e.Tags, tag)
216	}
217	
218	// LocationFor returns host's location without exposing the map for mutation.
219	func (e Entry) LocationFor(host string) (Location, bool) {
220		location, ok := e.Locations[host]
221		return location, ok
222	}
223	
224	// SetLocation validates and records one host location.
225	func (e *Entry) SetLocation(host string, location Location) error {
226		if e == nil {
227			return errors.New("set location on nil catalog entry")
228		}
229		if err := validateLocation(host, location); err != nil {
230			return err
231		}
232		if e.Locations == nil {
233			e.Locations = make(map[string]Location)
234		}
235		e.Locations[host] = location
236		return nil
237	}
238	
239	// Clone returns a deep copy suitable for mutation before an atomic update.
240	func (e Entry) Clone() *Entry {
241		clone := e
242		clone.Tags = append([]string(nil), e.Tags...)
243		if e.Experiment != nil {
244			value := *e.Experiment
245			clone.Experiment = &value
246		}
247		if e.RecoveryReceipt != nil {
248			value := *e.RecoveryReceipt
249			clone.RecoveryReceipt = &value
250		}
251		if e.MoveIntent != nil {
252			value := *e.MoveIntent
253			clone.MoveIntent = &value
254		}
255		if e.Locations != nil {
256			clone.Locations = make(map[string]Location, len(e.Locations))
257			for host, location := range e.Locations {
258				clone.Locations[host] = location
259			}
260		}
261		return &clone
262	}
263	
264	// Validate rejects records that later lifecycle operations could not interpret
265	// safely. Store.Create fills identity and timestamps before calling it.
266	func (e Entry) Validate() error {
267		if e.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
268			return &UnsupportedSchemaError{ID: e.ID, Version: e.SchemaVersion}
269		}
270		if err := ValidateID(e.ID); err != nil {
271			return err
272		}
273		switch e.Kind {
274		case KindTry, KindRepository:
275		default:
276			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: unknown kind %q", e.ID, e.Kind)
277		}
278		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Name) == "" {
279			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: name is required", e.ID)
280		}
281		if !slices.Equal(e.Tags, NormalizeTags(e.Tags)) {
282			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: tags must be normalized lowercase values", e.ID)
283		}
284		if e.Experiment != nil {
285			switch e.Experiment.Phase {
286			case PhaseActive, PhaseDeprecated, PhaseGraduated:
287			default:
288				return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: unknown experiment phase %q", e.ID, e.Experiment.Phase)
289			}
290		}
291		for host, location := range e.Locations {
292			if err := validateLocation(host, location); err != nil {
293				return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: %w", e.ID, err)
294			}
295		}
296		if e.MoveIntent != nil {
297			if e.MoveIntent.SourcePath == "" || e.MoveIntent.DestinationPath == "" {
298				return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: move intent requires source and destination paths", e.ID)
299			}
300			if e.MoveIntent.SourcePath == e.MoveIntent.DestinationPath {
301				return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: move intent source and destination are identical", e.ID)
302			}
303		}
304		if e.Created.IsZero() || e.Discovered.IsZero() || e.Updated.IsZero() {
305			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: created, discovered and updated timestamps are required", e.ID)
306		}
307		return nil
308	}
309	
310	func validateLocation(host string, location Location) error {
311		if strings.TrimSpace(host) == "" {
312			return errors.New("location host is required")
313		}
314		for field, value := range map[string]string{
315			"current_path":   location.CurrentPath,
316			"restore_path":   location.RestorePath,
317			"real_path":      location.RealPath,
318			"git_common_dir": location.GitCommonDir,
319		} {
320			if strings.ContainsRune(value, '\x00') {
321				return fmt.Errorf("location %s %s contains NUL", host, field)
322			}
323		}
324		switch location.State {
325		case LocationPresent:
326			if location.CurrentPath == "" {
327				return fmt.Errorf("location %s: present state requires current_path", host)
328			}
329		case LocationArchived:
330			if location.CurrentPath == "" || location.RestorePath == "" {
331				return fmt.Errorf("location %s: archived state requires current_path and restore_path", host)
332			}
333		case LocationEvicted:
334			if location.RestorePath == "" {
335				return fmt.Errorf("location %s: evicted state requires restore_path", host)
336			}
337		default:
338			return fmt.Errorf("location %s: unknown state %q", host, location.State)
339		}
340		return nil
341	}

19	var (

21		ErrNotFound = errors.New("catalog asset not found")
22		// ErrAlreadyExists is returned when ID generation repeatedly collides.
23		ErrAlreadyExists = errors.New("catalog asset already exists")
24	)
25	
26	// Diagnostic describes one record skipped by a directory listing. The listing
27	// still returns every valid record; callers decide whether and where to render
28	// these notices.
29	type Diagnostic struct {
30		Path string
31		Err  error
32	}
33	
34	func (d Diagnostic) Error() string {
35		return fmt.Sprintf("skipping %s: %v", filepath.Base(d.Path), d.Err)
36	}
37	
38	func (d Diagnostic) Unwrap() error { return d.Err }
39	
40	// IDGenerator supplies stable random filename stems. It is injectable so tests
41	// can assert exact filenames without weakening production randomness.
42	type IDGenerator func() string
43	
44	// DiagnosticSink receives non-fatal per-record listing failures.
45	type DiagnosticSink func(Diagnostic)
46	
47	// StoreOption configures a Store.
48	type StoreOption func(*Store)
49	
50	// WithIDGenerator replaces UUID generation.
51	func WithIDGenerator(generator IDGenerator) StoreOption {
52		return func(store *Store) { store.generateID = generator }
53	}
54	
55	// WithClock replaces timestamp generation.
56	func WithClock(clock func() time.Time) StoreOption {
57		return func(store *Store) { store.clock = clock }
58	}
59	
60	// WithDiagnosticSink directs skipped-record notices to sink.
61	func WithDiagnosticSink(sink DiagnosticSink) StoreOption {
62		return func(store *Store) { store.diagnostics = sink }
63	}
64	
65	// WithDiagnosticWriter writes one line per skipped record to writer. It never
66	// defaults to a process-global stream.
67	func WithDiagnosticWriter(writer io.Writer) StoreOption {
68		if writer == nil {
69			return func(*Store) {}
70		}
71		return WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic Diagnostic) {
72			fmt.Fprintln(writer, diagnostic.Error())
73		})
74	}
75	
76	// Store is a directory of one TOML file per asset.
77	type Store struct {
78		Dir string
79	
80		mu          sync.Mutex
81		generateID  IDGenerator
82		clock       func() time.Time
83		diagnostics DiagnosticSink
84	}
85	
86	// NewStore returns a catalog rooted at dir.
87	func NewStore(dir string, options ...StoreOption) *Store {
88		store := &Store{
89			Dir:        dir,
90			generateID: uuid.NewString,
91			clock:      time.Now,
92		}
93		for _, option := range options {
94			if option != nil {
95				option(store)
96			}
97		}
98		return store
99	}
100	
101	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
102	
103	// Create assigns a random stable ID and atomically persists entry. The caller's
104	// value is updated only after the rename succeeds.
105	func (s *Store) Create(entry *Entry) error {
106		if entry == nil {
107			return errors.New("create nil catalog entry")
108		}
109		if entry.ID != "" {
110			return fmt.Errorf("create catalog asset: ID is assigned by the store")
111		}
112	
113		s.mu.Lock()
114		defer s.mu.Unlock()
115	
116		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
117			return fmt.Errorf("create catalog directory: %w", err)
118		}
119		for range 32 {
120			candidate := entry.Clone()
121			candidate.ID = s.nextID()
122			if err := ValidateID(candidate.ID); err != nil {
123				return fmt.Errorf("generated catalog ID: %w", err)
124			}
125			if _, err := os.Lstat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
126				continue
127			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
128				return fmt.Errorf("check catalog ID %s: %w", candidate.ID, err)
129			}
130	
131			now := s.now()
132			candidate.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
133			if candidate.Created.IsZero() {
134				candidate.Created = now
135			}
136			if candidate.Discovered.IsZero() {
137				candidate.Discovered = now
138			}
139			candidate.Updated = now
140			prepareNested(candidate, now)
141			candidate.Normalize()
142			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
143				return err
144			}
145			if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
146				return err
147			}
148			*entry = *candidate
149			return nil
150		}
151		return fmt.Errorf("generate unique catalog ID: %w", ErrAlreadyExists)
152	}
153	
154	// Get loads one asset by exact ID.
155	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Entry, error) {
156		if err := ValidateID(id); err != nil {
157			return nil, err
158		}
159		return s.get(id)
160	}
161	
162	func (s *Store) get(id string) (*Entry, error) {
163		var entry Entry
164		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &entry); err != nil {
165			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
166				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
167			}
168			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
169		}
170		entry.ID = id
171		if entry.SchemaVersion != 0 && entry.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
172			return nil, &UnsupportedSchemaError{ID: id, Version: entry.SchemaVersion}
173		}
174		// Version zero is the only implicit form: it means the schema marker was
175		// absent, not that an unknown future layout should be guessed.
176		if entry.SchemaVersion == 0 {
177			entry.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
178		}
179		entry.Normalize()
180		if err := entry.Validate(); err != nil {
181			return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
182		}
183		return &entry, nil
184	}
185	
186	// List loads every valid record in deterministic ID order. Per-record failures
187	// are skipped and sent to the configured diagnostic sink; directory-level
188	// failures are returned.
189	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Entry, error) {
190		entries, diagnostics, err := s.ListWithDiagnostics()
191		if err != nil {
192			return nil, err
193		}
194		if s.diagnostics != nil {
195			for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
196				s.diagnostics(diagnostic)
197			}
198		}
199		return entries, nil
200	}
201	
202	// ListWithDiagnostics is List's explicit diagnostic form. It is useful to
203	// services that want to aggregate notices rather than render them immediately.
204	func (s *Store) ListWithDiagnostics() ([]*Entry, []Diagnostic, error) {
205		directoryEntries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
206		if err != nil {
207			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
208				return nil, nil, nil
209			}
210			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog directory: %w", err)
211		}
212	
213		var entries []*Entry
214		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
215		for _, directoryEntry := range directoryEntries {
216			name := directoryEntry.Name()
217			if directoryEntry.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") {
218				continue
219			}
220			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
221			entry, err := s.Get(id)
222			if err != nil {
223				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err})
224				continue
225			}
226			entries = append(entries, entry)
227		}
228		Sort(entries)
229		sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
230		return entries, diagnostics, nil
231	}
232	
233	// Update applies mutate to a deep copy and atomically replaces the record only
234	// if the mutation and validation both succeed. ID, Created, and Discovered are
235	// immutable.
236	func (s *Store) Update(id string, mutate func(*Entry) error) (*Entry, error) {
237		if err := ValidateID(id); err != nil {
238			return nil, err
239		}
240		if mutate == nil {
241			return nil, errors.New("catalog update requires a mutation")
242		}
243	
244		s.mu.Lock()
245		defer s.mu.Unlock()
246	
247		current, err := s.get(id)
248		if err != nil {
249			return nil, err
250		}
251		updated := current.Clone()
252		if err := mutate(updated); err != nil {
253			return nil, err
254		}
255		if updated.ID != current.ID {
256			return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change ID")
257		}
258		if updated.SchemaVersion != current.SchemaVersion {
259			return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change schema version")
260		}
261		if !updated.Created.Equal(current.Created) {
262			return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change Created")
263		}
264		if !updated.Discovered.Equal(current.Discovered) {
265			return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change Discovered")
266		}
267	
268		now := s.now()
269		updated.Updated = now
270		prepareNested(updated, now)
271		updated.Normalize()
272		if err := updated.Validate(); err != nil {
273			return nil, err
274		}
275		if err := s.writeAtomic(updated); err != nil {
276			return nil, err
277		}
278		return updated.Clone(), nil
279	}
280	
281	// Sort orders entries by stable ID.
282	func Sort(entries []*Entry) {
283		sort.SliceStable(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
284			return entries[i].ID < entries[j].ID
285		})
286	}
287	
288	func (s *Store) writeAtomic(entry *Entry) error {
289		temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+entry.ID+".*.tmp")
290		if err != nil {
291			return fmt.Errorf("create catalog temp file: %w", err)
292		}
293		name := temporary.Name()
294		defer os.Remove(name)
295	
296		if err := toml.NewEncoder(temporary).Encode(entry); err != nil {
297			_ = temporary.Close()
298			return fmt.Errorf("encode catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
299		}
300		if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
301			return fmt.Errorf("close catalog temp file: %w", err)
302		}
303		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o644); err != nil {
304			return fmt.Errorf("set catalog file mode: %w", err)
305		}
306		if err := os.Rename(name, s.path(entry.ID)); err != nil {
307			return fmt.Errorf("replace catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
308		}
309		return nil
310	}
311	
312	func (s *Store) nextID() string {
313		if s.generateID == nil {
314			return uuid.NewString()
315		}
316		return s.generateID()
317	}
318	
319	func (s *Store) now() time.Time {
320		if s.clock == nil {
321			return time.Now().UTC()
322		}
323		return s.clock().UTC()
324	}
325	
326	func prepareNested(entry *Entry, now time.Time) {
327		if entry.Experiment != nil && entry.Experiment.Started.IsZero() {
328			entry.Experiment.Started = now
329		}
330		for host, location := range entry.Locations {
331			if location.Updated.IsZero() {
332				location.Updated = now
333				entry.Locations[host] = location
334			}
335		}
336		if entry.RecoveryReceipt != nil && entry.RecoveryReceipt.Created.IsZero() {
337			entry.RecoveryReceipt.Created = now
338		}
339		if entry.MoveIntent != nil && entry.MoveIntent.Started.IsZero() {
340			entry.MoveIntent.Started = now
341		}
342	}

16	
17	var ErrAmbiguous = errors.New("ambiguous catalog match")
18	
19	// AmbiguousMatchError reports records that cannot be safely distinguished. A
20	// remote-only ambiguity is never resolved by picking the first entry.
21	type AmbiguousMatchError struct {
22		Observation  Observation
23		CandidateIDs []string
24		Reason       string
25	}
26	
27	func (e *AmbiguousMatchError) Error() string {
28		reason := e.Reason
29		if reason == "" {
30			reason = "multiple records match"
31		}
32		return fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s (%s)", ErrAmbiguous, reason, strings.Join(e.CandidateIDs, ", "))
33	}
34	
35	func (e *AmbiguousMatchError) Unwrap() error { return ErrAmbiguous }
36	
37	// Observation is live repository identity gathered from discovery. Path is the
38	// navigation path, RealPath its physical target, and either common-dir field may
39	// carry Git's shared administrative directory. CommonDir matches repo.Repo;
40	// GitCommonDir is accepted for callers using gitx.Repo terminology.
41	type Observation struct {
42		Host           string
43		Path           string
44		RealPath       string
45		CommonDir      string
46		GitCommonDir   string
47		Name           string
48		RemoteIdentity string
49	}
50	
51	// Registry adds live matching and lazy repository persistence to a Store.
52	type Registry struct {
53		store *Store
54		mu    sync.Mutex
55	}
56	
57	// NewRegistry returns a registry backed by store.
58	func NewRegistry(store *Store) *Registry { return &Registry{store: store} }
59	
60	// Store exposes the durable store for callers that need listing APIs.
61	func (r *Registry) Store() *Store { return r.store }
62	
63	// Match finds an observation without changing the catalog. Exact canonical path
64	// or common-directory identity on the same host always wins. A remote identity
65	// is considered only as a conservative relocation hint.
66	func (r *Registry) Match(observation Observation) (*Entry, error) {
67		normalized, err := normalizeObservation(observation, false)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, err
70		}
71		entry, _, err := r.match(normalized)
72		return entry, err
73	}
74	
75	// EnsureRepository returns the matching repository, attaching the observed host
76	// location when safe. If nothing matches—or a remote is ambiguous because it
77	// may describe another live clone—it creates a distinct repository record.
78	func (r *Registry) EnsureRepository(observation Observation) (*Entry, error) {
79		normalized, err := normalizeObservation(observation, true)
80		if err != nil {
81			return nil, err
82		}
83		if r == nil || r.store == nil {
84			return nil, errors.New("catalog registry has no store")
85		}
86	
87		r.mu.Lock()
88		defer r.mu.Unlock()
89	
90		matched, method, matchErr := r.match(normalized)
91		if matchErr == nil {
92			return r.attach(matched.ID, normalized)
93		}
94		if !errors.Is(matchErr, ErrNotFound) && !(errors.Is(matchErr, ErrAmbiguous) && method == matchRemote) {
95			return nil, matchErr
96		}

112	// Patch applies an atomic catalog mutation.
113	func (r *Registry) Patch(id string, mutate func(*Entry) error) (*Entry, error) {
114		if r == nil || r.store == nil {
115			return nil, errors.New("catalog registry has no store")
116		}
117		return r.store.Update(id, mutate)
118	}

120	// Attach explicitly records observation as id's present location. Explicit
121	// attachment may update a changed remote because the caller supplied the stable
122	// catalog identity rather than asking the remote hint to choose one.
123	func (r *Registry) Attach(id string, observation Observation) (*Entry, error) {
124		normalized, err := normalizeObservation(observation, true)
125		if err != nil {
126			return nil, err
127		}
128		if r == nil || r.store == nil {
129			return nil, errors.New("catalog registry has no store")
130		}
131		return r.attach(id, normalized)

134	func (r *Registry) attach(id string, observation Observation) (*Entry, error) {
135		return r.store.Update(id, func(entry *Entry) error {
136			if observation.RemoteIdentity != "" {

138			}
139			return entry.SetLocation(observation.Host, locationFromObservation(observation))
140		})
141	}

143	// FindByPath performs only exact host+canonical-path matching; it never falls
144	// back to a remote identity.
145	func (r *Registry) FindByPath(host, path string) (*Entry, error) {
146		normalized, err := normalizeObservation(Observation{Host: host, Path: path}, false)
147		if err != nil {
148			return nil, err
149		}
150		entries, err := r.entries()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		matches := exactMatches(entries, normalized)
155		return selectExact(normalized, matches)
156	}
157	
158	// FindByCommonDir performs exact host+Git-common-directory matching.
159	func (r *Registry) FindByCommonDir(host, commonDir string) (*Entry, error) {
160		normalized, err := normalizeObservation(Observation{Host: host, CommonDir: commonDir}, false)
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, err
163		}
164		entries, err := r.entries()
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, err
167		}
168		matches := exactMatches(entries, normalized)
169		return selectExact(normalized, matches)

171	
172	type matchMethod int
173	
174	const (
175		matchNone matchMethod = iota
176		matchExact
177		matchRemote
178	)
179	
180	func (r *Registry) match(observation Observation) (*Entry, matchMethod, error) {
181		entries, err := r.entries()
182		if err != nil {
183			return nil, matchNone, err
184		}
185		if matches := exactMatches(entries, observation); len(matches) > 0 {
186			entry, err := selectExact(observation, matches)
187			return entry, matchExact, err
188		}
189		if observation.RemoteIdentity == "" {
190			return nil, matchNone, fmt.Errorf("catalog observation %q: %w", observation.Path, ErrNotFound)
191		}
192	
193		var remoteMatches []*Entry
194		for _, entry := range entries {
195			if NormalizeRemoteIdentity(entry.RemoteIdentity) == observation.RemoteIdentity {
196				remoteMatches = append(remoteMatches, entry)
197			}
198		}
199		Sort(remoteMatches)
200		switch len(remoteMatches) {
201		case 0:
202			return nil, matchNone, fmt.Errorf("remote %q: %w", observation.RemoteIdentity, ErrNotFound)
203		case 1:
204			if remoteCanRelocate(remoteMatches[0], observation) {
205				return remoteMatches[0], matchRemote, nil
206			}
207			return nil, matchRemote, ambiguous(observation, remoteMatches,
208				"remote also belongs to a different live clone on this host")
209		default:
210			return nil, matchRemote, ambiguous(observation, remoteMatches,
211				"remote identity matches multiple catalog records")
212		}
213	}
214	
215	func (r *Registry) entries() ([]*Entry, error) {
216		if r == nil || r.store == nil {
217			return nil, errors.New("catalog registry has no store")
218		}
219		return r.store.List()
220	}
221	
222	func exactMatches(entries []*Entry, observation Observation) []*Entry {
223		matched := make(map[string]*Entry)
224		observationPaths := canonicalValues(observation.Path, observation.RealPath)
225		observationCommon := canonicalValue(observation.CommonDir)
226		for _, entry := range entries {
227			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(observation.Host)
228			if !ok {
229				continue
230			}
231			locationPaths := canonicalValues(location.CurrentPath, location.RealPath)
232			pathMatch := intersects(observationPaths, locationPaths)
233			commonMatch := observationCommon != "" && observationCommon == canonicalValue(location.GitCommonDir)
234			if pathMatch || commonMatch {
235				matched[entry.ID] = entry
236			}
237		}
238		out := make([]*Entry, 0, len(matched))
239		for _, entry := range matched {
240			out = append(out, entry)
241		}
242		Sort(out)
243		return out
244	}
245	
246	func selectExact(observation Observation, matches []*Entry) (*Entry, error) {
247		switch len(matches) {
248		case 0:
249			return nil, fmt.Errorf("catalog path %q on host %q: %w", observation.Path, observation.Host, ErrNotFound)
250		case 1:
251			return matches[0], nil
252		default:
253			return nil, ambiguous(observation, matches, "canonical path or Git common directory matches multiple records")
254		}
255	}
256	
257	func ambiguous(observation Observation, entries []*Entry, reason string) error {
258		ids := make([]string, len(entries))
259		for i, entry := range entries {
260			ids[i] = entry.ID
261		}
262		sort.Strings(ids)
263		return &AmbiguousMatchError{Observation: observation, CandidateIDs: ids, Reason: reason}
264	}
265	
266	func remoteCanRelocate(entry *Entry, observation Observation) bool {
267		location, ok := entry.LocationFor(observation.Host)
268		if !ok || location.State != LocationPresent || location.CurrentPath == "" {
269			return true
270		}
271		// Exact aliases and common directories were already handled. A still-present
272		// different path is another clone, not evidence that this record moved.
273		_, err := os.Stat(location.CurrentPath)
274		return errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
275	}
276	
277	func locationFromObservation(observation Observation) Location {
278		currentPath := observation.Path
279		if currentPath == "" {
280			currentPath = observation.RealPath
281		}
282		return Location{
283			State:        LocationPresent,
284			CurrentPath:  currentPath,
285			RealPath:     observation.RealPath,
286			GitCommonDir: observation.CommonDir,
287		}
288	}
289	
290	func normalizeObservation(observation Observation, requireLocation bool) (Observation, error) {
291		observation.Host = strings.TrimSpace(observation.Host)
292		observation.Name = strings.TrimSpace(observation.Name)
293		if observation.Host == "" {
294			return Observation{}, errors.New("catalog observation host is required")
295		}
296	
297		commonDir := observation.CommonDir
298		if commonDir == "" {
299			commonDir = observation.GitCommonDir
300		} else if observation.GitCommonDir != "" {
301			left, leftErr := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
302			right, rightErr := pathx.Canonical(observation.GitCommonDir)
303			if leftErr != nil || rightErr != nil || left != right {
304				return Observation{}, errors.New("catalog observation CommonDir and GitCommonDir disagree")
305			}
306		}
307	
308		var err error
309		if observation.Path != "" {
310			observation.Path, err = absoluteClean(observation.Path)
311			if err != nil {
312				return Observation{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog observation path: %w", err)
313			}
314		}
315		if observation.RealPath != "" {
316			observation.RealPath, err = pathx.Canonical(observation.RealPath)
317			if err != nil {
318				return Observation{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog observation real path: %w", err)
319			}
320		} else if observation.Path != "" {
321			observation.RealPath, err = pathx.Canonical(observation.Path)
322			if err != nil {
323				return Observation{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog observation path: %w", err)
324			}
325		}
326		if commonDir != "" {
327			observation.CommonDir, err = pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
328			if err != nil {
329				return Observation{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog observation Git common directory: %w", err)
330			}
331		}
332		observation.GitCommonDir = observation.CommonDir
333		observation.RemoteIdentity = NormalizeRemoteIdentity(observation.RemoteIdentity)
334	
335		if requireLocation && observation.Path == "" && observation.RealPath == "" {
336			return Observation{}, errors.New("catalog repository observation requires a path")
337		}
338		if observation.Name == "" {
339			path := observation.Path
340			if path == "" {
341				path = observation.RealPath
342			}
343			observation.Name = filepath.Base(path)
344		}
345		if requireLocation && (observation.Name == "" || observation.Name == ".") {
346			return Observation{}, errors.New("catalog repository observation requires a name")
347		}
348		return observation, nil
349	}
350	
351	func absoluteClean(path string) (string, error) {
352		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
353		if err != nil {
354			return "", err
355		}
356		return filepath.Clean(absolute), nil
357	}
358	
359	func canonicalValues(values ...string) map[string]struct{} {
360		out := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
361		for _, value := range values {
362			if canonical := canonicalValue(value); canonical != "" {
363				out[canonical] = struct{}{}
364			}
365		}
366		return out
367	}
368	
369	func canonicalValue(value string) string {
370		if value == "" {
371			return ""
372		}
373		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(value)
374		if err != nil {
375			return ""
376		}
377		return canonical
378	}
379	
380	func intersects(left, right map[string]struct{}) bool {
381		for value := range left {
382			if _, ok := right[value]; ok {
383				return true
384			}
385		}
386		return false
387	}
388	
389	// NormalizeRemoteIdentity converts common HTTPS and SCP-style Git URLs into a
390	// stable lower-case host/path key. The result remains only a hint for matching.
391	func NormalizeRemoteIdentity(identity string) string {
392		identity = strings.TrimSpace(identity)
393		if identity == "" {
394			return ""
395		}
396		if parsed, err := url.Parse(identity); err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" {
397			identity = parsed.Host + "/" + strings.TrimPrefix(parsed.Path, "/")
398		} else if at := strings.LastIndexByte(identity, '@'); at >= 0 {
399			afterUser := identity[at+1:]
400			if colon := strings.IndexByte(afterUser, ':'); colon >= 0 {
401				identity = afterUser[:colon] + "/" + afterUser[colon+1:]
402			}
403		}
404		identity = strings.Trim(identity, "/")
405		identity = strings.TrimSuffix(identity, ".git")
406		return strings.ToLower(identity)
407	}

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"slices"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	var (
17		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
18		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
19		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
20		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
21		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
22		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
23		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
24		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
25	)
26	
27	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
28	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
29	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
30	// before creating or moving anything into it.
31	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
32		if path == "" {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
34		}
35		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
36		if err != nil {
37			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
38		}
39		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
40	
41		probe := absolute
42		var missing []string
43		for {
44			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
45			if err == nil {
46				slices.Reverse(missing)
47				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
48				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
49			}
50			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
51				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
52			}
53			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
54			if parent == probe {
55				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
56			}
57			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
58			probe = parent
59		}
60	}
61	
62	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
63	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
64	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
65	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
66		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
67			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
68		}
69		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
70		if err != nil {
71			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
72		}
73		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
74		if err != nil {
75			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
76		}
77	
78		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
79		if err != nil {
80			return "", fmt.Errorf("compare %q with root %q: %w", candidate, root, err)
81		}
82		switch {
83		case rel == ".":
84			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
85		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
86			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
87		default:
88			return canonicalCandidate, nil
89		}
90	}

93	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.

105	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one

112		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):

package catalog_test

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
)

func idSequence(ids ...string) catalog.IDGenerator {
	index := 0
	return func() string {
		if index >= len(ids) {
			return ids[len(ids)-1]
		}
		id := ids[index]
		index++
		return id
	}
}

func TestRegistryMatchesExactCanonicalPathBeforeRemote(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	physical := filepath.Join(root, "physical")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(physical, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	alias := filepath.Join(root, "alias")
	if err := os.Symlink(physical, alias); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlinks unavailable: %v", err)
	}

	store := catalog.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "assets"),
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(idSequence(firstID, secondID)))
	registry := catalog.NewRegistry(store)
	original, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host:           "laptop",
		Path:           physical,
		CommonDir:      filepath.Join(physical, ".git"),
		Name:           "repo",
		RemoteIdentity: "https://github.com/example/repo.git",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	matched, err := registry.Match(catalog.Observation{
		Host:           "laptop",
		Path:           alias,
		RemoteIdentity: "github.com/someone/entirely-different",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Match alias: %v", err)
	}
	if matched.ID != original.ID {
		t.Errorf("canonical path match = %s, want %s", matched.ID, original.ID)
	}
	found, err := registry.FindByPath("laptop", alias)
	if err != nil || found.ID != original.ID {
		t.Errorf("FindByPath = %+v, %v", found, err)
	}
}

func TestRegistryMatchesGitCommonDirectory(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	mainPath := filepath.Join(root, "main")
	worktreePath := filepath.Join(root, "worktree")
	commonDir := filepath.Join(root, "git-common")
	for _, path := range []string{mainPath, worktreePath, commonDir} {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	registry := catalog.NewRegistry(catalog.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "assets"),
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(func() string { return firstID })))
	original, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "desktop", Path: mainPath, CommonDir: commonDir, Name: "repo",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	matched, err := registry.Match(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "desktop", Path: worktreePath, GitCommonDir: commonDir, Name: "repo",
	})
	if err != nil || matched.ID != original.ID {
		t.Fatalf("common-dir Match = %+v, %v", matched, err)
	}
	found, err := registry.FindByCommonDir("desktop", commonDir)
	if err != nil || found.ID != original.ID {
		t.Errorf("FindByCommonDir = %+v, %v", found, err)
	}
}

func TestRegistryRemoteAmbiguityNeverAutoMergesClones(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	paths := []string{
		filepath.Join(root, "clone-one"),
		filepath.Join(root, "clone-two"),
		filepath.Join(root, "clone-three"),
	}
	for _, path := range paths {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	thirdID := "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333"
	store := catalog.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "assets"),
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(idSequence(firstID, secondID, thirdID)))
	registry := catalog.NewRegistry(store)
	remote := "git@github.com:example/shared.git"

	first, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: paths[0], Name: "shared", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: paths[1], Name: "shared-copy", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if first.ID == second.ID {
		t.Fatal("a second live clone was auto-merged by remote identity")
	}

	_, err = registry.Match(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: paths[2], Name: "third", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, catalog.ErrAmbiguous) {
		t.Fatalf("ambiguous remote Match = %v, want ErrAmbiguous", err)
	}
	var ambiguous *catalog.AmbiguousMatchError
	if !errors.As(err, &ambiguous) || len(ambiguous.CandidateIDs) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("ambiguous candidates = %#v", err)
	}

	third, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: paths[2], Name: "third", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if third.ID == first.ID || third.ID == second.ID {
		t.Error("EnsureRepository chose an ambiguous remote candidate")
	}
	entries, err := store.List()
	if err != nil || len(entries) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("catalog should retain three clone identities: %d, %v", len(entries), err)
	}

	// Even with an ambiguous remote, an exact path is authoritative.
	matched, err := registry.Match(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: paths[0], RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil || matched.ID != first.ID {
		t.Errorf("exact path did not win: %+v, %v", matched, err)
	}
}

func TestRegistryUsesUniqueRemoteForMissingRelocation(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	oldPath := filepath.Join(root, "old")
	newPath := filepath.Join(root, "new")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(oldPath, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	registry := catalog.NewRegistry(catalog.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "assets"),
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(idSequence(firstID, secondID))))
	remote := "https://github.com/example/moved.git"
	original, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: oldPath, Name: "moved", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.RemoveAll(oldPath); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(newPath, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	relocated, err := registry.EnsureRepository(catalog.Observation{
		Host: "laptop", Path: newPath, Name: "moved", RemoteIdentity: remote,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if relocated.ID != original.ID {
		t.Errorf("unique missing relocation created %s, want stable %s", relocated.ID, original.ID)
	}
	location, _ := relocated.LocationFor("laptop")
	if location.CurrentPath != newPath {
		t.Errorf("relocated path = %q, want %q", location.CurrentPath, newPath)
	}
}

````markdown
# Repo quick notes + TUI notes workflow

## Context

The user wants quick thoughts attached to a repository and triggerable directly
from the TASKS/REPOS TUI. Notes must live in dev's sidecar state rather than
creating another dot-folder in every repository. The in-progress
`try-tui-metadata-reclamation` / `dev-try-wobbly-lovelace` work is introducing
`internal/catalog` with stable asset IDs, path/symlink/common-dir matching and
cross-host locations. Notes should wait for that work to land and use its stable
repository ID rather than invent a competing identity.

Chosen interaction:

- multiple append-only notes, not one overwritable scratchpad;
- `n` adds a quick one-line note to the selected local repo;
- `N` opens a notes overlay for browse/search/edit/delete;
- Markdown files are durable truth; SQLite FTS is a disposable index;
- `td` and `beads` stay optional future adapters, not core dependencies.

## Dependency / sequencing

1. Wait until the catalog agent's changes are committed and available on the
   current branch.
2. Verify the final `catalog.Registry` API and storage location before writing
   notes code. Reuse `EnsureRepository`, `Match`, stable `Entry.ID`, and
   host-local location matching.
3. Do not modify or stage the other agent's currently untracked
   `internal/catalog/`, `internal/pathx/`, or App/config integration while it is
   active.

## Storage design

### Durable source of truth

```
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/
└── <catalog-repository-id>/
    ├── <uuid>.md
    └── <uuid>.md
```

One file per thought minimizes cross-machine merge conflicts and keeps every
note readable/exportable without dev. Each file uses YAML/TOML-style frontmatter
plus Markdown body:

```markdown
---
schema_version: 1
id: <uuid>
repository_id: <catalog-id>
created: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
updated: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
tags: [idea, follow-up]
---

Try replacing the polling loop with an event subscription.
```

The filename ID and frontmatter ID must agree. Writes are temp-file + atomic
rename. Editing preserves ID/created/repository ID. Deleting requires explicit
confirmation (`--yes` escape hatch).

### Search index (disposable)

```
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
```

Use the existing pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` dependency with FTS5. Index note
body, tags, repo display name and catalog ID. The Markdown files remain
authoritative; if the database is absent/stale/corrupt, rebuild it.

- `dev note reindex` performs an explicit rebuild.
- add/edit/delete update the index incrementally.
- search detects a missing index and builds it.
- `dev cache list` reports `notes`; `dev cache clear notes` deletes only the
  FTS database and never the Markdown source.
- `stats.db` remains activity-only. Do not add note tables to it.

## CLI surface

Add `internal/note/` for the file store and FTS index, then wire:

```bash
dev note add [repo] "thought" [--tag TAG...]
dev note add [repo] --editor
dev note list [repo] [--tag TAG] [--json]
dev note show <note-id>
dev note search <query> [--repo REPO] [--json]
dev note edit <note-id> [--editor CMD]
dev note delete <note-id> [--yes]
dev note path [repo]
dev note reindex
```

Repo inference follows existing command conventions: explicit repo argument,
otherwise task/repository containing cwd. Resolve/ensure repository identity
through the catalog Registry using observed host, navigation path, real path,
Git common dir and normalised remote identity.

`add` requires text or `--editor`; it must not silently create an empty note.
Structured output goes to stdout; diagnostics to stderr.

## TUI interaction

Extend the existing context-sensitive key model in `internal/tui/model.go` and
`internal/tui/view.go`:

### Quick add (`n`)

- TASKS / REPOS: `n` opens a one-line prompt for the selected repo.
- REMOTE: only enabled when a local clone exists.
- Enter atomically creates one note and refreshes note counts/latest preview.
- Esc cancels without writing.

### Notes overlay (`N`)

Default scope is the selected repository:

```text
NOTES · dev-cli                                     4 notes

  WHEN   TAGS              THOUGHT
▸ 2m     idea,git          distinguish staged vs unstaged counts
  3d     follow-up         test glab member endpoint on newer CLI

j/k move · / search · Enter expand · a add · e edit · d delete · Esc back
```

- `/` uses the FTS index and searches body/tags/repo.
- Enter toggles expanded Markdown body.
- `a` enters the same add prompt as `n`.
- `e` suspends Bubble Tea via `tea.ExecProcess`, using the existing editor
  resolution (`--editor`/VISUAL/EDITOR/nvim/vim/vi), then atomically validates
  and reindexes the edited note.
- `d` enters a visible confirmation mode; no one-key deletion.
- The global `e = edit config` remains unchanged outside the notes overlay.

Add a configurable `notes` REPOS column (count), but do not enable it by
default because the default table is already width-constrained. The selected
repo/task detail pane shows note count and latest-note preview.

## Catalog integration

Create a small adapter from live `repo.Repo` / task checkout facts to
`catalog.Observation`; reuse it from CLI and TUI. The note store keys only by
catalog ID, never by mutable filesystem path. A rename, symlink index, physical
move or second host therefore keeps the same notes.

The existing `catalog.Entry.Note` field is not used as the multi-note store.
Leave it compatible for the catalog agent; optionally plan a later migration of
non-empty legacy `Entry.Note` into one append-only note after both features are
stable.

## External task-tool boundary

Keep the TODO entries for `td` and `beads`. A future adapter may detect their
repo-local dot-folders and delegate through their CLIs. It must not mirror those
tasks into dev notes or create their folders automatically. Notes are informal
sidecar thoughts; td/beads are structured repo-local task systems.

## Critical files

- New: `internal/note/{note,store,index}.go` and tests.
- Catalog integration: the final committed `internal/catalog` APIs and
  `internal/cli/app.go` registry wiring.
- CLI: new `internal/cli/note.go`, `internal/cli/root.go`, `internal/cli/cache.go`.
- TUI: `internal/tui/{model,rows,view}.go`, `internal/cli/tui.go` and tests.
- Config/path helpers: `internal/config/config.go` only if note paths/options
  need an explicit surface.
- Docs/skill: README, storage/TUI help topics, `internal/skill/dev-cli`,
  generated command reference, TODO promotion.

## Verification

### Unit

- note frontmatter round-trip and schema/ID validation;
- atomic create/edit and safe delete;
- one-note-per-file concurrency and deterministic ordering;
- catalog ID survives repo rename/symlink/host location change;
- FTS body/tag/repo search, missing-index rebuild and incremental update;
- clearing `notes.db` leaves Markdown files untouched;
- malformed note is diagnosed without hiding valid notes.

### TUI

- `n` adds to the selected TASK/REPO and is disabled for uncloned REMOTE;
- `N` overlay navigation, live search, expand, editor callback and confirmed
  delete;
- note overlay respects terminal height/top-bar invariants;
- returning from editor refreshes note data/index;
- optional notes column and detail preview.

### CLI / end-to-end

In a sandboxed HOME/XDG state:

```bash
dev bootstrap <repo-root>
dev note add demo "try event subscription" --tag idea
dev note list demo --json

- plan: `# Repo quick notes + TUI notes workflow

## Context

The user wants quick thoughts attached to a repository and triggerable directly
from the TASKS/REPOS TUI. Notes must live in dev's sidecar state rather than
creating another dot-folder in every repository. The in-progress
`try-tui-metadata-reclamation` / `dev-try-wobbly-lovelace` work is introducing
`internal/catalog` with stable asset IDs, path/symlink/common-dir matching and
cross-host locations. Notes should wait for that work to land and use its stable
repository ID rather than invent a competing identity.

Chosen interaction:

- multiple append-only notes, not one overwritable scratchpad;
- `n` adds a quick one-line note to the selected local repo;
- `N` opens a notes overlay for browse/search/edit/delete;
- Markdown files are durable truth; SQLite FTS is a disposable index;
- `td` and `beads` stay optional future adapters, not core dependencies.

## Dependency / sequencing

1. Wait until the catalog agent's changes are committed and available on the
   current branch.
2. Verify the final `catalog.Registry` API and storage location before writing
   notes code. Reuse `EnsureRepository`, `Match`, stable `Entry.ID`, and
   host-local location matching.
3. Do not modify or stage the other agent's currently untracked
   `internal/catalog/`, `internal/pathx/`, or App/config integration while it is
   active.

## Storage design

### Durable source of truth

```
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/
└── <catalog-repository-id>/
    ├── <uuid>.md
    └── <uuid>.md
```

One file per thought minimizes cross-machine merge conflicts and keeps every
note readable/exportable without dev. Each file uses YAML/TOML-style frontmatter
plus Markdown body:

```markdown
---
schema_version: 1
id: <uuid>
repository_id: <catalog-id>
created: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
updated: 2026-08-27T10:30:00Z
tags: [idea, follow-up]
---

Try replacing the polling loop with an event subscription.
```

The filename ID and frontmatter ID must agree. Writes are temp-file + atomic
rename. Editing preserves ID/created/repository ID. Deleting requires explicit
confirmation (`--yes` escape hatch).

### Search index (disposable)

```
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
```

Use the existing pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` dependency with FTS5. Index note
body, tags, repo display name and catalog ID. The Markdown files remain
authoritative; if the database is absent/stale/corrupt, rebuild it.

- `dev note reindex` performs an explicit rebuild.
- add/edit/delete update the index incrementally.
- search detects a missing index and builds it.
- `dev cache list` reports `notes`; `dev cache clear notes` deletes only the
  FTS database and never the Markdown source.
- `stats.db` remains activity-only. Do not add note tables to it.

## CLI surface

Add `internal/note/` for the file store and FTS index, then wire:

```bash
dev note add [repo] "thought" [--tag TAG...]
dev note add [repo] --editor
dev note list [repo] [--tag TAG] [--json]
dev note show <note-id>
dev note search <query> [--repo REPO] [--json]
dev note edit <note-id> [--editor CMD]
dev note delete <note-id> [--yes]
dev note path [repo]
dev note reindex
```

Repo inference follows existing command conventions: explicit repo argument,
otherwise task/repository containing cwd. Resolve/ensure repository identity
through the catalog Registry using observed host, navigation path, real path,
Git common dir and normalised remote identity.

`add` requires text or `--editor`; it must not silently create an empty note.
Structured output goes to stdout; diagnostics to stderr.

## TUI interaction

Extend the existing context-sensitive key model in `internal/tui/model.go` and
`internal/tui/view.go`:

### Quick add (`n`)

- TASKS / REPOS: `n` opens a one-line prompt for the selected repo.
- REMOTE: only enabled when a local clone exists.
- Enter atomically creates one note and refreshes note counts/latest preview.
- Esc cancels without writing.

### Notes overlay (`N`)

Default scope is the selected repository:

```text
NOTES · dev-cli                                     4 notes

  WHEN   TAGS              THOUGHT
▸ 2m     idea,git          distinguish staged vs unstaged counts
  3d     follow-up         test glab member endpoint on newer CLI

j/k move · / search · Enter expand · a add · e edit · d delete · Esc back
```

- `/` uses the FTS index and searches body/tags/repo.
- Enter toggles expanded Markdown body.
- `a` enters the same add prompt as `n`.
- `e` suspends Bubble Tea via `tea.ExecProcess`, using the existing editor
  resolution (`--editor`/VISUAL/EDITOR/nvim/vim/vi), then atomically validates
  and reindexes the edited note.
- `d` enters a visible confirmation mode; no one-key deletion.
- The global `e = edit config` remains unchanged outside the notes overlay.

Add a configurable `notes` REPOS column (count), but do not enable it by
default because the default table is already width-constrained. The selected
repo/task detail pane shows note count and latest-note preview.

## Catalog integration

Create a small adapter from live `repo.Repo` / task checkout facts to
`catalog.Observation`; reuse it from CLI and TUI. The note store keys only by
catalog ID, never by mutable filesystem path. A rename, symlink index, physical
move or second host therefore keeps the same notes.

The existing `catalog.Entry.Note` field is not used as the multi-note store.
Leave it compatible for the catalog agent; optionally plan a later migration of
non-empty legacy `Entry.Note` into one append-only note after both features are
stable.

## External task-tool boundary

Keep the TODO entries for `td` and `beads`. A future adapter may detect their
repo-local dot-folders and delegate through their CLIs. It must not mirror those
tasks into dev notes or create their folders automatically. Notes are informal
sidecar thoughts; td/beads are structured repo-local task systems.

## Critical files

- New: `internal/note/{note,store,index}.go` and tests.
- Catalog integration: the final committed `internal/catalog` APIs and
  `internal/cli/app.go` registry wiring.
- CLI: new `internal/cli/note.go`, `internal/cli/root.go`, `internal/cli/cache.go`.
- TUI: `internal/tui/{model,rows,view}.go`, `internal/cli/tui.go` and tests.
- Config/path helpers: `internal/config/config.go` only if note paths/options
  need an explicit surface.
- Docs/skill: README, storage/TUI help topics, `internal/skill/dev-cli`,
  generated command reference, TODO promotion.

## Verification

### Unit

- note frontmatter round-trip and schema/ID validation;
- atomic create/edit and safe delete;
- one-note-per-file concurrency and deterministic ordering;
- catalog ID survives repo rename/symlink/host location change;
- FTS body/tag/repo search, missing-index rebuild and incremental update;
- clearing `notes.db` leaves Markdown files untouched;
- malformed note is diagnosed without hiding valid notes.

### TUI

- note overlay respects terminal height/top-bar invariants;
- returning from editor refreshes note data/index;
- optional notes column and detail preview.

In a sandboxed HOME/XDG state:

```
