171	func (m Model) renderRepos() string {
172		items := m.visibleRepoItems()
173		if len(items) == 0 {
174			if m.loadingLocal {
175				return "  " + styleDim.Render("Loading local repositories…") + "\n"
176			}
177			return "  " + styleDim.Render("No repositories found. Check paths.scan_roots in your config,"+
178				" or run `dev config init`.\n")
179		}
180		columns := m.repoColumns()
181	
182		var b strings.Builder
183		var headers []string
184		for _, c := range columns {
185			headers = append(headers, fitCell(c.header, c.width))
186		}
187		b.WriteString(styleHeader.Render("  "+strings.Join(headers, "  ")) + "\n")
188	
189		from, to := m.window(len(items))
190		for i := from; i < to; i++ {
191			item := items[i]
192			r := item.Repo
193			cells := make([]string, 0, len(columns))
194			for _, c := range columns {
195				cells = append(cells, fitCell(m.repoItemColumnValue(item, c.name), c.width))
196			}
197			line := strings.Join(cells, "  ")
198			styled := line
199			if checkout, child := item.checkout(); child {
200				if checkout.Status.Dirty() {
201					styled = styleDirty.Render(line)
202				} else if checkout.Ownership == inventory.CheckoutExternal ||
203					checkout.Ownership == inventory.CheckoutEphemeral {
204					styled = styleDim.Render(line)
205				}
206			} else if r.Status.Dirty() {
207				styled = styleDirty.Render(line)
208			} else if len(r.Tasks) == 0 && !r.Live {
209				styled = styleClean.Render(line)
210			}
211			b.WriteString(m.renderLine(i, line, styled))
212		}
213		b.WriteString(m.scrollNote(len(items), from, to))
214		return b.String()
215	}

217	func (m Model) repoItemColumnValue(item repoItem, name string) string {
218		r := item.Repo
219		checkout, child := item.checkout()
220		if !child {
221			if name == "repo" && r.Worktrees > 0 {
222				marker := "▸ "
223				if m.repoExpanded(r) {
224					marker = "▾ "
225				}
226				return marker + r.Repo.Display()
227			}
228			if name == "live" {
229				return parentLiveColumn(r)
230			}
231			return repoColumnValue(r, name)
232		}
233	
234		switch name {
235		case "repo":
236			connector := "├─ "
237			if item.CheckoutIndex == len(r.Context.Checkouts)-1 {
238				connector = "└─ "
239			}
240			label := filepath.Base(checkout.Worktree.Path)
241			if label == "." || label == string(filepath.Separator) || label == "" {
242				label = checkout.Branch()
243			}
244			if checkout.Ownership == inventory.CheckoutExternal || checkout.Ownership == inventory.CheckoutEphemeral {
245				label += " (" + string(checkout.Ownership) + ")"
246			}
247			return connector + label
248		case "branch":
249			if branch := checkout.Branch(); branch != "" {
250				return branch
251			}
252			return "(detached)"
253		case "git":
254			switch {
255			case checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists:
256				return "prunable"
257			case checkout.Worktree.Locked:
258				return "locked"
259			case checkout.StatusErr != nil:
260				return "?"

144	func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
145		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
146		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
147			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
148			if structured {
149				switch key {
150				case "tag":
151					if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
152						return false
153					}
154					continue
155				case "remote":
156					if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
157						return false
158					}
159					continue
160				case "size":
161					if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
162						return false
163					}
164					continue
165				case "kind":
166					kind := catalog.KindRepository
167					if r.Asset != nil {
168						kind = r.Asset.Kind
169					}
170					if string(kind) != value {
171						return false
172					}
173					continue
174				}
175			}
176			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
177				return false
178			}
179		}
180		return true
181	}

// NoteTarget identifies the selected local repository. CatalogID may be empty
// until the first note action persists the repository observation.
type NoteTarget struct {
	CatalogID string
	Repo      repo.Repo
}

func (t NoteTarget) Name() string { return t.Repo.Name }
func (t NoteTarget) Path() string { return t.Repo.Path }

// NoteEdit suspends the TUI in an editor and atomically completes from its
// temporary body after the process exits.
type NoteEdit struct {
	Command  *exec.Cmd
	Complete func() error
}

	List   func(ctx context.Context, target NoteTarget) ([]*note.Note, error)

func (m Model) openNoteAdd(target NoteTarget, returnToBrowse bool) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

func (m Model) openNotes(target NoteTarget) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	m.noteTarget, m.noteQuery = target, ""
	m.noteCursor, m.noteExpanded = 0, false
	m.mode, m.noteLoading, m.err = modeNoteBrowse, true, nil
	return m, m.loadNotes()

func (m Model) loadNotes() tea.Cmd {
	return func() tea.Msg {
		if m.actions.Notes.List == nil {
			return noteListMsg{}
		}
		var (
			notes []*note.Note
			err   error
		)
		if m.noteQuery != "" && m.actions.Notes.Search != nil {
			notes, err = m.actions.Notes.Search(context.Background(), m.noteTarget, m.noteQuery)
		} else {
			notes, err = m.actions.Notes.List(context.Background(), m.noteTarget)
		}
		return noteListMsg{notes: notes, err: err}
	}
}

func (m Model) currentNote() (*note.Note, bool) {
	if m.noteCursor < 0 || m.noteCursor >= len(m.notes) {
		return nil, false
	}
	return m.notes[m.noteCursor], true
}

func (m *Model) clampNoteCursor() {
	switch {
	case len(m.notes) == 0:
		m.noteCursor = 0
	case m.noteCursor >= len(m.notes):
		m.noteCursor = len(m.notes) - 1
	case m.noteCursor < 0:
		m.noteCursor = 0
	}
}

func (m Model) updateNotes(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	switch m.mode {
	case modeNoteBrowse:
		switch msg.String() {
		case "esc", "N", "q":
			m.mode, m.notes, m.noteQuery, m.err = modeList, nil, "", nil
			return m, nil
		case "j", "down":
			m.noteCursor++
			m.noteExpanded = false
			m.clampNoteCursor()
		case "k", "up":
			m.noteCursor--
			m.noteExpanded = false
			m.clampNoteCursor()
		case "g", "home":
			m.noteCursor, m.noteExpanded = 0, false
		case "G", "end":
			m.noteCursor, m.noteExpanded = len(m.notes)-1, false
			m.clampNoteCursor()
		case "enter":
			if _, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
				m.noteExpanded = !m.noteExpanded
			}
		case "a", "n":
			return m.openNoteAdd(m.noteTarget, true)
		case "/":
			m.mode = modeNoteSearch
			m.input.SetValue(m.noteQuery)
			m.input.Placeholder = "search body, tags, repo"
			m.input.CursorEnd()
			return m, m.input.Focus()
		case "d":
			if _, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
				m.mode = modeNoteConfirmDelete
			}
		case "e":
			n, ok := m.currentNote()
			if !ok || m.actions.Notes.Edit == nil {
				return m, nil
			}
			edit, err := m.actions.Notes.Edit(n)
			if err != nil {
				m.err = err
				return m, nil
			}
			return m, tea.ExecProcess(edit.Command, func(runErr error) tea.Msg {
				if runErr == nil && edit.Complete != nil {
					runErr = edit.Complete()
				}
				return noteActionMsg{status: "updated note " + n.ID[:8], returnBrowse: true, err: runErr}
			})
		}
		return m, nil

	case modeNoteAdd:
		switch msg.String() {
		case "esc":
			m.input.Blur()
			if m.noteReturnToBrowse {
				m.mode = modeNoteBrowse
			} else {
				m.mode = modeList
			}
			return m, nil
		case "enter":
			body := strings.TrimSpace(m.input.Value())
			if body == "" {
				m.err = fmt.Errorf("note body is empty")
				return m, nil
			}
			m.input.Blur()
			returnBrowse := m.noteReturnToBrowse
			return m, func() tea.Msg {
				status, err := m.actions.Notes.Add(context.Background(), m.noteTarget, body)
				return noteActionMsg{status: status, returnBrowse: returnBrowse, err: err}
			}
		}
		input, cmd := m.input.Update(msg)
		m.input = input
		return m, cmd

	case modeNoteSearch:
		switch msg.String() {
		case "esc":
			m.input.Blur()
			m.noteQuery, m.mode, m.noteLoading = "", modeNoteBrowse, true
			return m, m.loadNotes()
		case "enter":
			m.noteQuery = strings.TrimSpace(m.input.Value())
			m.input.Blur()
			m.mode, m.noteLoading, m.noteCursor = modeNoteBrowse, true, 0
			return m, m.loadNotes()
		}
		input, cmd := m.input.Update(msg)
		m.input = input
		return m, cmd

	case modeNoteConfirmDelete:
		switch msg.String() {
		case "esc", "n":
			m.mode = modeNoteBrowse
		case "y", "Y":
			n, ok := m.currentNote()
			if !ok || m.actions.Notes.Delete == nil {
				m.mode = modeNoteBrowse
				return m, nil
			}
			return m, func() tea.Msg {
				status, err := m.actions.Notes.Delete(context.Background(), n)
				return noteActionMsg{status: status, returnBrowse: true, err: err}
			}
		}
		return m, nil
	}
	return m, nil
}

cat > /Users/david/.herdr/worktrees/dev-cli/feat-repo-quick-notes/internal/tui/note_view.go <<'EOF'
package tui

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
)

func (m Model) noteMode() bool {
	return m.mode == modeNoteBrowse || m.mode == modeNoteAdd ||
		m.mode == modeNoteSearch || m.mode == modeNoteConfirmDelete
}

func (m Model) renderNotes() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	title := m.noteTarget.Name()
	if title == "" {
		title = "repository"
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n\n", styleTitle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("dev  NOTES  %s  ·  %d notes", title, len(m.notes))))

	switch m.mode {
	case modeNoteAdd:
		b.WriteString("  " + styleTitle.Render("quick thought") + "\n\n")
		b.WriteString("  " + m.input.View() + "\n\n")
		if m.err != nil {
			b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()) + "\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("enter save · esc cancel"))
		return b.String()

	case modeNoteSearch:
		b.WriteString("  " + styleTitle.Render("search") + "\n\n")
		b.WriteString("  " + m.input.View() + "\n\n")
		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("enter search · esc clear and return"))
		return b.String()

	case modeNoteConfirmDelete:
		if n, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
			b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("Delete note "+n.ID[:8]+"?") + "\n")
			b.WriteString("  " + n.Preview(max(20, m.width-6)) + "\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("y delete · n / esc cancel"))
		return b.String()
	}

	if m.noteQuery != "" {
		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("search: "+m.noteQuery) + "\n\n")
	}
	if m.noteLoading {
		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("Loading notes…") + "\n")
		return b.String()
	}
	if m.err != nil {
		b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()) + "\n")
	}
	if len(m.notes) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("No notes. Press a or n to add one.") + "\n\n")
		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("a/n add · / search · N/esc back"))
		return b.String()
	}

	idW, whenW, tagsW := 8, 6, clamp(m.width/5, 10, 24)
	thoughtW := m.width - idW - whenW - tagsW - 12
	if thoughtW < 20 {
		thoughtW = 20
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s  %s  %s  %s\n",
		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("ID", idW)),
		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("WHEN", whenW)),
		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("TAGS", tagsW)),
		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("THOUGHT", thoughtW)))

	maxRows := m.height - 11
	if m.noteExpanded {
		maxRows -= 6
	}
	if maxRows < 3 {
		maxRows = 3
	}
	from, to := noteWindow(len(m.notes), m.noteCursor, maxRows)
	for i := from; i < to; i++ {
		n := m.notes[i]
		tags := strings.Join(n.Tags, ",")
		if tags == "" {
			tags = "—"
		}
		line := strings.Join([]string{
			fitCell(n.ID[:8], idW), fitCell(noteAge(n.Created), whenW),
			fitCell(tags, tagsW), fitCell(n.Preview(thoughtW), thoughtW),
		}, "  ")
		if i == m.noteCursor {
			b.WriteString(styleSelected.Render("▸ ") + styleSelected.Render(line) + "\n")
		} else {
			b.WriteString("  " + line + "\n")
		}
	}
	if len(m.notes) > maxRows {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n", styleDim.Render(fmt.Sprintf("… %d–%d of %d", from+1, to, len(m.notes))))
	}
	if m.noteExpanded {
		if n, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
			body := lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(max(20, m.width-4)).Render(strings.TrimSpace(n.Body))
			b.WriteString("\n  " + styleDim.Render(n.ID+" · "+n.Updated.Format(time.RFC3339)) + "\n")
			b.WriteString("  " + strings.ReplaceAll(body, "\n", "\n  ") + "\n")
		}
	}
	b.WriteString("\n  " + styleHelp.Render("j/k move · / search · enter expand · a add · e edit · d delete · N/esc back"))
	return b.String()
}

func noteWindow(total, cursor, height int) (from, to int) {
	if total <= height {
		return 0, total
	}
	from = cursor - height/2
	if from < 0 {
		from = 0
	}
	if from+height > total {
		from = total - height
	}
	return from, from + height
}

func noteAge(created time.Time) string {
	d := time.Since(created)
	switch {
	case d < time.Minute:
		return "now"
	case d < time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
	case d < 24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
	case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
	}
}

func max(a, b int) int {
	if a > b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}
EOF

	if ref != "" {
		// A stable catalog ID is accepted anywhere a repo name is.
		if entry, err := app.Registry.Get(ref); err == nil {
			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname())
			if !ok || location.CurrentPath == "" {
				return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog repository %s has no path on this host", ref)
			}
			r := repo.Repo{Name: entry.Name, Path: location.CurrentPath,
				RealPath: location.RealPath, CommonDir: location.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true}
			return entry, r, nil
		}
		resolved, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
		}
		return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: resolved})
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
	}
	g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("%s is not in a repository; pass --repo", config.Contract(cwd))
	}
	r := repo.Repo{Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
		CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, MainRoot: g.MainRoot, HasGit: true}
	return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: r})
}

func ensureNoteRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, target tui.NoteTarget) (*catalog.Entry, repo.Repo, error) {
	r := target.Repo
	if target.CatalogID != "" {
		if entry, err := app.Registry.Get(target.CatalogID); err == nil {
			return entry, r, nil
		}
	}
	if r.RealPath == "" || r.CommonDir == "" {
		if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, r.Path); err == nil {
			// Notes belong to the clone's canonical repository, never to a
			// disposable linked-worktree path.
			r.Path, r.RealPath, r.MainRoot = g.MainRoot, g.MainRoot, g.MainRoot
			if r.Name == "" {
				r.Name = g.Name
			}
			r.CommonDir = g.GitCommonDir
		}
	}
	observation := catalog.Observation{
		Host: config.Hostname(), Path: r.Path, RealPath: r.RealPath,
		CommonDir: r.CommonDir, Name: r.Name,
		RemoteIdentity: gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"),
	}
	var entry *catalog.Entry
	err := app.Catalog.WithLock(ctx, func() error {
		var ensureErr error
		entry, ensureErr = app.Registry.EnsureRepository(observation)
		return ensureErr
	})
	return entry, r, err
}

func prepareTUINoteEdit(app *App, n *note.Note) (tui.NoteEdit, error) {
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-*.md")
	if err != nil {
		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
	}
	path := tmp.Name()
	if _, err := io.WriteString(tmp, n.Body); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		_ = os.Remove(path)
		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
	}
	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
		_ = os.Remove(path)
		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
	}
	proc, _, err := editorProcess(path, "")
	if err != nil {
		_ = os.Remove(path)
		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
	}
	return tui.NoteEdit{
		Command: proc,
		Complete: func(runErr error) error {
			defer os.Remove(path)
			if runErr != nil {
				return runErr
			}
			body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if strings.TrimSpace(string(body)) == "" {
				return fmt.Errorf("edited note body is empty; not saved")
			}
			_, err = app.Notes.Update(context.Background(), n.ID, string(body), n.Tags)
			return err
		},
	}, nil
}
EOF

435	func latestAge(at time.Time) string {
436		if at.IsZero() {
437			return "—"
438		}
439		d := time.Since(at)
440		switch {
441		case d < time.Hour:
442			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
443		case d < 24*time.Hour:
444			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
445		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
446			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
447		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
448			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
449		default:
450			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
451		}
452	}

66			CloneRemote: func(_ context.Context, rr tui.RemoteRow) (string, string, error) {
67				r.cloned = append(r.cloned, rr.Repo.FullName)
68				return "cloned", "/src/" + rr.Repo.Name, nil
69			},

71				r.started = append(r.started, "worktree:"+rr.Repo.Name+"/"+name)
72				return "started", nil
73			},
74			StartDirect: func(_ context.Context, rr tui.RepoRow, name string) (string, error) {
75				r.started = append(r.started, "direct:"+rr.Repo.Name+"/"+name)
76				return "started direct", nil
77			},
78			Open: func(_ context.Context, t *task.Task) (string, error) {
79				r.opened = append(r.opened, t.ID)
80				return "opened " + t.ID, nil
81			},
82			Park: func(_ context.Context, t *task.Task, next string) (string, error) {
83				r.parked = append(r.parked, t.ID)
84				r.nexts[t.ID] = next
85				return "parked " + t.ID, nil
86			},
87			SetNext: func(_ context.Context, t *task.Task, next string) error {
88				r.nexts[t.ID] = next

93				return nil
94			},
95		}

97	
98	// send feeds a sequence of key presses through Update, running any command the
99	// model returns so the action callbacks actually fire — that is what makes
100	// these tests exercise the real key bindings rather than the model's fields.
101	func send(m tui.Model, msgs ...tea.Msg) tui.Model {
102		var cur tea.Model = m
103		for _, msg := range msgs {
104			var cmd tea.Cmd
105			cur, cmd = cur.Update(msg)
106			// Follow the command chain, so an action's resulting message (and the
107			// reload it triggers) is applied too. Commands that do not return
108			// promptly are the cursor's blink timers; running those would make the
109			// suite sleep for half a second per keystroke.
110			for i := 0; cmd != nil && i < 8; i++ {
111				out, ok := runQuickly(cmd)
112				if !ok || out == nil {
113					break
114				}
115				if _, isBatch := out.(tea.BatchMsg); isBatch {
116					break
117				}
118				cur, cmd = cur.Update(out)
119			}
120		}
121		return cur.(tui.Model)
122	}
123	
124	// runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
125	// practice means the cursor blink timers.
126	func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
127		done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
128		go func() { done <- cmd() }()
129		select {
130		case msg := <-done:
131			return msg, true
132		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
133			return nil, false
134		}
135	}

package cli

func TestPrepareTUINoteEditUpdatesAtomicallyAfterEditor(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	service := note.NewService(note.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "notes")), filepath.Join(root, "cache", "notes.db"))
	n, err := service.Add(context.Background(), "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", "demo", "original", []string{"idea"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	editor := filepath.Join(root, "editor")
	if err := os.WriteFile(editor, []byte("#!/bin/sh\nprintf 'changed in TUI\\n' > \"$1\"\n"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Setenv("VISUAL", editor)
	app := &App{Notes: service}
	edit, err := prepareTUINoteEdit(app, n)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	runErr := edit.Command.Run()
	if err := edit.Complete(runErr); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, err := service.Get(n.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(got.Body) != "changed in TUI" || len(got.Tags) != 1 || got.Tags[0] != "idea" {
		t.Errorf("updated note = %+v", got)
	}
	if hits, _ := service.Search("changed", n.RepositoryID, 10); len(hits) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("editor completion should reindex: %+v", hits)
	}
}

func TestPrepareTUINoteEditFailureDoesNotChangeSource(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	service := note.NewService(note.NewStore(filepath.Join(root, "notes")), filepath.Join(root, "cache", "notes.db"))
	n, err := service.Add(context.Background(), "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", "demo", "original", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Setenv("VISUAL", "false")
	app := &App{Notes: service}
	edit, err := prepareTUINoteEdit(app, n)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	runErr := edit.Command.Run()
	if runErr == nil {
		t.Fatal("fixture editor should fail")
	}
	if err := edit.Complete(runErr); err == nil {
		t.Error("completion should preserve editor failure")
	}
	got, _ := service.Get(n.ID)
	if strings.TrimSpace(got.Body) != "original" {
		t.Errorf("failed editor changed source: %q", got.Body)
	}
}

# Repository quick notes

Read this when capturing, searching, editing or deleting informal repository
thoughts, or when deciding whether a thought belongs in dev, td, or beads.

## Storage boundary

Durable source:

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repository-id>/<note-id>.md
```

Search index:

```text
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
```

Markdown is authoritative. SQLite FTS is disposable and rebuilt automatically
when absent or stale. `dev cache clear notes` must never remove Markdown.

Each note is append-only by default and has a stable UUID, created/updated
timestamps, normalized tags and a Markdown body. Repo rename, symlink index,
worktree path or a second host do not change its attachment because the
repository directory key is the catalog asset ID.

## CLI workflow

```bash
dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
dev note list api
dev note search "event subscription" --repo api
dev note show <id-or-unique-prefix>
dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
dev note delete <id-or-prefix>       # confirms
dev note reindex
dev note path api
```

`add` requires text or `--editor`; it never creates an empty note. `edit` opens
a temporary body, then validates and atomically replaces the durable file only
when the editor succeeds with non-empty content. Tags survive unless `--tag`
is explicitly supplied.

Search is term-wise prefix FTS for Latin text. Non-ASCII input uses literal
term-wise matching because SQLite `unicode61` does not segment CJK substrings;
`改善` must still find `記得改善 worktree`.

## TUI workflow

On TASKS or REPOS (including a child worktree):

```text
n   quick one-line note, Enter saves, Esc cancels
N   notes overlay for the selected repository
```

On a REMOTE row, notes are enabled only when a local clone exists. In TRY,
lowercase `n` remains “new Try”; repo quick notes do not attach to Try assets.

Inside NOTES:

```text
j/k       move
/         search body, tags and repo
Enter     expand/collapse body
a or n    add
 e        edit body in VISUAL/EDITOR
d         visible delete confirmation; y confirms
N/Esc/q   return
```

The configurable REPOS column `notes` shows a count; it is not enabled by
default because the table is width-constrained. Repo/task detail always shows
count + latest preview when notes exist.

## What is not a quick note

`catalog.Entry.Note` remains the single metadata summary used by `repo mark`
and Try lifecycle. Quick notes do not overwrite it.

`td` / `beads` are structured repo-local task systems and may create dot-folders
inside a checkout. They remain optional future adapters. Do not mirror their
tasks into quick notes or initialize either tool automatically.

## Gotchas

- A note opened from a linked worktree attaches to the canonical clone by Git
  common-directory identity, not the disposable worktree path.
- Deleting `notes.db` deletes no thoughts; the next search rebuilds it.
- Deleting a Markdown file is durable deletion and requires confirmation.
- The FTS database contains full private note bodies and is mode 0600.
EOF

dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
dev note list api
dev note search "event subscription"
dev note show <id-or-prefix>
dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
```

Inside a repo, `--repo` is optional.

## TUI

```text
TASKS / REPOS:  n quick add · N browse
REMOTE:         n/N only when a local clone exists
TRY:            n remains new Try
```

Notes overlay:

```text
j/k move · / search · Enter expand · a/n add · e edit · d delete · Esc back
```

Delete opens a visible confirmation and requires `y`. Editing suspends the TUI,
opens only the Markdown body in VISUAL/EDITOR, validates non-empty content, then
atomically updates the source and FTS index.

## Where notes live

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repo-id>/<note-id>.md  durable, mode 0600
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db                            disposable FTS, mode 0600
```

Repository catalog IDs survive path moves, symlink indexes and linked worktree
paths. A note created while standing in a worktree therefore appears on the
canonical repo.

```bash
dev note path api
dev note path --all
dev note reindex
dev cache clear notes       # source Markdown remains
dev note search "query"     # rebuilds missing/stale index
```

Search is term-wise prefix FTS for Latin text, with literal term-wise fallback
for CJK substrings.

`repo mark --note` is a separate single-line catalog summary. Structured task
systems such as td/beads are separate optional future adapters; dev does not
initialize their repo dot-folders.

450	### Repository quick notes
451	
452	Quick thoughts live beside repos in dev state, not inside each checkout:
453	
454	```bash

456	dev note list api

459	dev note delete <id-or-prefix>

461	
462	In TASKS/REPOS, `n` quick-adds and `N` opens a browse/search/edit/delete overlay.
463	A REMOTE row supports notes only after it has a local clone; TRY keeps `n` for
464	creating experiments. Add `notes` to `[tui.repos].columns` for the count; detail
465	always shows count and latest preview.
466	
467	Durable Markdown lives under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-id>/`. The
468	catalog ID survives path moves, symlink indexes and linked worktrees. The
469	private `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is only an FTS index:
470	
471	```bash
472	dev cache clear notes                    # Markdown remains
473	dev note search "event"                 # index rebuilds automatically
474	dev note reindex                         # explicit rebuild
475	```
476	
477	`repo mark --note` remains a single catalog summary and is not overwritten.
478	Structured task systems such as td/beads remain optional future adapters rather
479	than creating dot-folders automatically.
480	
481	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
482	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
483	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
484	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
485	
486	```bash
487	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
488	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
489	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
490	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
491	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
492	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
493	```
494	
495	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
496	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
497	
498	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
499	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
500	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
501	Regenerable data lives separately:

505	dev cache path
506	dev cache clear remote
507	dev cache clear size
508	dev cache clear gitignore
509	dev cache clear all
510	```
511	
512	Those remove only regenerable files under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/` (remote
513	inventory, size measurements and gitignore templates) and never touch
514	`stats.db` or project data.

  reindex     Rebuild the disposable SQLite FTS index from Markdown notes
  search      Full-text search note body, tags, and repository

Submit a prompt to an agent

Usage: herdr agent prompt <TARGET> <TEXT> [OPTIONS]

Arguments:
  <TARGET>
          

  <TEXT>
          

Options:
      --wait
          Wait for the first matching state observed after submission

      --until <STATUS>
          State to match after --wait; repeat for more than one state
          
          [possible values: idle, working, blocked, done, unknown]

      --timeout <MS>
          Fail after this many milliseconds

If the agent is already blocked, submission is rejected with agent_blocked before any input is sent. When an accepted submission starts from another non-working state, --wait first requires an observed state change within 5000ms; otherwise it returns agent_prompt_stalled. A shorter --timeout returns timeout instead. It then matches idle, done, or blocked by default, or any exact --until state. It does not track turns: if the agent is already working, that active turn's completion may match. Without --timeout, the settled-state wait is indefinite.

       Markdown is the sole durable source of truth.

       containing directory after rename. Likewise sync the directory after
       deletion.

     newer changes

     - Trigger: Two processes open the same note, or another process updates it
       while an editor remains open. The later editor submits its stale body and

       body or tag changes despite mutation locking.

       holding the file lock, reject the write if the current note no longer
       matches. Report a conflict and preserve the edited temporary file for

       notes_fts table. Recovery only handles OpenIndex failures.
     - Impact: Every search/reindex continues failing against a disposable cache
       until the user manually clears it.

       or corruption errors, close the database, remove all SQLite sidecars,
       reopen, rebuild from Markdown, and retry once.

       against a note the user did not select in the current repository.

       note load messages; discard responses that do not match the active
       target/request.

     and delete the sole note

func TestStaleNoteLoadCannotPopulateNewRepositoryOverlay(t *testing.T) {
	rows := []inventory.Row{
		{Task: &task.Task{ID: "a", Name: "A task", Repo: "repo-a", RepoPath: "/src/a", Branch: "main", State: task.Hot}, CheckoutExists: true},
		{Task: &task.Task{ID: "b", Name: "B task", Repo: "repo-b", RepoPath: "/src/b", Branch: "main", State: task.Hot}, CheckoutExists: true},
	}
	aNote := sampleNote("22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", "A private thought", time.Minute)
	bNote := sampleNote("33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", "B selected thought", time.Minute)
	actions := newActions(&recorder{}, rows)
	actions.Notes.List = func(_ context.Context, target tui.NoteTarget) ([]*note.Note, error) {
		if target.Name() == "repo-a" {
			return []*note.Note{aNote}, nil
		}
		return []*note.Note{bNote}, nil
	}
	m := tui.New(actions, rows, nil)

	// Start A's async load but do not deliver its result yet.
	next, cmdA := m.Update(key("N"))
	m = next.(tui.Model)
	if cmdA == nil {
		t.Fatal("A load command missing")
	}
	// Leave A, select B, and start B's load.
	m = send(m, key("N"), key("down"))
	next, cmdB := m.Update(key("N"))
	m = next.(tui.Model)
	if cmdB == nil {
		t.Fatal("B load command missing")
	}

	// B arrives first and is accepted; delayed A arrives second and must be ignored.
	m = send(m, cmdB())
	m = send(m, cmdA())

9	
10	# dev-cli
11	
12	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
13	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
14	
15	```
16	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
17	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
18	herdr / tmux / zellij
19	                a per-host live runtime
20	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
21	```
22	
23	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
24	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
25	action** in one TOML file per task under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`; transient
26	pane data is not persisted.
27	
28	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
29	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
30	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
31	abandoning a task.
32	
33	## Check it is there first
34	
35	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
36	
37	```bash
38	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
39	dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
40	```
41	
42	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
43	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
44	hard-depend on one.
45	
46	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
47	
48	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
49	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
50	
51	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
52	|---|---|---|---|
53	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
54	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
55	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
56	
57	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
58	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
59	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
60	
61	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
62	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
63	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
64	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
65	
66	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
67	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
68	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
69	
70	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
71	
72	## The task lifecycle
73	
74	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
77	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
78	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
79	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
80	
81	```bash
82	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
83	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
84	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
85	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
86	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
87	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
88	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
89	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
90	```
91	
92	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
93	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
94	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
95	
96	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`.
97	
98	## Pick the task's checkout mode
99	
100	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
101	
102	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
103	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
104	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
105	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
106	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
107	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
108	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
109	
110	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
111	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
112	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
113	
114	## Parallel background work
115	
116	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
117	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
118	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
119	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
120	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
121	
122	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
123	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
124	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
125	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
126	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
127	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
128	
129	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
130	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
131	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
132	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.
133	
134	## Everyday commands
135	
136	```bash
137	dev                        # interactive dashboard (plain listing when piped)
138	dev note add "thought"     # append to repo containing cwd
139	dev note search "query"    # rebuilds FTS index if needed
140	dev edit                   # open the effective config; generate it first if absent
141	dev ls                     # what am I working on, everywhere
142	dev ls --json              # stable machine-readable form (also over ssh)
143	dev status                 # what is this directory: repo, branch, task, session
144	dev sweep                  # what has gone stale or drifted, and what to do
145	dev sweep --apply          # act on it, confirming each change
146	
147	dev start                  # context-aware wizard; confirms before creating
148	dev start -t "token refresh" --base main  # fast managed worktree task
149	
150	dev wt create feat/auth --base main    # worktree at the configured path
151	dev wt list                            # every worktree of this repo
152	dev wt plan                            # what a new worktree would be set up with
153	dev wt plan --write                    # seed a committed .dev.toml from it
154	dev wt rm feat/auth                    # remove the checkout; the branch stays
155	
156	dev repo list --sizes      # repos, recovery topology, owned logical bytes
157	dev repo list --no-remote  # local Git with no configured remote
158	dev repo list --local-only # branches lacking a remote-backed upstream
159	dev repo context [repo]    # agent-ready checkouts, Git, runtime and task state
160	dev repo clone owner/name  # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
161	dev repo clone https://dev.azure.com/acme/Platform/_git/api
162	dev repo sync --all        # fetch + prune, and report what moved
163	dev repo remote [query]     # search configured forge inventories
164	dev bootstrap ~/code       # recursively inventory an existing machine
165	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects   # plan a non-destructive symlink catalog
166	dev gitignore              # .gitignore from GitHub templates + the common bits
167	dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
168	
169	dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
170	dev tries mark redis-streams --add important  # durable personal metadata
171	dev tries archive redis-streams               # reversible; does not delete
172	dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
173	
174	dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
175	dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
176	dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
177	dev cache list             # regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-index caches
178	dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages
179	```
180	
181	Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
182	
183	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
184	
185	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
186	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
187	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
188	
189	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
190	`paths.scan_roots` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
191	
192	```bash
193	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
194	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
195	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
196	```
197	
198	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
199	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
200	
201	## Dashboard and forge inventory
202	
203	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, TRY and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style
204	h/l. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
205	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
206	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
207	
208	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
209	organization/project targets lazily, uses a short-lived private cache, and `/`
210	filters provider, owner/name and description. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
211	confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
212	for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query.
213	
214	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
215	
216	```toml
217	[[forge.azure_devops]]
218	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
219	project = "Platform"
220	```
221	
222	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
223	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
224	
225	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
226	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
227	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
228	expand linked worktrees; children
229	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
230	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
231	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
232	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
233	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
234	it.
235	
236	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
237	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
238	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
239	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
240	regenerable forge/size/gitignore data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
241	
242	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
243	explicitly. Runtime
244	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
245	
246	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
247	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
248	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
249	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
250	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
251	the binding should be portable across machines.
252	
253	## Repository quick notes
254	
255	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
256	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
257	
258	Quick notes are append-only Markdown under
259	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-id>/`; the catalog ID attaches them to the
260	canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and moves. SQLite FTS at
261	`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts
262	and the next search rebuilds it.
263	
264	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
265	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
266	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
267	
268	## Editing configuration
269	
270	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
271	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
272	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
273	
274	## Rules for agents
275	
276	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
277	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
278	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
279	
280	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
281	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
282	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
283	   history unattended.
284	
285	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
286	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
287	   user before overriding it.
288	
289	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
290	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
291	   for them.
292	
293	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
294	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
295	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
296	
297	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
298	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
299	   pushed.
300	
301	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
302	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
303	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
304	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
305	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
306	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
307	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
308	
309	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
310	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
311	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
312	
313	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
314	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json`. Never infer from
315	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
316	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
317	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
318	
319	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
320	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
321	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
322	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
323	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
324	
325	11. **Cleanup is explicit, never agent-state-driven.** Herdr `done` means a turn
326	    settled. Sync/stage exact artifacts first; use park/done/sweep semantics,
327	    and never auto-close from `done`.
328	
329	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
330	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
331	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
332	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
333	
334	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
335	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
336	   their judgement, not yours.
337	
338	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
339	   `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes` and
340	   reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation.
341	
342	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
343	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
344	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/size/gitignore caches.
345	
346	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
347	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
348	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
349	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
350	
351	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
352	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
353	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
354	
355	18. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
356	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
357	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
358	   does not duplicate them.
359	
360	## When to use this skill
361	
362	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
363	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
364	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
365	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
366	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
367	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
368	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
369	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
370	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
371	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
372	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
373	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
374	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
375	
376	## When NOT to use it
377	
378	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
379	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
380	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
381	  `dev start --json` cross-tool launch workflow remains here.
382	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
383	
384	## Reference files
385	
386	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
387	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
388	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
389	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
390	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
391	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
392	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
393	  work moves between machines.
394	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
395	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
396	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
397	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
398	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
399	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
400	
401	## Gotchas
402	
403	- **`dev` is a shell function, not just a binary.** Commands that move you into
404	  a checkout print a `cd` directive for the wrapper installed by
405	  `eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`. Without it they print a path and do not move
406	  you — that is not a bug.
407	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
408	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
409	  skips that and leaves you to it.
410	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
411	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
412	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
413	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
414	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
415	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
416	- **`dev done` defaults to reporting.** With neither `--ff` nor `--pr` it
417	  explains the options and changes nothing.
418	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
419	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
420

## TUI 快捷鍵

在 **TASKS / REPOS / child worktree**：

```text
n   快速新增一筆 note
N   開啟 notes overlay
```

在 **REMOTE**：

- 已有 local clone：可使用 `n` / `N`
- 尚未 clone：不允許建立 local sidecar note

在 **TRY**：

```text
n   仍然是 New Try
```

Notes overlay：

```text
j / k       上下移動
/           搜尋 body、tags、repo
Enter       展開／收起完整 note
a / n       新增 note
e           用 VISUAL / EDITOR 編輯
d           進入刪除確認
y           確認刪除
N / Esc / q 返回
```

REPOS 可選擇顯示 note count：

```toml
[tui.repos]
columns = [
  "repo",
  "branch",
  "git",
  "size",

## CLI

```bash
dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
dev note add --editor
dev note list api
dev note list --all --json
dev note search "event subscription"
dev note search "改善 worktree" --repo api
dev note show <id-or-prefix>
dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
dev note path api
dev note path --all
dev note reindex
```

ID abbreviation 最少需要 8 characters，避免空 shell variable：

```bash
dev note delete "$NOTE_ID" --yes
```

在 `$NOTE_ID=""` 時意外刪除唯一 note。

## Storage

Durable source：

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repo-id>/<note-id>.md
```

也就是預設：

```text
~/.local/share/dev/notes/<catalog-repo-id>/<note-id>.md
```

- 一 note 一檔
- TOML frontmatter + Markdown body
- mode `0600`
- UUID identity
- atomic rename
- temp file + directory fsync
- cross-process lock

搜尋 index：

```text
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
```

預設：

```text
~/.cache/dev/notes.db
```

- SQLite FTS5
- mode `0600`
- 可完全重建
- Latin term-wise prefix search
- CJK 使用 literal substring fallback

清除 index 不會刪 note：

```bash
dev cache clear notes
dev note search "query"     # 自動重建
```

若 SQLite 是 valid database、但 schema incompatible，或 database 損壞，也會自動 clear → rebuild → retry 一次。

## Catalog identity

Notes 以 catalog stable repository ID 分類，不以可變的 path 作 identity。因此：

- 從 linked worktree 新增 note，會 attach 到 canonical repo
- symlink index 不會產生另一份 notes
- repo move/rename 後仍然是同一組 notes
- 多機器 location 可共享同一 catalog asset

既有的：

```bash
dev repo mark --note "..."
```

仍是單一 catalog summary，與 append-only quick notes 分開。

## Concurrency safety

Independent QA 找到並修正：

1. crash durability：寫入成功前同步 file + directory metadata
2. stale editor：另一 process 先修改時拒絕覆寫
3. editor conflict：使用者編輯內容保留在 temporary recovery path
4. incompatible/corrupt FTS schema：自動重建
5. delayed async TUI response：加入 target key + monotonically increasing request ID
6. empty/過短 ID prefix：拒絕解析

因此快速切換 repo A → B 時，A 延遲回來的 notes 不會污染 B overlay，也無法對錯誤 repo 做 edit/delete。

```text
Git remote      durable code state
Git branch      change-stream identity
Git worktree    disposable filesystem isolation

Important workflow policy:

```text
Worktree per independent change stream.
Pane per agent.
Not one worktree per agent.

Task lifecycle:

```text
HOT   worktree/checkout + live runtime
WARM  checkout retained, runtime closed
COLD  committed/pushed, disposable worktree removed
DONE  integrated

2. Key Technical Concepts

Languages/frameworks/libraries:

- Go
- Cobra
- Bubble Tea
- Bubbles textinput
- Lipgloss
- BurntSushi TOML
- modernc.org/sqlite
- FTS5
- Google UUID

External tools/backends:

- Git

- tmux
- zellij
- GitHub CLI (`gh`)
- GitLab CLI (`glab`)
- Azure DevOps CLI integration from later main changes
- lazygit
- yazi
- nvim/editor
- WakaTime

Storage model:

```text
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/*.toml
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/assets/*.toml
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db
$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-id>/<note-id>.md

$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/remotes.json
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/sizes-v1.json
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/gitignore/
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
```

Important distinction:

- `stats.db` is durable activity data, not cache.
- Note Markdown is durable source of truth.
- `notes.db` is disposable FTS cache.
- `dev cache clear notes` must never delete Markdown.

Repository identity:

- Catalog stable UUID.
- Same clone matched by host + canonical path + Git common-dir.
- Remote identity is only a conservative relocation hint.
- A note created from a linked worktree attaches to the canonical clone.

Note file format implemented:

```text
+++
schema_version = 1
id = "<note-uuid>"
repository_id = "<catalog-uuid>"
repository = "dev-cli"
created = 2026-08-28T...
updated = 2026-08-28T...
tags = ["idea", "git"]
+++

Try replacing the polling loop with an event subscription.
```

Note concurrency/durability:

- Per-store process mutex.
- Cross-process file lock:
  - `unix.Flock` on Unix.
  - `windows.LockFileEx` on Windows.
- Temporary file + `Sync()` + atomic rename.
- Directory sync after rename/delete on Unix.
- Mode 0600 for note files and FTS database.
- Optimistic `Note.Revision()` fingerprint checked while holding mutation lock.
- Stale editor updates rejected with `ErrConflict`.
- Edited temp body retained and recovery path reported on conflict.

SQLite FTS:

- FTS5 table over repository, tags and body.
- Manifest uses full content revision/fingerprint, not only timestamp.
- Missing/stale/corrupt/incompatible index is cleared and rebuilt from Markdown.
- Latin search: term-wise prefix FTS.
- CJK/non-ASCII: term-wise literal substring fallback because unicode61 does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings.
- Valid SQLite with incompatible `notes_fts` schema is detected and rebuilt.
- Schema uses `PRAGMA user_version`.

TUI notes:

- `n`: quick one-line add.
- `N`: notes browser.
- `/`: note search.
- Enter: expand/collapse body.
- `a` or `n`: add from overlay.
- `e`: edit body via external editor.
- `d`: enter delete confirmation.
- `y`: confirm delete.
- Stale async note loads carry:
  - target key
  - monotonically increasing request generation
- Delayed results for repo A are discarded after switching to repo B.

```text
1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.
6	
7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and the TUI consume this joined view.
59	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
60	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
61	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage` and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
62	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
63	
64	The principal task flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Lifecycle behavior lives in `park.go`, `resume.go`, `done.go`, and `sweep.go`; preserve their report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering.
65	
66	State is split intentionally:
67	
68	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
69	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
70	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
71	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
72	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
73	
74	## Behavioral contracts
75	
76	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`.
77	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
78	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
79	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
80	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews.
81	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
82	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
83	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
84	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
85	
86	## Versioning and changelog
87	
88	The current published baseline is `v0.1.0` (2026-08-28). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
89	
90	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`.
91	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
92	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
93	
94	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a post-`v0.1.0` feature build as `v0.1.0`; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version (normally the next minor during `0.x`, while compatible fixes normally increment patch). Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
95	
96	For a release:
97	
98	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
99	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
100	3. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag.
101	4. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, and create the GitHub release.
102	
103	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
104	
105	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
106	
107	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
108	
109	| Change | Required synchronization |
110	|---|---|
111	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
112	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
113	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
114	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
115	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
116	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
117	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
118	
119	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
120	
121	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
122
```
</details></tool-use>

79	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
80	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews.
81	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
82	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
83	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
84	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
85	
86	## Versioning and changelog
87	
88	The current published baseline is `v0.1.0` (2026-08-28). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
89	
90	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`.
91	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
92	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
93	
94	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a post-`v0.1.0` feature build as `v0.1.0`; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version (normally the next minor during `0.x`, while compatible fixes normally increment patch). Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
95	
96	For a release:
97	
98	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
99	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
100	3. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag.
101	4. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, and create the GitHub release.
102	
103	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
104	
105	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
106	
107	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
108	
109	| Change | Required synchronization |
110	|---|---|
111	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
112	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
113	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
114	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
115	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
116	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
117	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
118	
119	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
120	
121	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
122
```
