<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `/Users/david/.herdr/worktrees/dev-cli/feat-repo-quick-notes/README.md`

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux / zellij
11	                a per-host live runtime
12	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
13	```
14	
15	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
16	only human intent Git cannot answer: task **state/owner/next action**, plus
17	stable asset identity, personal tags/notes and experiment lifecycle. Live Git
18	status stays live; logical size measurements are explicitly disposable cache.
19	
20	## The problem
21	
22	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
23	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
24	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
25	defeats the point of having one.
26	
27	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
28	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
29	
30	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
31	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
32	expected.
33	
34	```
35	$ dev ls
36	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
37	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
38	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
39	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
40	```
41	
42	## Install
43	
44	### Homebrew (macOS)
45	
46	```bash
47	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
48	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
49	```
50	
51	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
52	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
53	
54	### Go or source
55	
56	```bash
57	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
58	# Pin @v0.1.0 instead when you need a reproducible install.
59	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
60	```
61	
62	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
63	them:
64	
65	```bash
66	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
67	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
68	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
69	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
70	```
71	
72	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
73	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
74	a forge or the network.
75	
76	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
77	
78	```bash
79	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
80	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
81	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
82	```
83	
84	A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
85	passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
86	while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
87	the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
88	
89	The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
90	
91	```bash
92	dev skill install
93	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
94	```
95	
96	Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
97	Azure CLI each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
98	
99	## The lifecycle
100	
101	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
102	|---|---|---|---|
103	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
104	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
105	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
106	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
107	
108	```bash
109	dev start                                           # interactive managed-task wizard
110	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # non-interactive fast path → hot
111	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
112	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
113	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
114	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated + cleaned
115	dev done --pr                                      # open review; keep task/worktree
116	dev sweep                                          # report what has gone stale
117	```
118	
119	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
120	
121	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
122	
123	```bash
124	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
125	dev repo open api
126	
127	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
128	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
129	
130	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
131	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
132	
133	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
134	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
135	```
136	
137	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
138	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
139	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
140	
141	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
142	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
143	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
144	the parallel task depends on them.
145	
146	For automation, `dev start … --json` emits one pure creation object with absolute
147	paths and transient runtime facts. Only a newly created first-class Herdr
148	worktree with a non-empty exact `root_pane_id` is a launch target; reuse,
149	fallback, Tmux, none, or missing pane data fails closed. Worktree starts use the
150	same `repo/branch` label as `dev wt create` and pins the Git-derived parent
151	checkout with Herdr `--cwd`, preserving native nested repository/worktree
152	grouping without separate provenance metadata.
153	
154	Herdr-aware writer claims—`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
155	`resume`—reject another recognized agent in the same canonical Git worktree.
156	Every state, including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied. Pure
157	`repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter reuse/focus the live owner without
158	claiming another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is only for explicitly
159	coordinated disjoint ownership; normal new-worktree creation remains allowed.
160	
161	Task runtime handles carry their backend name and are validated against live
162	checkout coverage before reuse or close. Stale handles reopen on resume; a
163	verified close failure stops cold/done/worktree removal before deleting a
164	checkout that may still host the runtime.
165	
166	### The dashboard
167	
168	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens four lists, switched with `tab`:
169	
170	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
171	- **REPOS** — durable repositories under the scan roots, with branch, dirty
172	  state, owned size, runtime, worktrees and task tally. What do I have here.
173	- **TRY** — dated scratch experiments, including non-Git folders, with durable
174	  tags/notes and explicit active/deprecated/archived/graduated state.
175	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through authenticated forge CLIs, including
176	  configured Azure DevOps projects, marked when a local repo or Try exists.
177	  What can I open or clone.
178	
179	TASKS, REPOS and TRY use the same services as their non-interactive commands.
180	Git-backed Tries appear in TRY rather than being duplicated in REPOS; REMOTE
181	still knows that local checkout exists. The repo list matters on day one: with
182	forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just
183	be empty.
184	
185	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
186	
187	```
188	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
189	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
190	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
191	```
192	
193	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. Inside Herdr/tmux/Zellij it
194	switches the current client; outside it exits the dashboard and attaches to
195	the target session. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
196	for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
197	`space` expands linked worktrees inline, `m` edits repository tags/notes, `s`
198	starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task.
199	Expanded children carry their own Git/session/task state and can be opened
200	directly. In TRY, `n` creates or clones an experiment;
201	`space` opens mark/deprecate/archive/restore/graduate actions; `a` includes
202	retained history. `?` opens the complete context-sensitive key map. That makes
203	the branch/worktree and lifecycle costs explicit rather than silently applying
204	them to every directory.
205	
206	REPOS also has an agent-handoff copy menu. Press `y`, then `y` for contextual
207	Markdown, `p` for the checkout path, `b` for the branch, `s` for runtime/agent
208	sessions, or `w` for every linked-worktree path. Parent `yy` includes the whole
209	repo; child `yy` includes only that worktree. The same full context is
210	pipe-friendly outside the TUI:
211	
212	```bash
213	dev repo context api
214	dev repo context          # current repo, even from inside a linked worktree
215	```
216	
217	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
218	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
219	
220	```toml
221	[[tui.tools]]
222	key  = "L"
223	name = "lazygit"
224	run  = "lazygit"
225	
226	[[tui.tools]]
227	key  = "V"
228	name = "nvim"
229	run  = "nvim ."
230	
231	[[tui.tools]]
232	key  = "B"
233	name = "vibe"
234	run  = "vibe"
235	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
236	
237	[[tui.tools]]
238	key  = "P"
239	name = "plans here"
240	run  = "claude-plans-here"
241	interactive = true
242	```
243	
244	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
245	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
246	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
247	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
248	
249	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
250	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes all configured
251	forge providers.
252	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
253	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
254	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
255	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
256	
257	Azure DevOps Services inventory is opt-in because `az repos list` requires an
258	organization and team project. Repeat the target for every project wanted:
259	
260	```toml
261	[[forge.azure_devops]]
262	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
263	project = "Platform"
264	```
265	
266	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension and authenticate with Azure CLI.
267	`dev` does not install extensions, change Azure defaults or store credentials.
268	Azure DevOps Server/on-premises is not supported by the official extension.
269	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …). Multiple
270	repo sessions collapse to `herdr:N live`; expanding the repo reveals each
271	checkout and whether its session is live or closed. External and turn-scoped
272	agent worktrees remain visible with `(external)` / `(ephemeral)` labels, so the
273	tree always reconciles with WT. `H` opens the selected repo's
274	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or
275	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
276	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
277	
278	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
279	task update, plus asynchronous `SIZE`. Size is portable logical bytes:
280	
281	- `checkout_bytes` excludes only the checkout root's `.git` entry.
282	- `private_git_bytes` belongs only to this checkout and is included in
283	  `owned_bytes`, the table value.
284	- `shared_git_bytes` is shown separately and never charged to every linked
285	  worktree. `+S` means shared Git storage exists but is not reclaimable with
286	  that row.
287	
288	Measurements stream in after the first frame, use a 10-minute private XDG cache,
289	and can be forced with `r`; unreadable subtrees display a lower bound (`≥`).
290	Columns and default ordering are config:
291	
292	```toml
293	[tui.repos]
294	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "size", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
295	sort = "activity"       # activity | latest | name | git | size | tasks
296	reverse = false
297	```
298	
299	In REPOS and TRY, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. Structured filters include
300	`tag:important`, `remote:none`, `size:>1GiB`, `phase:deprecated` and
301	`where:archived` where applicable. Local repo probes run with bounded
302	parallelism, and the alternate screen appears before they finish.
303	
304	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
305	
306	### Experiments and local-data risk
307	
308	`dev try <name>` keeps its low-friction positional grammar. Lifecycle management
309	uses the separate plural group, so `dev try archive` still means "open/create a
310	Try named archive":
311	
312	```bash
313	dev tries list --json                 # active, present Tries
314	dev tries list --all --sizes          # include deprecated/archived history
315	dev tries mark redis --add important --note "compare streams"
316	dev tries deprecate redis             # intent only; files do not move
317	dev tries archive redis               # reversible move under tries_root/.dev
318	dev tries restore redis
319	dev tries graduate redis -c Infra     # same service as dev graduate
320	```
321	
322	Archive is organization, **not disk reclamation**: it moves the directory to a
323	hidden location on the same filesystem and preserves its stable catalog ID.
324	Phase 1 deliberately has no `evict`, recursive delete, or automatic remote
325	backup. Safe local removal needs repo-wide ref verification and remains a
326	follow-up rather than treating "has a remote" as proof.
327	
328	The catalog also exposes personal repository tags/notes (`dev repo mark`). To
329	find local Git state at risk before any future cleanup:
330	
331	```bash
332	dev repo list --no-remote              # no configured remotes at all
333	dev repo list --local-only             # at least one branch lacks remote upstream
334	dev repo list --multiple-remotes
335	dev repo list --multiple-upstreams     # branches track more than one remote
336	dev repo list --sizes --json           # full remotes/branches/size contract
337	```
338	
339	`no remote`, `local-only branch`, and `multiple upstreams` are distinct facts.
340	They do not claim whether commit objects are present remotely; a future reclaim
341	preflight must compare every local head/tag/note/stash against actual remote
342	refs immediately before removal.
343	
344	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
345	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
346	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
347	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
348	
349	## Rich Git state
350	
351	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
352	
353	```text
354	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
355	```
356	
357	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
358	- `=` — conflicted paths
359	- `+` — staged paths
360	- `!` — unstaged paths
361	- `?` — untracked paths
362	
363	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
364	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
365	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
366	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
367	
368	## Worktree ownership
369	
370	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
371	to improvise:
372	
373	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
374	|---|---|---|---|
375	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
376	| Harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | owned by that harness; no history-relocation guarantee |
377	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
378	
379	**If code, history, or plans must remain reviewable—or you may return tomorrow—
380	use `dev`.**
381	
382	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
383	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
384	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
385	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
386	
387	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
388	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
389	copy of the tree.
390	
391	### Provisioning
392	
393	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
394	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
395	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
396	command detected from the lockfiles. Included files must remain the same
397	regular file through open; source swaps and symlinked destination parents are
398	refused, existing destinations are reported as skipped, and contents are never
399	logged:
400	
401	```toml
402	[worktree]
403	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
404	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
405	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
406	```
407	
408	`.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal include. Add that exact path
409	only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude launcher and verify it
410	arrives. `claude-copilot-once` preserves an existing Copilot pin and creates/
411	removes only one it added when absent; its proxy must already run.
412	`codex-copilot-once` injects backend via CLI and may auto-start its proxy path,
413	so neither wrapper needs the copied file.
414	
415	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
416	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
417	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
418	
419	```toml
420	[worktree]
421	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
422	
423	[worktree.strategies]
424	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
425	```
426	
427	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
428	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
429	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
430	
431	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
432	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
433	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
434	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
435	
436	```
437	$ dev wt plan
438	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
439	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
440	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
441	
442	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
443	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
444	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
445	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
446	```
447	
448	## Other things it does
449	
450	```bash
451	dev repo list --sizes          # repos, remote topology and owned logical size
452	dev repo list --no-remote      # find local Git with no configured backup remote
453	dev repo context api           # agent-ready paths, Git, WT, runtime and tasks
454	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
455	dev repo clone https://dev.azure.com/acme/Platform/_git/api -c Work
456	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
457	
458	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
459	dev tries archive redis-streams    # reversible local archive; does not delete
460	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
461	
462	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
463	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
464	
465	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
466	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
467	```
468	
469	### Repository quick notes
470	
471	Quick thoughts live beside repos in dev state, not inside each checkout:
472	
473	```bash
474	dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
475	dev note list api
476	dev note search "event subscription"
477	dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
478	dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
479	```
480	
481	In TASKS/REPOS, `n` quick-adds and `N` opens a browse/search/edit/delete overlay.
482	A REMOTE row supports notes only after it has a local clone; TRY keeps `n` for
483	creating experiments. Add `notes` to `[tui.repos].columns` for the count; detail
484	always shows count and latest preview.
485	
486	Durable Markdown lives under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-id>/`. The
487	catalog ID survives path moves, symlink indexes and linked worktrees. The
488	private `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is only an FTS index:
489	
490	```bash
491	dev cache clear notes                    # Markdown remains
492	dev note search "event"                 # index rebuilds automatically
493	dev note reindex                         # explicit rebuild
494	```
495	
496	`repo mark --note` remains a single catalog summary and is not overwritten.
497	Structured task systems such as td/beads remain optional future adapters rather
498	than creating dot-folders automatically.
499	
500	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
501	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
502	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
503	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
504	
505	```bash
506	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
507	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
508	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
509	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
510	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
511	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
512	```
513	
514	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
515	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
516	
517	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
518	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
519	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
520	Regenerable data lives separately:
521	
522	```bash
523	dev cache list
524	dev cache path
525	dev cache clear remote
526	dev cache clear notes          # FTS only; Markdown remains
527	dev cache clear size
528	dev cache clear gitignore
529	dev cache clear all
530	```
531	
532	Those remove only regenerable files under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/` (remote
533	inventory, note FTS, size measurements and gitignore templates) and never touch
534	`stats.db`, durable note Markdown or project data.
535	
536	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
537	
538	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
539	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
540	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
541	explicit path:
542	
543	```bash
544	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
545	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
546	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
547	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
548	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
549	```
550	
551	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
552	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
553	path.
554	
555	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
556	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
557	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
558	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
559	paths.
560	
561	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
562	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
563	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
564	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
565	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
566	
567	## Adopting work in flight
568	
569	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
570	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
571	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
572	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
573	and writes only the ones that exist:
574	
575	```
576	$ dev config init
577	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
578	
579	Detected:
580	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
581	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
582	~/src                16     scan root
583	```
584	
585	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
586	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
587	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
588	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
589	up itself:
590	
591	```bash
592	dev adopt            # report only
593	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
594	```
595	
596	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
597	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
598	`dev help adopting`.
599	
600	## .gitignore
601	
602	```bash
603	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
604	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
605	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
606	```
607	
608	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
609	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
610	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and
611	ephemeral coding-agent state such as linked worktrees and local settings.
612	Review artifacts such as SpecStory histories and agent plans remain trackable
613	unless you add your own ignore rule for them.
614	
615	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
616	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
617	
618	## Configuration
619	
620	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
621	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
622	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
623	
624	```bash
625	dev edit
626	dev config edit
627	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
628	```
629	
630	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
631	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
632	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
633	
634	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
635	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
636	
637	```toml
638	[paths]
639	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
640	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
641	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
642	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
643	```
644	
645	`state_dir/tasks/*.toml` stores task intent; `state_dir/assets/*.toml` stores
646	stable repository/Try identity, tags/notes, experiment lifecycle and per-host
647	locations. Git status and byte counts are not copied there. The latter lives in
648	`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/sizes-v1.json` and is safe to delete.
649	
650	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
651	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
652	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
653	named `{{rep}}`.
654	
655	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
656	special mode:
657	
658	```toml
659	[paths]
660	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
661	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
662	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
663	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
664	```
665	
666	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
667	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
668	
669	## Multiple machines
670	
671	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
672	the handoff boundary:
673	
674	```bash
675	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
676	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
677	```
678	
679	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
680	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
681	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
682	
683	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
684	
685	```bash
686	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
687	```
688	
689	## The agent skill
690	
691	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
692	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
693	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
694	reading none.
695	
696	```bash
697	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
698	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
699	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
700	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
701	```
702	
703	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
704	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
705	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
706	responsibility.
707	
708	## Development
709	
710	```bash
711	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
712	make test
713	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
714	make skill-check
715	```
716	
717	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
718	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
719	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
720	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
721
```

1	# TUI navigation
2	
3	Bare `dev` opens the dashboard when stdin/stdout are terminals; `dev tui`
4	opens it explicitly. When piped, bare `dev` prints `dev ls` instead, so shell
5	composition stays predictable.
6	
7	## Four views
8	
9	Switch with `tab`, `l`/`h`, or right/left:
10	
11	| View | Answers | Data source |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry + live Git/runtime state |
14	| REPOS | What durable repositories exist here? | configured scan roots + asset catalog |
15	| TRY | Which experiments can I resume, archive or graduate? | experiment catalog + live Git/runtime state |
16	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated forge CLI inventories |
17	
18	REPOS shows branch, dirty state, owned logical size, linked-worktree count and
19	HOT/WARM/COLD task tallies. Press `space` to expand a repo into its linked
20	worktrees; each child has its own Git, runtime and task state, and enter opens
21	that checkout. Git-backed Tries are shown in TRY rather than appearing twice;
22	REMOTE still labels their local checkout as `try`. Repos with active work sort
23	first. On a first run with no tasks, switch to REPOS and press `s`, or use TRY
24	`n` for a low-cost experiment.
25	
26	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A
27	private XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes explicitly. It
28	marks remotes already cloned under `scan_roots`. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
29	asks before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`.
30	
31	GitHub and GitLab are discovered from authenticated `gh` and `glab` CLIs.
32	Azure DevOps Services inventory is opt-in because each query needs an explicit
33	organization and team project:
34	
35	```toml
36	[[forge.azure_devops]]
37	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
38	project = "Platform"
39	```
40	
41	Repeat the table for additional projects. Azure CLI and its `azure-devops`
42	extension must already be installed and authenticated; dev does not install the
43	extension, change Azure defaults, or store credentials.
44	
45	## Vim-style movement
46	
47	```
48	j / k                next / previous
49	ctrl+d / ctrl+u      half page down / up
50	g / G                top / bottom
51	h / l, shift-tab/tab previous / next view
52	/                    filter as you type

61	applicable. `gitlab auth` still finds a GitLab repo whose name/description also

101	shared Git objects are shown in detail and never charged to every worktree. The
102	detail pane also calls out `no remote`, local-only branches and multiple

105	`y` opens a second-key copy menu:
106

108	yy  agent-ready Markdown context (whole repo on parent; one checkout on child)
109	yp  selected checkout's absolute path
110	yb  selected branch
111	ys  runtime handles and agent session IDs (parent or child scope)
112	yw  every linked-worktree path in the repo, one per line
113	```

115	The same full Markdown is available without a clipboard or TUI through

119	TRY:

123	n          create/clone a Try (name, optional clone ref, git yes/no)
124	space      mark, deprecate/reactivate, archive/restore, or graduate

144

153	An empty heatmap is actionable: press `b` to derive only the selected repo's

204	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's

206	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.

5	
6	# dev-cli
7	
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10	
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux / zellij
15	                a per-host live runtime
16	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
17	```
18	
19	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
20	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
21	action** in one TOML file per task under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`; transient
22	pane data is not persisted.
23	
24	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
25	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
26	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
27	abandoning a task.
28	
29	## Check it is there first
30	
31	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
32	
33	```bash
34	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
35	dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
36	```
37	
38	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
39	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
40	hard-depend on one.
41	
42	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
43	
44	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
45	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
46	
47	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
50	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
51	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
52	
53	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
54	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
55	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
56	
57	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
58	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
59	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
60	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
61	
62	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
63	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
64	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
65	
66	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## The task lifecycle
69	
70	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
73	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
74	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
75	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
76	
77	```bash
78	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
79	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
80	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
81	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
82	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
83	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
84	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
85	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
86	```
87	
88	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
89	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
90	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
91	
92	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`.
93	
94	## Pick the task's checkout mode
95	
96	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
97	
98	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
99	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
100	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
101	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
102	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
103	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
104	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
105	
106	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
107	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
108	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
109	
110	## Parallel background work
111	
112	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
113	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
114	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
115	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
116	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
117	
118	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
119	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
120	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
121	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
122	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
123	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
124	
125	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
126	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
127	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
128	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.

179	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
180	
181	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
182	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
183	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
184	
185	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through

188	```bash

190	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
191	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)

193	
194	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
195	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.

199	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, TRY and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style

249	## Repository quick notes
250	
251	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
252	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
253	
254	Quick notes are append-only Markdown under

257	`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts

259	
260	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
261	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
262	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
263	
264	## Editing configuration
265	
266	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
267	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
268	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
269	
270	## Rules for agents
271	
272	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
273	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
274	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
275	
276	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
277	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
278	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
279	   history unattended.
280	
281	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
282	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
283	   user before overriding it.
284	
285	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
286	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
287	   for them.
288	
289	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
290	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
291	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
292	
293	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
294	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
295	   pushed.
296	
297	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
298	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
299	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
300	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
301	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
302	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
303	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
304	
305	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
306	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
307	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
308	
309	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
310	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json`. Never infer from
311	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
312	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
313	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
314	
315	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
316	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
317	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
318	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
319	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
320	
321	11. **Cleanup is explicit, never agent-state-driven.** Herdr `done` means a turn
322	    settled. Sync/stage exact artifacts first; use park/done/sweep semantics,
323	    and never auto-close from `done`.
324	
325	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
326	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
327	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
328	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
329	
330	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
331	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
332	   their judgement, not yours.
333	
334	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
335	   `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes` and
336	   reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation.
337	
338	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
339	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
340	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/size/gitignore caches.
341	
342	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
343	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
344	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
345	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
346	
347	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
348	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
349	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
350	
351	18. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
352	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
353	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
354	   does not duplicate them.
355	
356	## When to use this skill
357	
358	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
359	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
360	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
361	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
362	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
363	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
364	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
365	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
366	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
367	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
368	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
369	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
370	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
371	
372	## When NOT to use it
373	
374	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
375	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
376	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
377	  `dev start --json` cross-tool launch workflow remains here.
378	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
379	
380	## Reference files
381	
382	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
383	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
384	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
385	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
386	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
387	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
388	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
389	  work moves between machines.
390	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
391	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
392	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
393	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
394	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
395	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
396	
397	## Gotchas
398	
399	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
400	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private child-only
401	  file descriptor, reads one NUL-terminated path and calls `builtin cd` without
402	  evaluating command output. Without the wrapper, the binary's printable legacy
403	  directive cannot change the parent shell — that is not a bug.
404	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
405	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
406	  skips that and leaves you to it.
407	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
408	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
409	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
410	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
411	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
412	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
413	- **`dev done` defaults to reporting.** With neither `--ff` nor `--pr` it
414	  explains the options and changes nothing.
415	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
416	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
417
```

```text
1	# Repository quick notes
2	
3	Read this when capturing, searching, editing or deleting informal repository
4	thoughts, or when deciding whether a thought belongs in dev, td, or beads.
5	
6	## Storage boundary
7	
8	Durable source:
9	
10	```text
11	$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repository-id>/<note-id>.md
12	```
13	
14	Search index:
15	
16	```text
17	$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
18	```
19	
20	Markdown is authoritative. SQLite FTS is disposable and rebuilt automatically
21	when absent or stale. `dev cache clear notes` must never remove Markdown.
22	
23	Each note is append-only by default and has a stable UUID, created/updated
24	timestamps, normalized tags and a Markdown body. Repo rename, symlink index,
25	worktree path or a second host do not change its attachment because the
26	repository directory key is the catalog asset ID.
27	
28	## CLI workflow
29	
30	```bash
31	dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
32	dev note list api
33	dev note search "event subscription" --repo api
34	dev note show <id-or-unique-prefix>
35	dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
36	dev note delete <id-or-prefix>       # confirms
37	dev note reindex
38	dev note path api
39	```
40	
41	`add` requires text or `--editor`; it never creates an empty note. `edit` opens
42	a temporary body, then validates and atomically replaces the durable file only
43	when the editor succeeds with non-empty content. Tags survive unless `--tag`
44	is explicitly supplied. Edit uses an optimistic content revision under the
45	mutation lock; if another process won first, the stale edit is rejected and its
46	temporary body path is reported for manual recovery.
47	
48	Search is term-wise prefix FTS for Latin text. Non-ASCII input uses literal
49	term-wise matching because SQLite `unicode61` does not segment CJK substrings;
50	`改善` must still find `記得改善 worktree`.
51	
52	## TUI workflow
53	
54	On TASKS or REPOS (including a child worktree):
55	
56	```text
57	n   quick one-line note, Enter saves, Esc cancels
58	N   notes overlay for the selected repository
59	```
60	
61	On a REMOTE row, notes are enabled only when a local clone exists. In TRY,
62	lowercase `n` remains “new Try”; repo quick notes do not attach to Try assets.
63	
64	Inside NOTES:
65	
66	```text
67	j/k       move
68	/         search body, tags and repo
69	Enter     expand/collapse body
70	a or n    add
71	 e        edit body in VISUAL/EDITOR
72	d         visible delete confirmation; y confirms
73	N/Esc/q   return
74	```
75	
76	The configurable REPOS column `notes` shows a count; it is not enabled by
77	default because the table is width-constrained. Repo/task detail always shows
78	count + latest preview when notes exist.
79	
80	## What is not a quick note
81	
82	`catalog.Entry.Note` remains the single metadata summary used by `repo mark`
83	and Try lifecycle. Quick notes do not overwrite it.
84	
85	`td` / `beads` are structured repo-local task systems and may create dot-folders
86	inside a checkout. They remain optional future adapters. Do not mirror their
87	tasks into quick notes or initialize either tool automatically.
88	
89	## Gotchas
90	
91	- A note opened from a linked worktree attaches to the canonical clone by Git
92	  common-directory identity, not the disposable worktree path.
93	- Delayed TUI load results carry target ID + request generation and are ignored
94	  after switching repositories; never remove that guard from `noteListMsg`.
95	- Deleting `notes.db` deletes no thoughts; the next search rebuilds it.
96	- Deleting a Markdown file is durable deletion and requires confirmation.
97	- The FTS database contains full private note bodies and is mode 0600.
98
```

    feat: add catalog-backed repository quick notes
    
    Store append-only repository thoughts as private Markdown files keyed by stable
    catalog asset IDs, so notes survive worktrees, symlink indexes, moves, and
    cross-host locations without adding dot-folders to repositories. Build a
    private disposable SQLite FTS index with CJK fallback, content fingerprints,
    schema validation, automatic corruption recovery, and explicit cache clearing.
    
    Add complete note CLI CRUD/search/path/reindex commands. Protect edits with
    optimistic revisions and cross-process locks, fsync successful mutations, keep
    stale editor bodies for recovery, and require safe ID prefixes plus confirmed
    deletion.
    
    Add TUI n quick-add and N notes overlay for tasks, repositories, child
    worktrees, and cloned remotes. Support browse, search, expand, editor, and
    confirmed delete; expose optional note counts and latest previews. Guard async
    loads with target identities and request generations so delayed results cannot
    cross repositories.
    
    Update cache/storage boundaries, docs, embedded skill, generated commands, and
    end-to-end coverage.

```text
1	---
2	description: Understand dev-cli as durable Git history, a small intent registry, disposable worktrees, and replaceable runtimes.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-28
6	---
7	
8	# Mental model and lifecycle
9	
10	`dev` treats a unit of work as a **change stream** whose durable identity is its Git branch. The checkout and runtime are replaceable projections of that stream.
11	
12	## Four responsibilities
13	
14	```text
15	Git remote + branch  durable history and cross-machine handoff
16	        ↓
17	worktree             local files, index, and checked-out HEAD
18	        ↓
19	runtime              Herdr workspace, tmux session, or current shell
20	        ↓
21	dev registry         human intent and reconstruction metadata
22	```
23	
24	The registry stores facts needed to act later: repository and branch identity, base, checkout path, lifecycle state, owner host, next action, notes/tags, runtime handle, optional agent session, and timestamps. Live Git status, ahead/behind, and runtime availability are derived again instead of treated as authoritative cached truth.
25	
26	## The four lifecycle states
27	
28	| State | Git and checkout | Runtime | Meaning |
29	|---|---|---|---|
30	| 🔥 `hot` | branch plus checkout | open | active now |
31	| 🌤 `warm` | branch plus checkout kept | closed | likely to return within days |
32	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed branch; worktree absent | none | paused and reconstructible elsewhere |
33	| ✅ `done` | integrated | none | retained until cleanup reaps the entry |
34	
35	```text
36	              dev start
37	                  │
38	                  ▼
39	               HOT ───── dev done --ff ─────► DONE
40	                │ ▲
41	       dev park │ │ dev resume
42	                ▼ │
43	               WARM
44	                │ ▲
45	 --cold --push  │ │ dev resume --fetch
46	                ▼ │
47	               COLD
48	```
49	
50	`dev done --pr` is intentionally not the HOT → DONE transition. It publishes the branch for review and leaves state and cleanup unchanged until integration is known.
51	
52	## Checkout modes
53	
54	A task records intent; it does not always require a linked worktree.
55	
56	| Mode | Use | Lifecycle limit |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| direct | one small change in the canonical checkout | HOT ↔ WARM; canonical checkout cannot be removed |
59	| branch-only | isolated history without a second directory | can go COLD after push and switching the canonical checkout away |
60	| worktree | independent mutation, parallel streams, durable feature work | full lifecycle |
61	
62	The mode is selected by collision and recovery needs, not by ceremony.
63	
64	## Runtime is deliberately lossy
65	
66	`runtime.Runtime` exposes `Open`, `Close`, `List`, and `Annotate`. `auto` selects Herdr when available, then tmux, then Zellij, then the always-available `none` backend. Closing any backend must not remove the checkout, branch, or task entry.
67	
68	This separation is why rebooting, closing a multiplexer, or changing runtime backend does not abandon work. `dev sweep` can compare the registry with live Git/runtime facts and report drift.
69	
70	## Cross-machine handoff
71	
72	The branch is the transport boundary:
73	
74	```bash
75	# machine A
76	dev park --cold --push
77	
78	# machine B
79	dev resume <task> --fetch
80	```
81	
82	One writer owns a branch at a time. If two machines or agents need to mutate the same feature concurrently, split the change stream and integrate afterwards.
83	
84	## Sources
85	
86	- [`internal/task/task.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/task/task.go)
87	- [`internal/runtime/runtime.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/runtime.go)
88	- [`internal/help/topics/parking.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/help/topics/parking.md)
89	- [`internal/cli/done.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/done.go)
90	- [`internal/cli/sweep.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/sweep.go)
91

1	---
2	description: 以持久 Git history、小型 intent registry、可丟棄 worktree 與可替換 runtime 理解 dev-cli。
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-28

8	
9	# 心智模型與生命週期
10	
11	!!! note "術語規則"
12	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
13	
14	`dev` 把一個工作單位視為變更流 (change stream)，而它的持久身分是 Git branch。Checkout 與執行環境 (runtime) 都只是可替換的投影。
15	
16	## 四種責任
17	
18	```text
19	Git remote + branch  持久 history 與跨機器 handoff
20	        ↓
21	worktree             本機 files、index 與 checked-out HEAD
22	        ↓
23	runtime              Herdr workspace、tmux session 或目前 shell
24	        ↓
25	dev registry         人類意圖與重建 metadata
26	```
27	
28	Registry 保存未來要能採取行動的資訊：repository 與 branch identity、base、checkout path、lifecycle state、owner host、next action、notes/tags、runtime handle、可選 agent session 與 timestamps。即時 Git status、ahead/behind 與 runtime availability 會重新推導，不會被當成權威 cache。
29	
30	## 四個 lifecycle state
31	
32	| State | Git 與 checkout | Runtime | 意義 |
33	|---|---|---|---|
34	| 🔥 `hot` | branch 加 checkout | 開啟 | 正在處理 |
35	| 🌤 `warm` | 保留 branch 與 checkout | 關閉 | 幾天內會回來 |
36	| ❄️ `cold` | branch 已 commit、push；worktree 不存在 | 無 | 已暫停，可在別處重建 |
37	| ✅ `done` | 已整合 | 無 | 等待 cleanup 回收 entry |
38	
39	```text
40	              dev start
41	                  │
42	                  ▼
43	               HOT ───── dev done --ff ─────► DONE
44	                │ ▲
45	       dev park │ │ dev resume
46	                ▼ │
47	               WARM
48	                │ ▲
49	 --cold --push  │ │ dev resume --fetch
50	                ▼ │
51	               COLD
52	```
53	
54	`dev done --pr` 刻意不是 HOT → DONE transition。它只會發布 branch 供 review，並在尚未確認整合前保留原 state 與 cleanup 狀態。
55	
56	## Checkout mode
57	
58	Task 記錄的是意圖，不一定要有 linked worktree。
59	
60	| Mode | 適用情境 | Lifecycle 限制 |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| direct | canonical checkout 中的一個小變更 | HOT ↔ WARM；canonical checkout 不能移除 |
63	| branch-only | 只需要 history isolation，不需要第二個 directory | push 且 canonical checkout 切離後可進 COLD |
64	| worktree | 獨立寫入、平行 stream、長期 feature | 完整 lifecycle |
65	
66	選擇 mode 的依據是碰撞與復原需求，不是儀式感。
67	
68	## Runtime 刻意是可丟失的
69	
70	`runtime.Runtime` 提供 `Open`、`Close`、`List` 與 `Annotate`。`auto` 會依序選 Herdr、tmux、Zellij，最後使用永遠可用的 `none` backend。關閉任何 backend 都不能移除 checkout、branch 或 task entry。
71	
72	因此 reboot、關閉 multiplexer 或更換 runtime backend 都不代表放棄工作。`dev sweep` 能比較 registry 與即時 Git/runtime facts 並回報 drift。
73	
74	## 跨機器 handoff
75	
76	Branch 是傳輸邊界：
77	
78	```bash
79	# machine A
80	dev park --cold --push
81	
82	# machine B
83	dev resume <task> --fetch
84	```
85	
86	每個 branch 同時只有一位 writer。若兩台機器或兩個 agent 必須同時修改同一 feature，應拆成不同 change stream，再於之後整合。
87

```text
1	---
2	description: Run a dev-cli change stream through start, park, resume, review or integration, and conservative cleanup.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-28
6	---
7	
8	# Change-stream workflow
9	
10	A `dev` task is a durable record of one line of work. Select the checkout mode, make the branch recoverable, and treat runtime sessions as disposable.
11	
12	## 1. Select the checkout mode
13	
14	| Mode | Command | Use when |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| direct | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --direct` | one small reversible change in the canonical checkout |
17	| branch-only | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --branch-only --base <ref>` | history isolation is useful but a second directory is not |
18	| worktree | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --base <ref>` | independent mutation, parallel work, or a stream that may outlive the session |
19	
20	Worktree mode is the default. If no branch is supplied, `dev` derives `feat/<task-slug>`; automation should still pass the intended base explicitly.
21	
22	Before changing the canonical checkout in direct or branch-only mode, `dev` guards against sharing it with another active agent/runtime.
23	
24	## 2. Start and inspect
25	
26	```bash
27	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main --next "reproduce expiry race"
28	dev ls
29	dev status
30	```
31	
32	Starting work resolves the repository, validates branch/base, creates or switches the checkout, provisions a worktree when needed, opens the selected runtime, and saves the task. If the branch is already tracked, use `dev resume` instead of creating a duplicate.
33	
34	## 3. Park intentionally
35	
36	```bash
37	dev park --next "add the failing expiry test"
38	```
39	
40	The normal transition is HOT → WARM: close the runtime but keep the checkout. `--next` is more valuable than a long note because it removes the need to re-derive the first action later.
41	
42	If the tree is dirty:
43	
44	```bash
45	dev park --wip --next "finish the expiry test"
46	```
47	
48	This creates a temporary `wip: checkpoint — …` commit. It is searchable and pushable; rewrite or squash it before integrating if it is not useful product history.
49	
50	To release local disk and hand off across machines:
51	
52	```bash
53	dev park --cold --push
54	```
55	
56	COLD requires recoverable commits on the remote. Direct tasks cannot go cold because the canonical checkout is not disposable.
57	
58	## 4. Resume from live facts
59	
60	```bash
61	dev resume "token refresh" --fetch
62	```
63	
64	- WARM: reuse the checkout and reopen the runtime.
65	- COLD: fetch, recreate the branch/worktree if needed, reprovision, and reopen.
66	- Work owned by another host: refuse unless ownership has been deliberately transferred or overridden.
67	
68	Runtime handles are advisory. `dev` re-resolves live sessions instead of assuming a recorded handle still exists.
69	
70	## 5. Integrate or hand off to review
71	
72	Preserve meaningful construction commits:
73	
74	```bash
75	dev done --ff
76	```
77	
78	This requires a clean tree, rebases the task branch onto the base, and runs a fast-forward-only merge in the canonical checkout. It then closes the runtime, removes the worktree unless retained, and marks the task DONE.
79	
80	Use review/CI instead:
81	
82	```bash
83	dev done --pr
84	```
85	
86	This pushes the branch and opens a GitHub pull request or GitLab merge request when the corresponding CLI is available. It **does not** mark the task DONE or clean up the checkout. Current `dev sweep` also does not infer remote request merges, so confirm integration before finishing the local lifecycle.
87	
88	## 6. Sweep drift and stale state
89	
90	```bash
91	dev sweep                 # report only
92	dev sweep --apply         # confirm each suggested action
93	dev sweep --apply --yes   # automation after reviewing the report
94	```
95	
96	Sweep can propose:
97	
98	- HOT → WARM when no live session exists;
99	- old, clean, pushed WARM → COLD;
100	- removing the registry entry for an already-DONE task;
101	- clearing a worktree path Git no longer knows;
102	- reviewing live runtime sessions no task claims.
103	
104	It never deletes uncommitted work. Reporting first is part of the safety model.
105	
106	## Recovery rules
107	
108	- Rebase conflict: resolve it, run `git rebase --continue`, then retry `dev done --ff`; use `git rebase --abort` to return to the pre-rebase state.
109	- Missing worktree directory: run `dev sweep` or `dev wt rm` to prune stale Git administration, then resume.
110	- Wrong owner host: verify the other writer has stopped and pushed before using an override.
111	- Unsure whether work is merged: keep the branch and task; deletion is cheaper after verification than recovery after guessing.
112	
113	## Sources
114

116	- [`internal/cli/park.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/park.go)

8	
9	# 變更流工作流程
10	
11	!!! note "術語規則"
12	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
13	
14	`dev` task 是一條工作線的持久紀錄。先選 checkout mode、讓 branch 可復原，再把 runtime session 當成可丟棄資源。
15	
16	## 1. 選擇 checkout mode
17	
18	| Mode | 命令 | 適用情境 |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| direct | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --direct` | canonical checkout 中的一個小型可逆變更 |
21	| branch-only | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --branch-only --base <ref>` | 需要 history isolation，但不需要第二個 directory |
22	| worktree | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --base <ref>` | 獨立寫入、平行工作或會比 session 存在更久的變更流 (change stream) |
23	
24	Worktree 是預設 mode。未指定 branch 時，`dev` 會產生 `feat/<task-slug>`；automation 仍應明確傳入預期 base。
25	
26	Direct 或 branch-only mode 在修改 canonical checkout 前，`dev` 會防止它與另一個 active agent/runtime 共用。
27	
28	## 2. Start 與檢查
29	
30	```bash
31	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main --next "reproduce expiry race"
32	dev ls
33	dev status
34	```
35	
36	Start 會解析 repository、驗證 branch/base、建立或切換 checkout、需要時佈建 worktree、開啟 runtime，再保存 task。Branch 已被追蹤時應使用 `dev resume`，不要建立重複 task。
37	
38	## 3. 有意識地 park
39	
40	```bash
41	dev park --next "add the failing expiry test"
42	```
43	
44	一般 transition 是 HOT → WARM：關閉 runtime，但保留 checkout。具體 `--next` 比很長的 note 更重要，因為它避免下次重新推導第一個動作。
45	
46	Working tree 尚未乾淨時：
47	
48	```bash
49	dev park --wip --next "finish the expiry test"
50	```
51	
52	這會建立暫時的 `wip: checkpoint — …` commit。它可搜尋、可 push；若不適合作為 product history，整合前應 reword 或 squash。
53	
54	需要釋放本機空間並跨機器 handoff 時：
55	
56	```bash
57	dev park --cold --push
58	```
59	
60	進入 COLD 前，commits 必須已在 remote 上可復原。Direct task 因 canonical checkout 不可丟棄，所以不能進入 COLD。
61	
62	## 4. 依即時 facts resume
63	
64	```bash
65	dev resume "token refresh" --fetch
66	```
67	
68	- WARM：重用 checkout 並重新開啟 runtime。
69	- COLD：fetch，需要時重建 branch/worktree、重新 provision，再開啟 runtime。
70	- 由另一台 host 擁有：除非已刻意移交或 override ownership，否則拒絕。
71	
72	Runtime handle 只是 advisory。`dev` 會重新解析 live sessions，不會假設記錄中的 handle 仍存在。
73	
74	## 5. 整合或交給 review
75	
76	保留有價值的 construction commits：
77	
78	```bash
79	dev done --ff
80	```
81	
82	這要求 clean tree，先把 task branch rebase 到 base，再於 canonical checkout 執行 fast-forward-only merge。完成後關閉 runtime、在未要求保留時移除 worktree，並標示 task DONE。
83	
84	改由 review/CI 處理：
85	
86	```bash
87	dev done --pr
88	```
89	
90	這會 push branch，並在對應 CLI 可用時建立 GitHub pull request 或 GitLab merge request。它**不會**標示 task DONE，也不會清理 checkout。目前 `dev sweep` 同樣不會推斷 remote request 已 merge，因此必須先確認整合，再結束本機 lifecycle。
91	
92	## 6. Sweep drift 與 stale state
93	
94	```bash
95	dev sweep                 # 只回報
96	dev sweep --apply         # 每個建議個別確認
97	dev sweep --apply --yes   # 已檢查 report 後的 automation
98	```
99	
100	Sweep 可建議：
101	
102	- 沒有 live session 時 HOT → WARM；
103	- 長時間未動、clean 且已 push 的 WARM → COLD；
104	- 移除已經 DONE 的 registry entry；
105	- 清除 Git 不再知道的 worktree path；
106	- 檢查沒有 task 認領的 live runtime sessions。
107	
108	它不會刪除 uncommitted work。先回報再動作就是 safety model 的一部分。
109	
110	## 復原規則
111	
112	- Rebase conflict：解決後執行 `git rebase --continue`，再重跑 `dev done --ff`；要回到 rebase 前狀態則用 `git rebase --abort`。
113	- Worktree directory 消失：先用 `dev sweep` 或 `dev wt rm` 清理 stale Git administration，再 resume。
114	- Owner host 不正確：使用 override 前，先確認另一位 writer 已停止並 push。
115	- 不確定是否已 merge：保留 branch 與 task；驗證後刪除永遠比猜錯後復原便宜。
116

8	
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
23	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
24	
25	## Confirmed project limitations
26	
27	### Pull-request completion is not tracked automatically
28	
29	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge to infer that a request later merged. Verify integration and finish/reconcile deliberately; do not assume remote merge implies local DONE.
30	
31	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
32	
33	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
34	
35	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
36	
37	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
38	
39	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
40	
41	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
42	
43	## Current behaviors that are implemented
44	
45	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
46	
47	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
48	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
49	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
50	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
51	
52	## Claude Code status matrix
53	
54	| Surface | Status on 2026-08-28 | Compatibility note |
55	|---|---|---|
56	| core agentic loop/tools | official | exact tools depend on surface/model/policy |
57	| worktree isolation | official, rapidly evolving | cleanup, baseRef, resume, and safety details are version-sensitive |
58	| subagents | official | fork/background defaults and naming changed across 2.1.x |
59	| Agent view | research preview | retain manual sessions/worktrees fallback |
60	| agent teams | experimental, disabled by default | no automatic worktree isolation; resumption/task/shutdown limitations |
61	| Dynamic Workflows | versioned feature | requires v2.1.154+; availability/config and limits vary by release |
62	| Agent SDK | official SDK | language SDK parity and event availability can differ |
63	
64	`TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` are historical tools removed in v2.1.178. The old `Task` worker tool name was replaced by `Agent`; do not confuse either with Task-list metadata tools.
65	
66	## Documentation-stack limitations
67	
68	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` reports that `zh-TW` is not a Lunr language, so Chinese search does not receive a dedicated Lunr stemmer/segmenter. Navigation and pages still build.
69	- `mkdocs-llmstxt` skips pages after static-i18n remaps them. This project replaces that empty output with a deterministic local generator and runs strict builds again.
70	- The copy-to-LLM plugin's button labels remain English on zh-TW pages; this is cosmetic.
71	- MkDocs and Material are pinned below their next major versions because the selected plugin stack targets MkDocs 1.x/Material 9.x.
72	
73	## Reporting a compatibility change
74	
75	Update the owning guide, both languages, this matrix, and [Sources and freshness](sources-freshness.md). Include the tested binary/version and a code/test or official-source link. Never preserve a known false statement for backward documentation compatibility.
76	
77	## Sources
78	
79	- [`internal/runtime/runtime.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/runtime.go)
80	- [`internal/cli/done.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/done.go)
81	- [`internal/cli/sweep.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/sweep.go)
82	- [`internal/task/task.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/task/task.go)
83	- [`internal/forge/cache.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/forge/cache.go)
84	- [Claude Code parallel agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents)
85
```

17	## dev-cli capability matrix
18	
19	| Capability | Dependency | 缺少時 |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| 核心 repository/task/worktree 操作 | Git | 無法使用；Git 是唯一 hard runtime dependency |

29	## 已確認的專案限制
30	
31	### Pull request completion 不會自動追蹤
32	
33	`dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。目前 `dev sweep` 不會 query forge 推斷 request 後來已 merge。請驗證 integration 後再刻意 finish/reconcile；不能假設 remote merge 代表 local DONE。
34

36	
37	Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
