40	
41	`dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
42	
43	### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
44	
45	Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
46	
47	## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
48	
49	以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
50	
51	- `dev start --focus` 會在 non-JSON creation 後 activate runtime。
52	- TUI navigation 會拒絕開啟 checkout 不存在的 COLD task，並要求使用 `dev resume`。
53	- Runtime handle 現在保存 backend provenance，cleanup 前會重新驗證。

55	
56	## Claude Code status matrix
57	
58	| Surface | 2026-08-28 status | Compatibility note |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| core agentic loop/tools | official | exact tools 依 surface/model/policy 而異 |
61	| worktree isolation | official、快速演進 | cleanup、baseRef、resume 與 safety details 都有 version sensitivity |
62	| subagents | official | fork/background defaults 與 naming 在 2.1.x 中曾變更 |
63	| Agent view | research preview | 保留 manual sessions/worktrees fallback |
64	| agent teams | experimental、預設關閉 | 無 automatic worktree isolation；有 resumption/task/shutdown limitations |
65	| Dynamic Workflows | versioned feature | 需要 v2.1.154+；availability/config/limits 依 release 而異 |
66	| Agent SDK | official SDK | 不同 language SDK 的 parity 與 event availability 可能不同 |

68	`TeamCreate` 與 `TeamDelete` 是 v2.1.178 移除的 historical tools。舊 `Task` worker tool 已由 `Agent` 取代；兩者都不能與 Task-list metadata tools 混淆。

70	## Documentation stack 限制
71	
72	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` 回報 `zh-TW` 不是 Lunr language，因此 Chinese search 沒有專用 Lunr stemmer/segmenter；navigation 與 pages 仍正常 build。

79	更新 owning guide、兩種語言、這份 matrix 與[來源與時效](sources-freshness.md)。附 tested binary/version 與 code/test 或 official-source link。不能為了 documentation backward compatibility 保留已知錯誤敘述。

1	"""MkDocs hooks for generated, route-local LLM Markdown endpoints."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import subprocess
6	import sys
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	
10	def on_config(config, **_kwargs):
11	    """Deduplicate assets when static-i18n reconfigures plugins per locale."""
12	    for key in ("extra_javascript", "extra_css"):
13	        values = config.get(key) or []
14	        seen: set[str] = set()
15	        unique = []
16	        for value in values:
17	            identity = str(value)
18	            if identity in seen:
19	                continue
20	            seen.add(identity)
21	            unique.append(value)
22	        config[key] = unique
23	    return config
24	
25	
26	def on_post_build(config, **_kwargs) -> None:
27	    """Publish one index.md endpoint beside every rendered HTML page."""
28	    root = Path(config.config_file_path).resolve().parent
29	    subprocess.run(
30	        [
31	            sys.executable,
32	            str(root / "scripts" / "check-docs.py"),
33	            "--publish-markdown",
34	            str(config.site_dir),
35	        ],
36	        cwd=root,
37	        check=True,
38	    )
39

169	    match = re.match(r"^(.*?)(?::(\d+))?(?::(\d+))?$", spec)
170	    if match is None:

176	def resolve_snippet(spec: str) -> tuple[Path | None, int | None, int | None]:

178	    for candidate in (ROOT / name, DOCS / name, DOCS / "_snippets" / name):

504	def output_path(site: Path, relative: str, language: str) -> Path:
505	    stem = relative[:-3]
506	    prefix = Path(language) if language != "en" else Path()
507	    if stem == "index":
508	        return site / prefix / "index.html"
509	    if stem.endswith("/index"):
510	        return site / prefix / f"{stem}.html"
511	    return site / prefix / stem / "index.html"

537	            content = rewrite_document_links(document, site_url, page_paths).rstrip() + "\n"

544	def local_target(site: Path, site_url: str, source: Path, href: str) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:
545	    parsed = urlsplit(href)
546	    if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc or href.startswith(("mailto:", "tel:", "javascript:", "data:")):
547	        return None, ""
548	
549	    base_path = urlsplit(site_url).path.rstrip("/")
550	    source_rel = source.relative_to(site).as_posix()
551	    if source_rel == "index.html":
552	        source_route = "/"
553	    elif source_rel.endswith("/index.html"):
554	        source_route = f"/{source_rel[:-len('index.html')]}"
555	    else:
556	        source_route = f"/{source_rel}"
557	    public_source = f"{base_path}{source_route}"
558	    target_route = urljoin(public_source, parsed.path or "")
559	    if base_path and not (target_route == base_path or target_route.startswith(f"{base_path}/")):
560	        return None, ""
561	    relative = target_route[len(base_path) :].lstrip("/") if base_path else target_route.lstrip("/")
562	    relative = posixpath.normpath(relative)
563	    if relative == ".":
564	        relative = ""
565	
566	    candidate = site / relative
567	    if target_route.endswith("/") or not relative:
568	        candidate = candidate / "index.html"
569	    elif candidate.is_dir():
570	        candidate = candidate / "index.html"
571	    elif not candidate.suffix:
572	        index = candidate / "index.html"
573	        if index.exists():
574	            candidate = index
575	    return candidate, unquote(parsed.fragment)
576	
577	
578	def absolute_site_target(site: Path, site_url: str, href: str) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:
579	    parsed = urlsplit(href)
580	    configured = urlsplit(site_url)
581	    if parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or parsed.netloc != configured.netloc:
582	        return None, ""
583	    base_path = configured.path.rstrip("/")
584	    if base_path and not (parsed.path == base_path or parsed.path.startswith(f"{base_path}/")):
585	        return None, ""
586	    relative = parsed.path[len(base_path) :].lstrip("/") if base_path else parsed.path.lstrip("/")
587	    candidate = site / relative
588	    if not relative or parsed.path.endswith("/"):
589	        candidate = candidate / "index.html"
590	    elif candidate.is_dir():
591	        candidate = candidate / "index.html"
592	    elif not candidate.suffix:
593	        candidate = candidate / "index.html"
594	    return candidate, unquote(parsed.fragment)

+# Repository quick notes
+
+Capture informal thoughts without adding another dot-folder to the repository.
+
+## Quick use
+
+```bash
+dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
+dev note list api
+dev note search "event subscription"
+dev note show <id-or-prefix>
+dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
+dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
+```
+
+Inside a repo, `--repo` is optional.
+
+## TUI
+
+```text
+TASKS / REPOS:  n quick add · N browse
+REMOTE:         n/N only when a local clone exists
+TRY:            n remains new Try
+```
+
+Notes overlay:
+
+```text
+j/k move · / search · Enter expand · a/n add · e edit · d delete · Esc back
+```
+
+Delete opens a visible confirmation and requires `y`. Editing suspends the TUI,
+opens only the Markdown body in VISUAL/EDITOR, validates non-empty content, then
+atomically updates the source and FTS index. If another process changed the note
+while the editor was open, dev rejects the stale update and reports where the
+edited temporary body was preserved.
+
+## Where notes live
+
+```text
+$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repo-id>/<note-id>.md  durable, mode 0600
+$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db                            disposable FTS, mode 0600
+```
+
+Repository catalog IDs survive path moves, symlink indexes and linked worktree
+paths. A note created while standing in a worktree therefore appears on the
+canonical repo.
+
+```bash
+dev note path api
+dev note path --all
+dev note reindex
+dev cache clear notes       # source Markdown remains
+dev note search "query"     # rebuilds missing/stale index
+```
+
+Search is term-wise prefix FTS for Latin text, with literal term-wise fallback
+for CJK substrings.
+
+`repo mark --note` is a separate single-line catalog summary. Structured task
+systems such as td/beads are separate optional future adapters; dev does not
+initialize their repo dot-folders.

+# Repository quick notes
+
+Read this when capturing, searching, editing or deleting informal repository
+thoughts, or when deciding whether a thought belongs in dev, td, or beads.
+
+## Storage boundary
+
+Durable source:
+
+```text
+$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-repository-id>/<note-id>.md
+```
+
+Search index:
+
+```text
+$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db
+```
+
+Markdown is authoritative. SQLite FTS is disposable and rebuilt automatically
+when absent or stale. `dev cache clear notes` must never remove Markdown.
+
+Each note is append-only by default and has a stable UUID, created/updated
+timestamps, normalized tags and a Markdown body. Repo rename, symlink index,
+worktree path or a second host do not change its attachment because the
+repository directory key is the catalog asset ID.
+
+## CLI workflow
+
+```bash
+dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
+dev note list api
+dev note search "event subscription" --repo api
+dev note show <id-or-unique-prefix>
+dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
+dev note delete <id-or-prefix>       # confirms
+dev note reindex
+dev note path api
+```
+
+`add` requires text or `--editor`; it never creates an empty note. `edit` opens
+a temporary body, then validates and atomically replaces the durable file only
+when the editor succeeds with non-empty content. Tags survive unless `--tag`
+is explicitly supplied. Edit uses an optimistic content revision under the
+mutation lock; if another process won first, the stale edit is rejected and its
+temporary body path is reported for manual recovery.
+
+Search is term-wise prefix FTS for Latin text. Non-ASCII input uses literal
+term-wise matching because SQLite `unicode61` does not segment CJK substrings;
+`改善` must still find `記得改善 worktree`.
+
+## TUI workflow
+
+On TASKS or REPOS (including a child worktree):
+
+```text
+n   quick one-line note, Enter saves, Esc cancels
+N   notes overlay for the selected repository
+```
+
+On a REMOTE row, notes are enabled only when a local clone exists. In TRY,
+lowercase `n` remains “new Try”; repo quick notes do not attach to Try assets.
+
+Inside NOTES:
+
+```text
+j/k       move
+/         search body, tags and repo
+Enter     expand/collapse body
+a or n    add
+ e        edit body in VISUAL/EDITOR
+d         visible delete confirmation; y confirms
+N/Esc/q   return
+```
+
+The configurable REPOS column `notes` shows a count; it is not enabled by
+default because the table is width-constrained. Repo/task detail always shows
+count + latest preview when notes exist.
+
+## What is not a quick note
+
+`catalog.Entry.Note` remains the single metadata summary used by `repo mark`
+and Try lifecycle. Quick notes do not overwrite it.
+
+`td` / `beads` are structured repo-local task systems and may create dot-folders
+inside a checkout. They remain optional future adapters. Do not mirror their
+tasks into quick notes or initialize either tool automatically.
+
+## Gotchas
+
+- A note opened from a linked worktree attaches to the canonical clone by Git
+  common-directory identity, not the disposable worktree path.
+- Delayed TUI load results carry target ID + request generation and are ignored
+  after switching repositories; never remove that guard from `noteListMsg`.
+- Deleting `notes.db` deletes no thoughts; the next search rebuilds it.
+- Deleting a Markdown file is durable deletion and requires confirmation.
+- The FTS database contains full private note bodies and is mode 0600.
```

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	### Added
10	
11	- Catalog-backed repository quick notes with durable Markdown storage, rebuildable full-text search, CLI commands, and TUI add/browse workflows.
12	- Azure DevOps Services repository inventory, search, cloning, and opt-in forge configuration.
13	- An interactive, context-aware `dev start` wizard for managed task creation.
14	- Runtime session activation so opened or reused task surfaces can be focused or attached.
15	- Exact-pane, fail-closed safeguards for launching parallel agents in newly created Herdr worktrees.
16	- Agent-ready repository context output, TUI copy actions, and an expanded worktree tree with per-checkout state.
17	- A bilingual English/Traditional Chinese MkDocs knowledge site with strict source/site checks and GitHub Pages deployment.
18	
19	### Fixed
20	
21	- Focused starts now activate their runtime session after the interactive wizard completes.
22	- Corrected command/config documentation to remove the unsupported `dev wt plan --json` example, include Azure forge configuration, and describe shell navigation without implying ordinary command output is evaluated.
23	- Corrected bundled skill reference coverage and agent-rule numbering.
24	
25	## [0.1.0] - 2026-08-28
26	
27	### Added
28	
29	- The HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE task lifecycle with direct, branch-only, and managed-worktree checkout modes.
30	- A TASKS/REPOS/TRY/REMOTE terminal dashboard backed by the same services as the non-interactive CLI.
31	- Try catalog identity, personal metadata, archive/restore, graduation, and guarded filesystem transitions.
32	- Rich Git inventory for upstream divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged, and untracked paths.
33	- Managed worktree placement and provisioning with explicit ignored-file handling and per-ecosystem dependency strategies.
34	- Repository discovery, remote-risk inspection, logical size accounting, and durable activity statistics.
35	- Recursive machine bootstrap with non-destructive symlink indexing and guarded physical move plans.
36	- Adoption of existing worktrees, runtime sessions, and unmerged branches into the task registry.
37	- Managed `.gitignore` generation from GitHub templates plus project-local sections.
38	- XDG-based configurable repository, worktree, task, catalog, cache, and runtime layouts.
39	- An embedded and installable `dev-cli` agent skill with a generated command reference checked in CI.
40	- Homebrew, Go, and source installation paths, shell completion, and directory-changing shell integration.
41

1	---
2	description: Navigate tasks, repositories, experiments, and remotes in the TUI; inventory or adopt existing work without destructive migration.
3	authority: project
4	status: evolving
5	verified_on: 2026-08-28
6	---
7	
8	# TUI, repositories, and bootstrap
9	
10	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when standard input/output are terminals. When piped, it prints the plain task listing so shell composition remains predictable.
11	
12	## Four views
13	
14	| View | Question | Source |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry plus live Git/runtime facts |
17	| REPOS | What durable repositories exist here? | configured scan roots and local catalog |
18	| TRY | Which experiments can I resume, archive, or graduate? | experiment catalog plus live facts |
19	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated `gh`/`glab` inventories and cache |
20	
21	Switch with `tab`, `h`/`l`, or arrows. Use `j`/`k`, `g`/`G`, `ctrl+d`/`ctrl+u`, `/` to filter, `?` for help, and `esc`/`q` to leave the current mode.
22	
23	## Common actions
24	
25	### TASKS
26	
27	```text
28	enter/o   open the selected task
29	p         park warm and enter the next action
30	c         edit the next action
31	1/2/3     HOT/WARM/COLD filters
32	```
33	
34	A COLD task must be rebuilt with `dev resume`; the TUI does not silently recreate it through a generic open action.
35	
36	### REPOS
37	
38	```text
39	enter/o   ad-hoc open without creating a task
40	space     expand linked worktrees
41	m         edit repository tags/note
42	d         track direct work on the current branch
43	s         start isolated work: branch + worktree + provisioning + runtime
44	H         open the repository activity heatmap
45	y         open copy/context actions
46	```
47	
48	Expanded rows explain every linked worktree, including harness-owned `(ephemeral)` and otherwise unmanaged `(external)` checkouts. The LIVE column shows runtime activity separately from task state.
49	
50	`dev repo context [repo]` emits the same agent-ready Markdown context available from the TUI copy menu, including paths, Git/worktree/runtime facts, and tasks.
51	
52	### TRY and REMOTE
53	
54	TRY handles low-cost experiments, reversible archive/restore, marking, and graduation. Archive is organization, not deletion or disk reclamation.
55	
56	REMOTE loads lazily so startup does not wait for the network. Enter opens a local clone; `c` confirms before cloning an absent repository; `r` refreshes forge inventories and their private XDG cache.
57	
58	## External tools
59	
60	```bash
61	dev tui tools
62	```
63	
64	Configured tools run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout while the alternate screen is suspended. `interactive = true` uses `$SHELL -lic` so local aliases/functions can resolve; use a real executable on `PATH` when the binding must be portable.
65	
66	```toml
67	[[tui.tools]]
68	key = "L"
69	name = "lazygit"
70	run = "lazygit"
71	```
72	
73	Keys are case-sensitive and cannot shadow dashboard-owned bindings. Returning from an editor can reload most config; switching runtime backend requires restarting the TUI.
74	
75	## Inventory an existing machine
76	
77	Start with a report:
78	
79	```bash
80	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work
81	dev bootstrap ~/code --json
82	```
83	
84	The scanner identifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories, and symlink aliases, then deduplicates them by Git identity.
85	
86	The recommended organization layer is a non-destructive symlink index:
87	
88	```bash
89	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat
90	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat --apply
91	```
92	
93	Physical moves are a separate, stricter mode. A move plan blocks dirty repositories, linked worktrees, live sessions/current working directories, aliases that would break, occupied destinations, and cross-filesystem renames. If any row is blocked, apply moves none.
94	
95	## Adopt work already in flight
96	
97	Bootstrap answers **where repositories are**. Adoption answers **which existing branches, worktrees, and sessions are active work**:
98	
99	```bash
100	dev adopt
101	dev adopt --apply
102	```
103	
104	Adopt reports by default and only writes task entries after `--apply` plus confirmation. It does not move, rename, or delete checkouts, and it excludes recognized harness-ephemeral worktrees.
105	
106	## Sources

108	- [`internal/help/topics/tui.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/help/topics/tui.md)
109	- [`internal/help/topics/bootstrap.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/help/topics/bootstrap.md)
110	- [`internal/cli/adopt.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/adopt.go)
111	- [`internal/cli/bootstrap.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/bootstrap.go)
112
```

3	authority: project

5	verified_on: 2026-08-28
6	---
7	
8	# Getting started
9	
10	Install `dev`, let it discover the machine, then run one small change stream through `start`, `park`, `resume`, and `done`.
11	
12	## 1. Install and initialize
13	
14	```bash
15	make install
16	dev config init
17	```
18	
19	Add the shell integration so commands that open a checkout can change the current shell's directory:
20	
21	=== "zsh or bash"
22	
23	    ```bash
24	    eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"   # use bash for bash
25	    ```
26	
27	=== "fish"
28	
29	    ```fish
30	    dev shell-init fish | source
31	    ```
32	
33	Check the effective environment:
34	
35	```bash
36	dev doctor
37	dev config show
38	```
39	
40	Only Git is required. Herdr, tmux, Zellij, `gh`, and `glab` add richer runtime and forge behavior but degrade cleanly when absent.
41	
42	## 2. Start work
43	
44	From any discovered repository, start a named task. Pass the base explicitly in scripts and agent-driven commands:
45	
46	```bash
47	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
48	```
49	
50	The default mode creates a branch, a linked worktree at the configured path, provisions it, opens the best available runtime, and records a HOT task.
51	
52	Use a lighter checkout mode only when it matches the work:
53	
54	```bash
55	dev start api --task "one-line typo" --direct
56	dev start api --task "small local branch" --branch-only --base main
57	```
58	
59	- `--direct` works in the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD.
60	- `--branch-only` creates a branch without a linked worktree.
61	- The default worktree mode is best for independent or parallel mutation.
62	
63	## 3. Park with a useful next action
64	
65	```bash
66	dev park --next "reproduce the refresh race, then add a regression test"
67	```
68	
69	This closes the runtime and marks the task WARM while retaining the branch and checkout. If the tree is dirty, make a recoverable checkpoint instead of an invisible stash:
70	
71	```bash
72	dev park --wip --next "finish the regression test"
73	```
74	
75	For cross-machine handoff, commit and push before removing the checkout:
76	
77	```bash
78	dev park --cold --push
79	```
80	
81	## 4. Resume and inspect
82	
83	```bash
84	dev ls
85	dev resume "token refresh" --fetch
86	dev status
87	```
88	
89	A WARM task reopens its existing checkout. A COLD task reconstructs a worktree from the remote branch. The branch is the durable identity; the directory is a cache.
90	
91	## 5. Integrate deliberately
92	
93	```bash
94	dev done --ff
95	```
96	
97	`--ff` rebases the change branch onto its base and fast-forwards the base, preserving useful commits. If review or CI should decide the merge, open a request instead:
98	
99	```bash
100	dev done --pr
101	```
102	
103	`--pr` pushes and opens a pull or merge request, but intentionally leaves the task unchanged and not DONE while review is pending. After integration, inspect cleanup suggestions:
104	
105	```bash
106	dev sweep
107	dev sweep --apply
108	```
109

1	---
2	description: Use dev-cli to keep Git change streams durable while worktrees, runtimes, and coding agents remain replaceable.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-28
6	---
7	
8	# dev-cli
9	
10	`dev` is a thin coordination layer over Git, worktrees, forges, terminal runtimes, and coding agents. It keeps the durable identity of work in Git while recording just enough intent to close a terminal today and resume the same change stream tomorrow.
11	
12	!!! tip "Start with one rule"
13	    **One branch per independent change stream. One worktree per mutation boundary. One pane per cooperating agent.**
14	
15	## What problem it solves
16	
17	Four layers often collapse into one mental model. `dev` keeps their responsibilities separate:
18	
19	| Layer | Owns | Safe to recreate? |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| Git remote and branch | durable code history and handoff | no — this is the source of truth |
22	| Git worktree | one checked-out view of a branch | yes, after commits are recoverable |
23	| Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or a shell | a live per-host runtime | yes |
24	| `dev` task registry | state, owner, next action, and reconstruction metadata | yes, from Git plus human intent |
25	
26	Closing a runtime therefore closes a session, not the work itself. Going cold removes a checkout, not its branch. A task becomes done only after integration.
27	
28	## Choose a path
29	
30	- **First use:** install and run a complete task in [Getting started](getting-started.md).
31	- **Daily workflow:** follow the [change-stream workflow](guides/change-stream-workflow.md).
32	- **Several agents:** use the [parallel work decision guide](claude/parallel-work-chooser.md).
33	- **Fresh worktree is missing `.env` or dependencies:** read [Worktrees and provisioning](guides/worktrees-provisioning.md).
34	- **Need a short policy:** use the [best-practice checklist](best-practices.md).
35	- **Need exact flags:** open [Commands and configuration](reference/commands-config.md).
36	
37	## The site map
38	
39	- **Concepts** defines the lifecycle, ownership boundaries, and vocabulary.
40	- **Using dev-cli** gives task-, worktree-, runtime-, and TUI-oriented recipes.
41	- **Git and GitHub** separates current GitHub Flow from Git semantics and historical variants.
42	- **Claude Code** explains the public agentic harness, its parallel-work primitives, and their limits.
43	- **Reference** records commands, compatibility, sources, and freshness.
44	- **Notes** provides a stable home and template for future research.
45	
46	## LLM-friendly outputs
47	
48	Every page provides copy-to-LLM controls. The build also publishes:
49	
50	- [`llms.txt`](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dev-cli/llms.txt) — a bilingual page index with descriptions.
51	- [`llms-full.txt`](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dev-cli/llms-full.txt) — the complete English and Traditional Chinese corpus.
52	
53	These outputs are generated from the same navigation and page metadata as the site and are checked in CI.
54	
55	## Source policy
56	
57	Project behavior is checked against code and tests. Git and GitHub behavior comes from current official documentation. Claude Code behavior comes from current Anthropic documentation and is marked when experimental or research preview. Historical material is never presented as the current workflow.
58	
59	See [Sources and freshness](reference/sources-freshness.md) for the claim matrix and review dates.
60
```

8	
9	# dev-cli
10	
11	!!! note "術語規則"
12	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
13	
14	`dev` 是連接 Git、worktree、forge、terminal runtime 與 coding agent 的輕量協調層。它把工作的持久身分留在 Git，另記錄足以讓你今天關閉 terminal、明天接續同一條變更流 (change stream) 的意圖。
15	
16	!!! tip "先記住一條規則"
17	    **每條獨立變更流一個 branch；每個變動邊界 (mutation boundary) 一個 worktree；每個協作 agent 一個 pane。**
18	
19	## 它解決什麼問題
20	
21	四個層次很容易被誤當成同一件事；`dev` 明確分開責任：
22	
23	| 層次 | 負責內容 | 能否安全重建？ |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| Git remote 與 branch | 持久 code history 與 handoff | 不行——這是 source of truth |
26	| Git worktree | branch 的一份 checkout | commits 可復原後可以 |
27	| Herdr、tmux、Zellij 或 shell | 每台 host 的即時執行環境 (runtime) | 可以 |
28	| `dev` task registry | state、owner、next action 與重建 metadata | 可由 Git 加上人類意圖重建 |
29	
30	因此，關閉 runtime 只會關掉 session，不會結束工作。進入 COLD 會移除 checkout，不會刪除 branch。只有完成整合後，task 才是 DONE。
31

36	- **同時使用多個 agent：**先看[平行工作決策指南](claude/parallel-work-chooser.md)。
37	- **新 worktree 缺少 `.env` 或 dependencies：**看[Worktree 與環境佈建](guides/worktrees-provisioning.md)。
38	- **只需要短版規則：**使用[最佳實務 checklist](best-practices.md)。
39	- **需要精確 flags：**開啟[命令與設定](reference/commands-config.md)。
40	
41	## 網站結構
42	
43	- **核心概念**定義 lifecycle、ownership boundary 與共同詞彙。
44	- **使用 dev-cli**提供 task、worktree、runtime 與 TUI 的 recipes。
45	- **Git 與 GitHub**分開目前的 GitHub Flow、Git 語義和歷史版本。
46	- **Claude Code**說明公開的 agentic harness、parallel primitives 與限制。
47	- **參考資料**保存命令、相容性、來源與 freshness。
48	- **筆記**提供未來研究可持續擴充的固定位置與模板。
49	
50	## 適合 LLM 的輸出
51	
52	每頁都有 copy-to-LLM 操作。建置也會發布：
53	
54	- [`llms.txt`](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dev-cli/llms.txt)：附描述的雙語頁面索引。
55	- [`llms-full.txt`](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dev-cli/llms-full.txt)：完整英文與繁中內容。
56	
57	兩者都由同一份 nav 與 page metadata 產生，並由 CI 檢查。
58	
59	## 來源政策
60	
61	專案行為要回到 code 與 tests 驗證；Git 與 GitHub 行為以目前官方文件為準；Claude Code 行為以目前 Anthropic 文件為準，experimental 或 research preview 必須明示；歷史資料永遠不能冒充現行 workflow。
62	
63	完整規則與查核日期請看[來源與時效](reference/sources-freshness.md)。
64
```

34	// paths on another volume (e.g. /mnt/fast/worktrees) all work.

49		// those names.
50		Backend string `toml:"backend"`
51		// MetadataSource is the --source id used for herdr workspace metadata.
52		MetadataSource string `toml:"metadata_source"`

55	// Worktree controls where linked worktrees land and how they get provisioned
56	// into a usable state (deps installed, gitignored env files carried over).
57	type Worktree struct {
58		// Include lists .gitignore-syntax patterns; matching files are copied into
59		// a new worktree only when they are actually gitignored in the source
60		// checkout. Tracked files are already in the checkout.
61		Include []string `toml:"include"`
62		// Link names directories symlinked rather than copied (opt-in: sharing
63		// node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that it
64		// must never be a default).
65		Link []string `toml:"link"`
66		// PostCreate is either the string "auto" (detect from lockfiles) or an
67		// explicit list of shell commands run in the new worktree.
68		PostCreate PostCreate `toml:"post_create"`
69		// Strategy is how a new worktree gets its installed dependencies:
70		// "reinstall" (correct, the default), "copy", "link" or "skip". dev
71		// narrows an unsound choice back to reinstall and says why — copying a
72		// virtualenv, for instance, cannot work, because it bakes its own
73		// absolute path into pyvenv.cfg.
74		Strategy string `toml:"strategy"`
75		// Strategies overrides Strategy per ecosystem ("python", "node", "go",
76		// "rust", "ruby", "elixir").
77		Strategies map[string]string `toml:"strategies"`

105		// wandering through a mounted filesystem forever.

354			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true, "notes": true,

360			}

387	func validAzureDevOpsOrganization(raw string) bool {
388		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
389		if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil ||
390			u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.Port() != "" {
391			return false
392		}
393		host := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
394		segments := strings.FieldsFunc(u.Path, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' })
395		switch {
396		case host == "dev.azure.com":
397			return len(segments) == 1
398		case strings.HasSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com"):
399			organization := strings.TrimSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com")
400			return organization != "" && organization != "vs-ssh" && len(segments) == 0
401		default:
402			return false
403		}
404	}

1	// Package note stores append-only repository thoughts as ordinary Markdown
2	// files. SQLite indexes them for search, but the files are the durable source
3	// of truth: readable without dev, syncable without database merge conflicts,
4	// and recoverable after every cache is deleted.
5	package note
6	
7	import (
8		"crypto/sha256"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
15	)
16	
17	const CurrentSchemaVersion = 1
18	
19	var (
20		ErrNotFound   = errors.New("note not found")
21		ErrConflict   = errors.New("note changed since it was opened")
22		ErrInvalid    = errors.New("invalid note")
23		ErrRepository = errors.New("invalid note repository")
24	)
25	
26	// Note is one timestamped thought attached to a stable catalog asset ID.
27	type Note struct {
28		SchemaVersion int       `toml:"schema_version" json:"schema_version"`
29		ID            string    `toml:"id" json:"id"`
30		RepositoryID  string    `toml:"repository_id" json:"repository_id"`
31		Repository    string    `toml:"repository" json:"repository"`
32		Created       time.Time `toml:"created" json:"created"`
33		Updated       time.Time `toml:"updated" json:"updated"`
34		Tags          []string  `toml:"tags" json:"tags"`
35	
36		Body string `toml:"-" json:"body"`
37		Path string `toml:"-" json:"path,omitempty"`
38	}
39	
40	func (n *Note) Normalize() {
41		if n == nil {
42			return
43		}
44		n.Repository = strings.TrimSpace(n.Repository)
45		n.Body = normalizeBody(n.Body)
46		n.Tags = catalog.NormalizeTags(n.Tags)
47	}
48	
49	func (n Note) Validate() error {
50		if n.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
51			return fmt.Errorf("note %s schema version %d: %w", n.ID, n.SchemaVersion, ErrInvalid)
52		}
53		if err := catalog.ValidateID(n.ID); err != nil {
54			return fmt.Errorf("note ID: %w", err)
55		}
56		if err := catalog.ValidateID(n.RepositoryID); err != nil {
57			return fmt.Errorf("repository ID: %w: %w", err, ErrRepository)
58		}
59		if strings.TrimSpace(n.Repository) == "" {
60			return fmt.Errorf("note %s: repository name is required: %w", n.ID, ErrRepository)
61		}
62		if strings.TrimSpace(n.Body) == "" {
63			return fmt.Errorf("note %s: body is empty: %w", n.ID, ErrInvalid)
64		}
65		if n.Created.IsZero() || n.Updated.IsZero() {
66			return fmt.Errorf("note %s: created and updated are required: %w", n.ID, ErrInvalid)
67		}
68		if n.Updated.Before(n.Created) {
69			return fmt.Errorf("note %s: updated precedes created: %w", n.ID, ErrInvalid)
70		}
71		return nil
72	}
73	
74	// Revision fingerprints every field an editor is allowed to preserve or
75	// replace. Update compares it while holding the mutation lock, preventing a
76	// stale editor session from silently overwriting another process's changes.
77	func (n Note) Revision() string {
78		payload := strings.Join([]string{
79			n.ID, n.RepositoryID, n.Repository,
80			n.Created.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
81			n.Updated.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
82			strings.Join(n.Tags, "\x00"), n.Body,
83		}, "\x00")
84		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256([]byte(payload)))
85	}
86	
87	// Preview returns the first non-empty body line, collapsed and truncated.
88	func (n Note) Preview(limit int) string {
89		line := ""
90		for _, candidate := range strings.Split(n.Body, "\n") {
91			if strings.TrimSpace(candidate) != "" {
92				line = strings.Join(strings.Fields(candidate), " ")
93				break
94			}
95		}
96		if limit <= 0 || len([]rune(line)) <= limit {
97			return line
98		}
99		runes := []rune(line)
100		return string(runes[:limit-1]) + "…"
101	}
102	
103	func normalizeBody(body string) string {
104		body = strings.ReplaceAll(body, "\r\n", "\n")
105		body = strings.TrimSpace(body)
106		if body == "" {
107			return ""
108		}
109		return body + "\n"
110	}

20	// Index is a disposable FTS5 database over durable Markdown notes.
21	type Index struct {

26	func OpenIndex(path string) (*Index, error) {
27		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
28			return nil, err
29		}
30		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		i := &Index{Path: path, db: db}
35		if err := i.migrate(); err != nil {
36			_ = db.Close()
37			return nil, err
38		}
39		// The index contains full note bodies, including private thoughts.
40		if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
41			_ = db.Close()
42			return nil, err
43		}
44		return i, nil
45	}

49	func (i *Index) migrate() error {
50		var version int
51		if err := i.db.QueryRow("PRAGMA user_version").Scan(&version); err != nil {
52			return err
53		}
54		if version > indexSchemaVersion {

56				ErrIndexSchema, version, indexSchemaVersion)

91	func validateColumns(db *sql.DB, table string, expected []string) error {
92		rows, err := db.Query("PRAGMA table_info(" + table + ")")
93		if err != nil {
94			return err
95		}
96		defer rows.Close()
97		var actual []string
98		for rows.Next() {
99			var cid, notNull, primaryKey int
100			var name, typ string
101			var defaultValue any
102			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &typ, &notNull, &defaultValue, &primaryKey); err != nil {
103				return err
104			}
105			actual = append(actual, name)
106		}
107		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if !slices.Equal(actual, expected) {
111			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s columns %v, want %v", ErrIndexSchema, table, actual, expected)

125	func (i *Index) Rebuild(notes []*Note) error {

169	(id, repository_id, repository, tags, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
170			n.ID, n.RepositoryID, n.Repository, strings.Join(n.Tags, " "), n.Body); err != nil {

172		}
173		if _, err := tx.Exec(`INSERT INTO note_manifest (id, updated) VALUES (?, ?)

180	func (i *Index) Delete(id string) error {
181		tx, err := i.db.Begin()
182		if err != nil {
183			return err
184		}
185		defer tx.Rollback()
186		if _, err := tx.Exec("DELETE FROM notes_fts WHERE id = ?", id); err != nil {
187			return err
188		}
189		if _, err := tx.Exec("DELETE FROM note_manifest WHERE id = ?", id); err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		return tx.Commit()
193	}
194	
195	// Current reports whether the manifest exactly matches the durable notes.
196	func (i *Index) Current(notes []*Note) bool {
197		rows, err := i.db.Query("SELECT id, updated FROM note_manifest")
198		if err != nil {
199			return false
200		}
201		defer rows.Close()
202		manifest := map[string]string{}
203		for rows.Next() {
204			var id, updated string
205			if rows.Scan(&id, &updated) != nil {
206				return false
207			}
208			manifest[id] = updated
209		}
210		if len(manifest) != len(notes) {
211			return false
212		}
213		for _, n := range notes {
214			if manifest[n.ID] != fingerprint(n) {
215				return false
216			}
217		}
218		return true
219	}

1	# TODO

4	
5	## Active
6	
7	### P1 · L — Verified backup receipts and safe local eviction
8	Phase 1 intentionally stops at reversible archive. Before adding `dev reclaim`
9	or any action that deletes a local checkout, build a fresh preflight that checks
10	all local heads/tags/notes/stash against actual remote refs, plus dirty,
11	untracked, ignored, LFS, submodule/nested-repo, live-runtime, task, cwd and
12	linked-worktree state. `no remote` or any local-only ref must block safe
13	removal; multiple remotes/upstreams require an explicit recovery target.
14	
15	Add an explicit `backup --push` receipt, report-only `reclaim`, typed/batch
16	confirmation, separately named data-loss acknowledgements (never a generic
17	`--force`), linked-worktree removal that preserves branch/common-dir, and
18	remote/shared-Git restore. Non-Git experiments need a real archive/export
19	format before they can be called recoverable. Do not infer safety merely from
20	"origin exists" or the current branch being synced.
21	
22	### P2 · M — Incremental local repo snapshot
23	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
24	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
25	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
26	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
27	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.
28	
29	### P3 · M — Optional repo-local task backend adapters (td / beads)
30	Research and detect repo-local task stores without making either a core
31	dependency:
32	
33	- td: <https://sidecar.haplab.com/docs/td>
34	- beads: <https://github.com/gastownhall/beads>
35	
36	Both may create dot-folders inside a repo. An adapter should report which
37	backend is present, delegate through its CLI, and avoid copying its task data
38	into dev's own notes/tasks. Decide only after comparing lifecycle, multi-agent
39	locking, git noise, cross-machine sync, archival and uninstall behavior. Until
40	then, record the integration point rather than prematurely selecting a tool.
41	
42	### P2 · M — Multi-host aggregation
43	`dev ls --all` fanning out over ssh to the machines in a configured host list,
44	merging their `dev ls --json`. The JSON contract is already stable and the
45	`owner` field already identifies which machine holds a task, so this is
46	plumbing rather than design. Today the same thing works by hand:
47	
48	```bash
49	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
50	```
51	
52	### P3 · S — Television / fzf channel
53	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
54	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point
55	of the tool; the TUI covers it, but a picker composes better with other tools.
56	
57	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
58	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
59	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
60	March" better than the aggregate does.
61	
62	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
63	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
64	stable binary path; nothing else new.
65	
66	## Deliberately not doing
67	
68	### Installing dependencies
69	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
70	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
71	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
72	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
73	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
74	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
75	
76	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
77	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
78	
79	### A second git database
80	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. Durable stores hold
81	human intent and identity: task state/owner/next action, asset tags/notes,
82	experiment lifecycle and per-host location. Recovery receipts may record one
83	past verification, but apply must verify again. Live branches, remotes,
84	ahead/behind, dirty state and sizes remain derived/cache-only; a durable tool
85	that disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
86	
87	### Syncing runtime state between machines
88	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
89	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
90	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
91	harder problem than the one this tool has.
92	
93	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
94	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
95	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
96	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.

1	package note

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"

9	
10	// Service keeps durable file operations and the disposable index in sync.
11	type Service struct {
12		Store     *Store
13		IndexPath string
14		// IndexDiagnostic reports an incremental index failure after the durable
15		// file operation already succeeded. Search/reindex return index errors
16		// directly because they have no useful result without it.
17		IndexDiagnostic func(error)
18	}
19	
20	func NewService(store *Store, indexPath string) *Service {
21		return &Service{Store: store, IndexPath: indexPath}
22	}
23	
24	func (s *Service) Add(ctx context.Context, repositoryID, repository, body string, tags []string) (*Note, error) {
25		n, err := s.Store.Create(ctx, repositoryID, repository, body, tags)
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, err
28		}
29		s.updateIndex(func(i *Index) error { return i.Upsert(n) })
30		return n, nil
31	}
32	
33	func (s *Service) List(repositoryID string) ([]*Note, error) {
34		return s.Store.List(repositoryID)
35	}
36	
37	func (s *Service) Get(id string) (*Note, error) { return s.Store.Get(id) }
38	
39	func (s *Service) Update(ctx context.Context, id, expectedRevision, body string, tags []string) (*Note, error) {
40		n, err := s.Store.Update(ctx, id, expectedRevision, body, tags)
41		if err != nil {
42			return nil, err
43		}
44		s.updateIndex(func(i *Index) error { return i.Upsert(n) })
45		return n, nil
46	}
47	
48	func (s *Service) Delete(ctx context.Context, id string) error {
49		if err := s.Store.Delete(ctx, id); err != nil {
50			return err
51		}
52		s.updateIndex(func(i *Index) error { return i.Delete(id) })
53		return nil
54	}
55	
56	func (s *Service) Search(query, repositoryID string, limit int) ([]*Note, error) {
57		notes, err := s.Store.List("")
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61		search := func() ([]Hit, error) {
62			i, err := s.openIndexRecover()
63			if err != nil {
64				return nil, err
65			}
66			defer i.Close()
67			if err := i.Ensure(notes); err != nil {
68				return nil, err
69			}
70			return i.Search(query, repositoryID, limit)
71		}
72		hits, err := search()
73		if err != nil {
74			// A valid SQLite file can still have incompatible tables or become
75			// corrupt after Open. It is disposable: clear, rebuild, retry once.
76			if clearErr := s.ClearIndex(); clearErr != nil {
77				return nil, errors.Join(err, clearErr)
78			}
79			hits, err = search()
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, err
83		}
84		byID := make(map[string]*Note, len(notes))
85		for _, n := range notes {
86			byID[n.ID] = n
87		}
88		out := make([]*Note, 0, len(hits))
89		for _, hit := range hits {
90			if n := byID[hit.ID]; n != nil {
91				out = append(out, clone(n))
92			}
93		}
94		return out, nil
95	}
96	
97	func (s *Service) Reindex() (int, error) {
98		notes, err := s.Store.List("")
99		if err != nil {
100			return 0, err
101		}
102		rebuild := func() error {
103			i, err := s.openIndexRecover()
104			if err != nil {
105				return err
106			}
107			defer i.Close()
108			return i.Rebuild(notes)
109		}
110		if err := rebuild(); err != nil {
111			if clearErr := s.ClearIndex(); clearErr != nil {
112				return 0, errors.Join(err, clearErr)
113			}
114			if err := rebuild(); err != nil {
115				return 0, err
116			}
117		}
118		return len(notes), nil
119	}
120	
121	// ClearIndex removes SQLite and its WAL sidecars. Durable Markdown notes are
122	// deliberately outside this path and remain untouched.
123	func (s *Service) ClearIndex() error {
124		var err error
125		for _, suffix := range []string{"", "-wal", "-shm"} {
126			if removeErr := os.Remove(s.IndexPath + suffix); removeErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(removeErr) {
127				err = errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("remove notes index%s: %w", suffix, removeErr))
128			}
129		}
130		return err
131	}
132	
133	// openIndexRecover treats a malformed SQLite file as the disposable cache it
134	// is: remove it and rebuild on the caller's next Ensure/Rebuild. Durable
135	// Markdown is never under this path.
136	func (s *Service) openIndexRecover() (*Index, error) {
137		i, err := OpenIndex(s.IndexPath)
138		if err == nil {
139			return i, nil
140		}
141		if clearErr := s.ClearIndex(); clearErr != nil {
142			return nil, errors.Join(err, clearErr)
143		}
144		return OpenIndex(s.IndexPath)
145	}
146	
147	func (s *Service) updateIndex(operation func(*Index) error) {
148		i, err := s.openIndexRecover()
149		if err == nil {
150			err = operation(i)
151			err = errors.Join(err, i.Close())
152		}
153		if err != nil && s.IndexDiagnostic != nil {
154			s.IndexDiagnostic(err)
155		}
156	}

1	//go:build windows

3	package note

5	import (
6		"context"
7		"errors"
8		"os"
9		"time"
10	
11		"golang.org/x/sys/windows"
12	)
13	
14	type noteFileLock struct {
15		file       *os.File
16		overlapped windows.Overlapped
17	}
18	
19	func acquireNoteFileLock(ctx context.Context, path string) (*noteFileLock, error) {
20		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
21			return nil, err
22		}
23		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
24		if err != nil {
25			return nil, err
26		}
27		lock := &noteFileLock{file: file}
28		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
29		defer ticker.Stop()
30		for {
31			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
32				_ = file.Close()
33				return nil, err
34			}
35			err = windows.LockFileEx(windows.Handle(file.Fd()),
36				windows.LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK|windows.LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY,
37				0, 1, 0, &lock.overlapped)
38			if err == nil {
39				return lock, nil
40			}
41			if !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION) && !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_IO_PENDING) {
42				_ = file.Close()
43				return nil, err
44			}
45			select {
46			case <-ctx.Done():
47				_ = file.Close()
48				return nil, ctx.Err()
49			case <-ticker.C:
50			}
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func (l *noteFileLock) Close() error {
55		unlockErr := windows.UnlockFileEx(windows.Handle(l.file.Fd()), 0, 1, 0, &l.overlapped)
56		return errors.Join(unlockErr, l.file.Close())
57	}
58

123	func cacheInfo(path string) (size int64, modified time.Time, exists bool) {
124		info, err := os.Stat(path)
125		if err != nil {
126			return 0, time.Time{}, false
127		}
128		exists, modified = true, info.ModTime()
129		if !info.IsDir() {
130			return info.Size(), modified, true
131		}
132		_ = filepath.WalkDir(path, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
133			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
134				return nil
135			}
136			if i, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
137				size += i.Size()
138				if i.ModTime().After(modified) {
139					modified = i.ModTime()
140				}
141			}
142			return nil
143		})
144		return size, modified, true
145	}

147	func humanBytes(n int64) string {
148		const unit = 1024
149		switch {
150		case n < unit:
151			return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", n)
152		case n < unit*unit:
153			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fK", float64(n)/unit)
154		case n < unit*unit*unit:
155			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fM", float64(n)/(unit*unit))
156		default:
157			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fG", float64(n)/(unit*unit*unit))
158		}
159	}

```text
1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
100
```

8	# Sources and freshness
9	
10	This site mixes product documentation, external specifications, fast-moving harness behavior, project policy, and history. Every page identifies which kind of statement it contains and when it was checked.
11	
12	## Authority order
13	
14	1. **dev-cli behavior:** repository code, tests, E2E, and generated command reference.
15	2. **Git semantics:** current `git-scm.com` manuals for the relevant installed Git version.
16	3. **GitHub collaboration:** current GitHub Docs.
17	4. **Claude Code behavior:** current Anthropic documentation, with preview/experimental/version labels.
18	5. **Standards:** named versioned specifications such as Conventional Commits 1.0.0 and SemVer 2.0.0.
19	6. **Historical context:** dated archives and older project essays, never a current operating rule.
20	7. **Project policy:** explicitly labeled recommendations; not presented as an upstream guarantee.
21	
22	A lower item may explain motivation but cannot override a higher authority's implementation claim.
23	
24	## Required page metadata
25	
26	```yaml
27	---
28	description: One sentence used by navigation and llms.txt.
29	authority: one value from the authority table below
30	status: one value from the status table below
31	verified_on: YYYY-MM-DD
32	minimum_version: optional
33	tested_with: optional
34	---
35	```

40	| `project-policy` | this project's recommendation |

42	| `git-and-project-policy`, `anthropic-docs-and-project-policy` | upstream semantics plus a labeled local recommendation |
43	| `project-and-upstream` | compatibility page spanning implementation and upstream status |
44

46	|---|---|

8	# Notes index

10	Notes are evidence-bearing working knowledge that may later graduate into a guide or reference page. They are not a dumping ground for unverified instructions.

12	## Taxonomy
13	
14	| Note type | Captures | Graduation target |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| `harness` | behavior/version research for Claude Code or another coding agent | provider guide or compatibility matrix |
17	| `experiment` | hypothesis, setup, observations, result, cleanup | best practice or discarded finding |
18	| `decision` | context, options, chosen rule, consequences | concepts/project policy |
19	| `incident` | symptom, evidence, recovery, prevention | troubleshooting/compatibility |
20	| `source-review` | what an external page actually supports and its date/status | sources matrix |
21	| `recipe` | a repeatable sequence with safety and verification | user guide or skill |
22	
23	Create future notes under `docs/notes/` with descriptive kebab-case names. Introduce a subdirectory only after several notes share a stable category; avoid deep taxonomies based on one item.
24	
25	## Lifecycle
26	
27	```text
28	draft → verified → maintained
29	   └──────► superseded / historical
30	```
31	
32	- **draft:** incomplete investigation; do not place operational commands on the happy path.

34	- **maintained:** an active reference with an owner/freshness expectation.
35	- **superseded:** retained only when the replacement link or historical reasoning matters.
36	- **historical:** intentionally describes an old release or practice.
37

39	
40	When a note is added, list it here with type, status, verification date, and one-sentence value. Once it graduates into a guide, replace the entry with a link to the canonical page rather than keeping two sources of truth.

50	- Link primary sources and code/tests, not only summaries.

215	func (s *Store) read(path string) (*Note, error) {
216		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
217		if err != nil {
218			return nil, err
219		}
220		meta, body, err := split(data)
221		if err != nil {
222			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", filepath.Base(path), err)
223		}
224		var n Note
225		md, err := toml.Decode(string(meta), &n)
226		if err != nil {
227			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s frontmatter: %w", filepath.Base(path), err)
228		}
229		if unknown := md.Undecoded(); len(unknown) > 0 {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s: unknown field(s): %v", filepath.Base(path), unknown)
231		}
232		n.Body, n.Path = string(body), path
233		n.Normalize()
234		if err := n.Validate(); err != nil {
235			return nil, err
236		}
237		if want := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(path), ".md"); n.ID != want {
238			return nil, fmt.Errorf("note ID %s does not match filename %s: %w", n.ID, want, ErrInvalid)
239		}
240		if want := filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(path)); n.RepositoryID != want {
241			return nil, fmt.Errorf("repository ID %s does not match directory %s: %w", n.RepositoryID, want, ErrRepository)
242		}
243		return &n, nil
244	}
245	
246	func (s *Store) writeAtomic(n *Note) error {
247		dir := filepath.Dir(n.Path)
248		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
249			return err
250		}
251		var front bytes.Buffer
252		if err := toml.NewEncoder(&front).Encode(n); err != nil {
253			return err
254		}
255		content := delimiter + "\n" + front.String() + delimiter + "\n\n" + n.Body
256		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, "."+n.ID+".*.tmp")
257		if err != nil {
258			return err
259		}
260		name := tmp.Name()
261		defer os.Remove(name)
262		if _, err := tmp.WriteString(content); err != nil {
263			_ = tmp.Close()
264			return err
265		}
266		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
267			_ = tmp.Close()
268			return fmt.Errorf("sync note temp file: %w", err)
269		}
270		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
271			return err
272		}
273		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
274			return err
275		}
276		if err := os.Rename(name, n.Path); err != nil {
277			return err
278		}
279		// Sync both the note directory (rename entry) and its parent (new
280		// repository directory) before reporting durable success.
281		return errors.Join(syncNoteDir(dir), syncNoteDir(filepath.Dir(dir)))
282	}
283	
284	func split(data []byte) ([]byte, []byte, error) {
285		if !bytes.HasPrefix(data, []byte(delimiter+"\n")) {
286			return nil, nil, errors.New("missing opening +++ frontmatter delimiter")
287		}
288		rest := data[len(delimiter)+1:]
289		marker := []byte("\n" + delimiter + "\n")
290		i := bytes.Index(rest, marker)
291		if i < 0 {
292			return nil, nil, errors.New("missing closing +++ frontmatter delimiter")
293		}
294		meta := rest[:i]
295		body := rest[i+len(marker):]
296		body = bytes.TrimPrefix(body, []byte("\n"))
297		return meta, body, nil
298	}

321		}
322		sort.Strings(paths)
323		return paths, err

354		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o700); err != nil {
355			return err
356		}
357		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(s.Dir)
358		if err != nil {

362		if err != nil {

366		lock, err := acquireNoteFileLock(ctx, lockPath)
367		if err != nil {

369		}
370		defer func() { err = errors.Join(err, lock.Close()) }()

229	// Search performs term-wise prefix search. Literal quoting prevents punctuation

231	func (i *Index) Search(query, repositoryID string, limit int) ([]Hit, error) {
232		rawQuery := strings.TrimSpace(query)
233		if rawQuery == "" {
234			return nil, nil
235		}
236		if limit <= 0 {
237			limit = 100
238		}
239		// unicode61 does not segment CJK words: a body token "記得改善" cannot
240		// match the substring "改善". Use term-wise literal LIKE for non-ASCII
241		// input while retaining FTS ranking/snippets for Latin-script searches.
242		if containsNonASCII(rawQuery) {

244		}
245		query = ftsQuery(rawQuery)
246		if query == "" {
247			return nil, nil

251	FROM notes_fts WHERE notes_fts MATCH ?`

255			args = append(args, repositoryID)
256		}
257		statement += " ORDER BY rank LIMIT ?"

287	FROM notes_fts WHERE `

292			pattern := "%" + term + "%"

294		}

300	func noteRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string) (*catalog.Entry, repo.Repo, error) {
301		if ref != "" {
302			// A stable catalog ID is accepted anywhere a repo name is.
303			if entry, err := app.Registry.Get(ref); err == nil {
304				if entry.Kind != catalog.KindRepository {
305					return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s is %s, not a repository", ref, entry.Kind)
306				}
307				location, ok := entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname())
308				if !ok || location.CurrentPath == "" {
309					return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog repository %s has no path on this host", ref)
310				}
311				r := repo.Repo{Name: entry.Name, Path: location.CurrentPath,
312					RealPath: location.RealPath, CommonDir: location.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true}
313				return entry, r, nil
314			}
315			resolved, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
316			if err != nil {
317				return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
318			}
319			return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: resolved})
320		}
321		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
322		if err != nil {
323			return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
324		}
325		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
326		if err != nil {
327			return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("%s is not in a repository; pass --repo", config.Contract(cwd))
328		}
329		r := repo.Repo{Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
330			CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, MainRoot: g.MainRoot, HasGit: true}
331		return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: r})
332	}

334	func ensureNoteRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, target tui.NoteTarget) (*catalog.Entry, repo.Repo, error) {
335		r := target.Repo
336		if target.CatalogID != "" {
337			if entry, err := app.Registry.Get(target.CatalogID); err == nil {
338				if entry.Kind != catalog.KindRepository {
339					return nil, r, fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s is %s, not a repository", entry.ID, entry.Kind)
340				}
341				return entry, r, nil
342			}
343		}
344		if r.RealPath == "" || r.CommonDir == "" {
345			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, r.Path); err == nil {
346				// Notes belong to the clone's canonical repository, never to a
347				// disposable linked-worktree path.
348				r.Path, r.RealPath, r.MainRoot = g.MainRoot, g.MainRoot, g.MainRoot
349				if r.Name == "" {
350					r.Name = g.Name
351				}
352				r.CommonDir = g.GitCommonDir
353			}
354		}
355		observation := catalog.Observation{
356			Host: config.Hostname(), Path: r.Path, RealPath: r.RealPath,
357			CommonDir: r.CommonDir, Name: r.Name,
358			RemoteIdentity: gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"),
359		}
360		var entry *catalog.Entry
361		err := app.Catalog.WithLock(ctx, func() error {
362			var ensureErr error
363			entry, ensureErr = app.Registry.EnsureRepository(observation)
364			if ensureErr == nil && entry.Kind != catalog.KindRepository {
365				ensureErr = fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s is %s, not a repository", entry.ID, entry.Kind)
366			}
367			return ensureErr
368		})
369		return entry, r, err
370	}

372	func resolveNote(app *App, ref string) (*note.Note, error) {
373		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
374		if len(ref) < 8 {
375			return nil, fmt.Errorf("note ID/prefix must be at least 8 characters")
376		}
377		if n, err := app.Notes.Get(ref); err == nil {
378			return n, nil
379		}
380		notes, err := app.Notes.List("")
381		if err != nil {
382			return nil, err
383		}
384		var hits []*note.Note
385		for _, n := range notes {
386			if strings.HasPrefix(n.ID, ref) {
387				hits = append(hits, n)
388			}
389		}
390		switch len(hits) {
391		case 1:
392			return hits[0], nil
393		case 0:
394			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", ref, note.ErrNotFound)
395		default:
396			return nil, fmt.Errorf("note prefix %q is ambiguous (%d matches)", ref, len(hits))
397		}
398	}

414		}

416		return nil
417	}

420		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-edit-*.md")
421		if err != nil {
422			return nil, err
423		}
424		path := tmp.Name()
425		if _, err := io.WriteString(tmp, n.Body); err != nil {
426			_ = tmp.Close()
427			_ = os.Remove(path)

429		}
430		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
431			_ = os.Remove(path)
432			return nil, err

434		proc, chosen, err := editorProcess(path, editorOverride)
435		if err != nil {
436			_ = os.Remove(path)
437			return nil, err
438		}
439		proc.Stdin, proc.Stdout, proc.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
440		if err := proc.Run(); err != nil {
441			_ = os.Remove(path)
442			return nil, fmt.Errorf("editor %q: %w", chosen, err)
443		}
444		body, err := os.ReadFile(path)

447		}

451		}

453		if err != nil {
454			return nil, fmt.Errorf("save edited note: %w; edited body preserved at %s", err, path)
455		}
456		_ = os.Remove(path)
457		return updated, nil
458	}

460	func editNoteBody(initial, editorOverride string) (string, error) {
461		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-*.md")
462		if err != nil {
463			return "", err
464		}
465		path := tmp.Name()
466		defer os.Remove(path)

468			_ = tmp.Close()
469			return "", err
470		}
471		if !strings.HasSuffix(initial, "\n") {
472			_, _ = io.WriteString(tmp, "\n")
473		}
474		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
475			return "", err
476		}
477		proc, chosen, err := editorProcess(path, editorOverride)
478		if err != nil {
479			return "", err
480		}
481		proc.Stdin, proc.Stdout, proc.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
482		if err := proc.Run(); err != nil {
483			return "", fmt.Errorf("editor %q: %w", chosen, err)
484		}
485		body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
486		if err != nil {
487			return "", err
488		}
489		if strings.TrimSpace(string(body)) == "" {
490			return "", fmt.Errorf("edited note body is empty; not saved")
491		}

```text
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Azure DevOps Services repository inventory, search, cloning, and opt-in forge configuration.
- An interactive, context-aware `dev start` wizard for managed task creation.
- Runtime session activation so opened or reused task surfaces can be focused or attached.
- Exact-pane, fail-closed safeguards for launching parallel agents in newly created Herdr worktrees.
- Agent-ready repository context output, TUI copy actions, and an expanded worktree tree with per-checkout state.
- A bilingual English/Traditional Chinese MkDocs knowledge site with strict source/site checks and GitHub Pages deployment.

### Fixed

- Focused starts now activate their runtime session after the interactive wizard completes.
- Corrected command/config documentation to remove the unsupported `dev wt plan --json` example, include Azure forge configuration, and describe shell navigation without implying ordinary command output is evaluated.
- Corrected bundled skill reference coverage and agent-rule numbering.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-08-28

### Added

- The HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE task lifecycle with direct, branch-only, and managed-worktree checkout modes.
- A TASKS/REPOS/TRY/REMOTE terminal dashboard backed by the same services as the non-interactive CLI.
- Try catalog identity, personal metadata, archive/restore, graduation, and guarded filesystem transitions.
- Rich Git inventory for upstream divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged, and untracked paths.
- Managed worktree placement and provisioning with explicit ignored-file handling and per-ecosystem dependency strategies.
- Repository discovery, remote-risk inspection, logical size accounting, and durable activity statistics.
- Recursive machine bootstrap with non-destructive symlink indexing and guarded physical move plans.
- Adoption of existing worktrees, runtime sessions, and unmerged branches into the task registry.
- Managed `.gitignore` generation from GitHub templates plus project-local sections.
- XDG-based configurable repository, worktree, task, catalog, cache, and runtime layouts.
- An embedded and installable `dev-cli` agent skill with a generated command reference checked in CI.
- Homebrew, Go, and source installation paths, shell completion, and directory-changing shell integration.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/compare/v0.1.0...HEAD
[0.1.0]: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/releases/tag/v0.1.0
```

+func prepareTUINoteEdit(app *App, n *note.Note) (tui.NoteEdit, error) {
+	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-*.md")
+	if err != nil {
+		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
+	}
+	path := tmp.Name()
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(tmp, n.Body); err != nil {
+		_ = tmp.Close()
+		_ = os.Remove(path)
+		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
+	}
+	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
+		_ = os.Remove(path)
+		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
+	}
+	proc, _, err := editorProcess(path, "")
+	if err != nil {
+		_ = os.Remove(path)
+		return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
+	}
+	return tui.NoteEdit{
+		Command: proc,
+		Complete: func(runErr error) error {
+			if runErr != nil {
+				_ = os.Remove(path)
+				return runErr
+			}
+			body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("read edited body (preserved at %s): %w", path, err)
+			}
+			if strings.TrimSpace(string(body)) == "" {
+				_ = os.Remove(path)
+				return fmt.Errorf("edited note body is empty; not saved")
+			}
+			_, err = app.Notes.Update(context.Background(), n.ID, n.Revision(), string(body), n.Tags)
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("save edited note: %w; edited body preserved at %s", err, path)
+			}
+			_ = os.Remove(path)
+			return nil
+		},
+	}, nil
+}

+func (m Model) selectedNoteTarget() (NoteTarget, bool) {

+func (m Model) openNoteAdd(target NoteTarget, returnToBrowse bool) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

+func (m Model) openNotes(target NoteTarget) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

+
+func (m Model) beginNoteLoad(refreshRepos bool) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
+	m.noteRequest++
+	request, targetKey, target := m.noteRequest, m.noteTarget.Key(), m.noteTarget
+	query := m.noteQuery
+	m.noteLoading = true
+	return m, func() tea.Msg {
+		if m.actions.Notes.List == nil {
+			return noteListMsg{request: request, targetKey: targetKey}
+		}
+		var (
+			notes []*note.Note
+			err   error
+		)
+		if query != "" && m.actions.Notes.Search != nil {
+			notes, err = m.actions.Notes.Search(context.Background(), target, query)
+		} else {
+			notes, err = m.actions.Notes.List(context.Background(), target)
+		}
+		msg := noteListMsg{notes: notes, request: request, targetKey: targetKey, err: err}
+		if refreshRepos && m.actions.ReloadRepos != nil {
+			msg.repos, err = m.actions.ReloadRepos(context.Background())
+			if msg.err == nil {
+				msg.err = err
+			}
+		}
+		return msg

+func (m Model) currentNote() (*note.Note, bool) {

+	return m.notes[m.noteCursor], true

+
+func (m *Model) clampNoteCursor() {
+	switch {

+	case m.noteCursor >= len(m.notes):

+	case m.noteCursor < 0:
+		m.noteCursor = 0
+	}
+}
+
+func (m Model) updateNotes(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

+		case "k", "up":
+			m.noteCursor--
+			m.noteExpanded = false
+			m.clampNoteCursor()
+		case "g", "home":
+			m.noteCursor, m.noteExpanded = 0, false
+		case "G", "end":
+			m.noteCursor, m.noteExpanded = len(m.notes)-1, false
+			m.clampNoteCursor()
+		case "enter":
+			if _, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
+				m.noteExpanded = !m.noteExpanded
+			}
+		case "a", "n":
+			return m.openNoteAdd(m.noteTarget, true)
+		case "/":
+			m.mode = modeNoteSearch
+			m.input.SetValue(m.noteQuery)
+			m.input.Placeholder = "search body, tags, repo"
+			m.input.CursorEnd()

+		case "d":
+			if _, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {

+			if err != nil {

+			return m, tea.ExecProcess(edit.Command, func(runErr error) tea.Msg {
+				if edit.Complete != nil {
+					runErr = edit.Complete(runErr)
+				}
+				return noteActionMsg{status: "updated note " + n.ID[:8], returnBrowse: true, err: runErr}
+			})
+		}
+		return m, nil
+
+	case modeNoteAdd:
+		switch msg.String() {
+		case "esc":
+			m.input.Blur()
+			if m.noteReturnToBrowse {

+				m.mode = modeList

+		}
+		input, cmd := m.input.Update(msg)
+		m.input = input

+	case modeNoteConfirmDelete:
+		switch msg.String() {
+		case "esc", "n":

+			n, ok := m.currentNote()

diff --git a/internal/tui/note_view.go b/internal/tui/note_view.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b412869
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/tui/note_view.go
@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+package tui
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
+)
+
+func (m Model) noteMode() bool {
+	return m.mode == modeNoteBrowse || m.mode == modeNoteAdd ||
+		m.mode == modeNoteSearch || m.mode == modeNoteConfirmDelete
+}
+
+func (m Model) renderNotes() string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	title := m.noteTarget.Name()
+	if title == "" {
+		title = "repository"
+	}
+	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n\n", styleTitle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("dev  NOTES  %s  ·  %d notes", title, len(m.notes))))
+
+	switch m.mode {
+	case modeNoteAdd:
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleTitle.Render("quick thought") + "\n\n")
+		b.WriteString("  " + m.input.View() + "\n\n")
+		if m.err != nil {
+			b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()) + "\n\n")
+		}
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("enter save · esc cancel"))
+		return b.String()
+
+	case modeNoteSearch:
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleTitle.Render("search") + "\n\n")
+		b.WriteString("  " + m.input.View() + "\n\n")
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("enter search · esc clear and return"))
+		return b.String()
+
+	case modeNoteConfirmDelete:
+		if n, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
+			b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("Delete note "+n.ID[:8]+"?") + "\n")
+			b.WriteString("  " + n.Preview(maxInt(20, m.width-6)) + "\n\n")
+		}
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("y delete · n / esc cancel"))
+		return b.String()
+	}
+
+	if m.noteQuery != "" {
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("search: "+m.noteQuery) + "\n\n")
+	}
+	if m.noteLoading {
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("Loading notes…") + "\n")
+		return b.String()
+	}
+	if m.err != nil {
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()) + "\n")
+	}
+	if len(m.notes) == 0 {
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("No notes. Press a or n to add one.") + "\n\n")
+		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("a/n add · / search · N/esc back"))
+		return b.String()
+	}
+
+	idW, whenW, tagsW := 8, 6, clamp(m.width/5, 10, 24)
+	thoughtW := m.width - idW - whenW - tagsW - 12
+	if thoughtW < 20 {
+		thoughtW = 20
+	}
+	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s  %s  %s  %s\n",
+		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("ID", idW)),
+		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("WHEN", whenW)),
+		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("TAGS", tagsW)),
+		styleHeader.Render(fitCell("THOUGHT", thoughtW)))
+
+	maxRows := m.height - 11
+	if m.noteExpanded {
+		maxRows -= 6
+	}
+	if maxRows < 3 {
+		maxRows = 3
+	}
+	from, to := noteWindow(len(m.notes), m.noteCursor, maxRows)
+	for i := from; i < to; i++ {
+		n := m.notes[i]
+		tags := strings.Join(n.Tags, ",")
+		if tags == "" {
+			tags = "—"
+		}
+		line := strings.Join([]string{
+			fitCell(n.ID[:8], idW), fitCell(noteAge(n.Created), whenW),
+			fitCell(tags, tagsW), fitCell(n.Preview(thoughtW), thoughtW),
+		}, "  ")
+		if i == m.noteCursor {
+			b.WriteString(styleSelected.Render("▸ ") + styleSelected.Render(line) + "\n")
+		} else {
+			b.WriteString("  " + line + "\n")
+		}
+	}
+	if len(m.notes) > maxRows {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n", styleDim.Render(fmt.Sprintf("… %d–%d of %d", from+1, to, len(m.notes))))
+	}
+	if m.noteExpanded {
+		if n, ok := m.currentNote(); ok {
+			body := lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(maxInt(20, m.width-4)).Render(strings.TrimSpace(n.Body))
+			body = limitLines(body, maxInt(3, m.height/3))
+			b.WriteString("\n  " + styleDim.Render(n.ID+" · "+n.Updated.Format(time.RFC3339)) + "\n")
+			b.WriteString("  " + strings.ReplaceAll(body, "\n", "\n  ") + "\n")
+		}
+	}
+	b.WriteString("\n  " + styleHelp.Render("j/k move · / search · enter expand · a add · e edit · d delete · N/esc back"))
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+func noteWindow(total, cursor, height int) (from, to int) {
+	if total <= height {
+		return 0, total
+	}
+	from = cursor - height/2
+	if from < 0 {
+		from = 0
+	}
+	if from+height > total {
+		from = total - height
+	}
+	return from, from + height
+}
+
+func noteAge(created time.Time) string {
+	d := time.Since(created)
+	switch {
+	case d < time.Minute:
+		return "now"
+	case d < time.Hour:
+		return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
+	case d < 24*time.Hour:
+		return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
+	case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
+		return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
+	default:
+		return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
+	}
+}
+
+func limitLines(text string, limit int) string {
+	lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
+	if len(lines) <= limit {
+		return text
+	}
+	return strings.Join(lines[:limit], "\n") + "\n…"
+}
+
+func maxInt(a, b int) int {
+	if a > b {
+		return a
+	}
+	return b
+}

 }
+
+// NoteTarget identifies the selected local repository. CatalogID may be empty
+// until the first note action persists the repository observation.
+type NoteTarget struct {
+	CatalogID string
+	Repo      repo.Repo
+}
+
+func (t NoteTarget) Name() string { return t.Repo.Name }
+func (t NoteTarget) Path() string { return t.Repo.Path }
+
+// Key identifies the target while an asynchronous load is in flight.
+func (t NoteTarget) Key() string {
+	for _, value := range []string{t.CatalogID, t.Repo.CommonDir, t.Repo.RealPath, t.Repo.Path} {
+		if value != "" {
+			return value
+		}
+	}
+	return t.Repo.Name
+}
+
+// NoteEdit suspends the TUI in an editor and atomically completes from its
+// temporary body after the process exits.
+type NoteEdit struct {
+	Command *exec.Cmd
+	// Complete always runs, even when the editor fails, so temporary files are
+	// cleaned. It may replace runErr with validation/index errors.
+	Complete func(runErr error) error
+}
+
+// NoteActions are the sidecar-note operations available to the dashboard.
+type NoteActions struct {
+	List   func(ctx context.Context, target NoteTarget) ([]*note.Note, error)
+	Search func(ctx context.Context, target NoteTarget, query string) ([]*note.Note, error)
+	Add    func(ctx context.Context, target NoteTarget, body string) (string, error)
+	Delete func(ctx context.Context, n *note.Note) (string, error)
+	Edit   func(n *note.Note) (NoteEdit, error)
+}
